ops.title: The Gate at Canton
ops.brief: In August 1784 Samuel Shaw, supercargo of the Empress of China, anchored at Whampoa and learned the terms of the only gate the Qing court kept open to the West.
ops.record: The Qing court confined Western trade to Canton from 1757. Every foreign ship needed a licensed hong merchant to stand surety for its conduct and its duties, and foreigners lived in a strip of factories outside the city walls for the trading season. The Empress of China had sailed from New York in February 1784 and traded ginseng for tea and silk under those rules.
ops.reading: The security merchant made one licensed person answer for every guest, a gate built on verification rather than trust. The gate held until opium moved outside it and the gatekeepers took a cut, which is where most later gates have failed.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. The gatekeepers earned from the traffic their office existed to stop.
ops.fix: Verify every request at the gate and audit the gatekeeper's income, the discipline zero trust now names.

ops.title: Terranova
ops.brief: In September 1821 a woman selling fruit from a boat beside the American ship Emily at Whampoa fell into the river and drowned. Qing officials charged a sailor named Francis Terranova with striking her with an earthenware jar.
ops.record: The American merchants tried Terranova aboard ship and refused to hand him over. Qing officials stopped all American trade until they did. The merchants surrendered him, a Qing court convicted him, and officials executed him by strangulation in October 1821.
ops.reading: The Qing court proved that trade access could buy a person, and the merchants proved that a guest with no law of its own will pay. The episode fed the American demand for extraterritoriality that Caleb Cushing won in 1844.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No American authority held the jurisdiction question, so each merchant weighed his cargo against one sailor's life.
ops.fix: Settle jurisdiction and consular access by treaty before the incident, so no trade lever can buy a citizen.

ops.title: The Opium Chests
ops.brief: On June 3, 1839, Commissioner Lin Zexu began destroying more than twenty thousand chests of opium in trenches at Humen. American chests went into the trenches with the British.
ops.record: American houses carried Turkish opium and held a minority share of the trade, and Russell and Company made fortunes for partners such as Warren Delano Jr. Lin confined the foreign community in its factories until it surrendered its stock in the spring of 1839. The Americans kept trading as neutral carriers after the British withdrew, and the war that followed opened five ports under the Treaty of Nanjing in 1842.
ops.reading: A trade that degrades the host's people buys a grievance that outlives every firm in it. The Party's official histories date modern Chinese history from 1840, and its patriotic education still teaches the opium trade as the first chapter of national humiliation.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The American merchants carried no rule against profiting from harm to the host's population.
ops.fix: Write the harm rule into the treaty, as Article 33 of the Wanghia treaty did when it stripped American protection from opium traders in 1844.

ops.title: Wanghia
ops.brief: On July 3, 1844, Caleb Cushing signed a treaty with the Qing commissioner Qiying in a temple at Wangxia village outside Macau.
ops.record: The treaty gave American consuls jurisdiction over American citizens in the open ports, and it granted the United States any privilege another power won later. It also declared opium contraband and left American opium traders to Qing law. The United States gave up extraterritorial rights in China by a treaty with the Republic of China in January 1943.
ops.reading: The United States let Britain fight and then took the terms, which is Stratagem 9 read from the winning bank. Extraterritoriality placed the guest's law inside the host's courts, and the Party still cites the unequal treaties when it rejects foreign law as interference.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. The host's legal platform admitted a second system it could not administer.
ops.fix: Refuse any arrangement that places a foreign system beyond local review, the same rule the Hong Kong case sets for the next guarantee.

ops.title: The Coolie Trade Act
ops.brief: On February 19, 1862, Abraham Lincoln signed a law that barred American ships from carrying Chinese contract laborers to foreign ports.
ops.record: American shipowners had carried Chinese laborers under contract to Cuba and Peru, where many worked off debts on plantations and in guano pits. American diplomats in China reported kidnapping, deaths and mutinies in the traffic. The act made carrying such laborers in American vessels a crime, and it required a consul to certify that each emigrant left freely.
ops.reading: Congress cut the lever at the carrier, the one node American law reached, and left the plantations it could not reach alone. The same design works today when a customs rule stops goods made by coerced hands at the border.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. American shipowners earned freight from a traffic that American law had not yet named.
ops.fix: Name the trafficking channel in statute and bind the carrier, the model the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act follows with its import presumption.

ops.title: The Summit Strike
ops.brief: In late June 1867 several thousand Chinese workers laid down their tools along the Sierra grade of the Central Pacific and asked for higher pay and shorter shifts in the tunnels.
ops.record: Chinese crews made up most of the Central Pacific's workforce on the Sierra grade and earned less than white crews for the same work. Charles Crocker cut off food and supplies to the camps, and the strike ended within about a week. The company's records of the week are thin, and the workers left no written account of their own.
ops.reading: The strike was an act of agency by people the record barely names. The railroad won by cutting supply rather than by argument, which is Stratagem 19 run by an American company against its own workforce.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The host had no rule of equal pay, so the lowest bidder for danger became the default.
ops.fix: Write equal pay for equal work into the contract and enforce it, whatever the worker's origin.

ops.title: Burlingame
ops.brief: In November 1867 the Qing court appointed Anson Burlingame, who had recently finished six years as the American minister in Peking, to lead its first diplomatic mission to the West.
ops.record: Burlingame negotiated a treaty with Secretary of State William Seward that the two sides signed on July 28, 1868. It recognized the right of free migration and promised reciprocal access to schools, and it withheld naturalization. Congress reversed the migration promise within fourteen years, and Burlingame died on the mission in St. Petersburg in 1870.
ops.reading: The Qing court borrowed an American's credibility to speak for it in Washington, and the words landed because they were American words. The promise then failed on the American side, and every later government in China learned what an American guarantee on migration was worth.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. A treaty principle bound the executive while Congress kept the power to repeal it by statute.
ops.fix: Make treaty promises and domestic statute answer to the same architecture contract, so one branch cannot silently void the other's word.

ops.title: The Recall
ops.brief: In 1881 Zhan Tianyou finished his degree at Yale's Sheffield Scientific School in the same year the Qing court recalled every student of its Educational Mission.
ops.record: Yung Wing, Yale's first Chinese graduate, had persuaded the court to send 120 boys to New England between 1872 and 1875. The mission's conservative commissioner warned that the boys were becoming American, and the United States refused to admit any of them to West Point or Annapolis in 1878. The court ordered the mission home in 1881, and Zhan later built the Beijing to Zhangjiakou railway without foreign engineers.
ops.reading: A host that fears what its students learn abroad recalls them, and a guest country that bars them from its best schools hands the host the reason. The Party's scholarship contracts still require state-funded students to come home and serve.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The United States promised Chinese students access to its schools in 1868 and closed its military academies to them a decade later.
ops.fix: Hold the education promise open and state the security limits in advance, so a closed door is a published rule rather than a surprise.

ops.title: Exclusion and the Geary Certificate
ops.fullTitle: Exclusion and the Geary Certificate (1882 to 1892)
ops.label: 1882 to 1892
ops.brief: In May 1892 the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association in San Francisco told Chinese residents across the country not to register under a new federal law that required them to carry a certificate of residence.
ops.record: The Chinese Exclusion Act of May 6, 1882, suspended the entry of Chinese laborers and barred Chinese immigrants from naturalization. The Geary Act of 1892 extended the ban and required every Chinese laborer to carry a certificate of residence on pain of arrest and deportation. The Supreme Court upheld the certificate in Fong Yue Ting v. United States in 1893, and Congress repealed exclusion only in December 1943.
ops.reading: Exclusion turned ancestry into a legal category and built a federal registry to enforce it. That registry was the Data and Surveillance domain, and the United States ran it on its own residents. The guardrail in Military-Civil Fusion answers it directly. Ancestry is not loyalty.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender wrote ancestry into law, so the registry answered a question no conduct had raised.
ops.fix: Screen conduct and institutions, never ancestry, the rule the book's guardrails already hold.

ops.title: Yick Wo v. Hopkins
ops.brief: In 1885 Lee Yick, who had run a laundry in San Francisco for twenty-two years, went to jail for washing clothes without a permit the city had refused him.
ops.record: San Francisco required a permit to run a laundry in a wooden building, and the supervisors refused all of some two hundred Chinese applicants. They granted all but one of about eighty applications from non-Chinese owners. The Supreme Court ruled on May 10, 1886, that the Fourteenth Amendment protects every person within the jurisdiction and that a law applied with an evil eye and an unequal hand violates it.
ops.reading: A neutral text can carry a targeted routine, and only the record of how the routine ran exposes it. The Court read the application layer rather than the statute, the audit the defenders still need against any rule written fair and run unfair.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The permit routine discriminated while the ordinance's text stayed neutral.
ops.fix: Audit outcomes by applicant class, not text alone, and publish the counts as the Yick Wo record did.

ops.title: Wong Kim Ark
ops.brief: In August 1895 customs officers at San Francisco stopped Wong Kim Ark, a cook born in the city in 1873, on his return from a visit to China and refused to let him land.
ops.record: The government argued that a child of Chinese subjects born on American soil was not a citizen. The Supreme Court held by six votes to two that the Fourteenth Amendment made Wong a citizen by birth. The Court ruled on March 28, 1898.
ops.reading: The republic's own court refused to make ancestry a legal category, and the refusal protected every later child of immigrants. The Party claims the loyalty of overseas Chinese by descent, and the Wong holding is the American answer in law.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The executive tried to write descent into citizenship, and the Court held the line.
ops.fix: Keep citizenship a matter of law and conduct, never descent, the principle the Long Arm chapter depends on.

ops.title: The Boycott of 1905
ops.brief: On July 16, 1905, a man named Feng Xiawei killed himself outside the American consulate in Shanghai to protest the treatment of Chinese in the United States.
ops.record: Shanghai merchants called a boycott of American goods in May 1905 unless Washington eased the exclusion laws, and the boycott began that July. Students, guilds and overseas Chinese communities spread it from Shanghai to Canton and beyond. The Qing court banned the boycott at the end of August under American pressure, and it faded in the south during 1906.
ops.reading: The boycott grew from the street, on a grievance the United States had written into its own statute book. The Party's boycotts of American firms start at the top and stop on command, which is the difference between Resonance and a switch.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender's own exclusion law supplied the grievance the boycott used.
ops.fix: Close the self-inflicted grievance first, since no information operation needs a lie when the statute book supplies the truth.

ops.title: The Indemnity Scholarships
ops.brief: In 1906 the University of Illinois president Edmund James wrote to Theodore Roosevelt that the nation educating China's young would reap the largest return in moral, intellectual and commercial influence.
ops.record: Congress authorized the return of about $11 million of the American Boxer indemnity in May 1908, and the Qing court agreed to spend it on students bound for the United States. The first scholars sailed in 1909, and the preparatory school that opened in Beijing in 1911 became Tsinghua. Hu Shih, Chao Yuen Ren and Qian Xuesen all studied in America on the indemnity.
ops.reading: The United States ran the Attract stage on purpose and on a thirty-year horizon, and the program returned scientists and diplomats. The same program produced Qian Xuesen, whom the United States later expelled, a reminder that a pipeline pays only while the host keeps faith with the people it draws.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. A long-horizon program depends on keeping faith with those it draws, and the United States broke faith with Qian in 1950.
ops.fix: Fund talent programs on a horizon longer than an election, and pair them with rules that keep faith with the people they draw.

ops.title: The Diaspora Funds a Republic
ops.brief: Sun Yat-sen was in Denver raising money when the Wuchang uprising began in October 1911, and he read of it in a newspaper.
ops.record: Sun joined the Chee Kung Tong, a secret society with lodges in American Chinatowns, in Honolulu in 1904 and used its network to raise funds. Laundrymen, cooks and merchants in American cities paid for much of the revolutionary league's work. The Party merged its Overseas Chinese Affairs Office into the United Front Work Department in 2018.
ops.reading: The republic grew from a diaspora mesh that no government commanded. The Party runs that same association layer through its United Front today, and the 2018 merger put the whole layer under one department.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. No defender owns the association layer, so a diaspora's own institutions sit open to capture.
ops.fix: Support independent community institutions and protect them from coercion, without treating their members as suspects.

ops.title: Shandong
ops.brief: On May 4, 1919, about three thousand students marched from their campuses to Tiananmen to protest the award of Shandong to Japan at Paris.
ops.record: Woodrow Wilson agreed at the end of April 1919 to let Japan keep the German rights in Shandong. The Republic of China's delegates refused to sign the Treaty of Versailles that June. Soviet Russia's Karakhan Manifesto of July 1919 offered to give up Tsarist privileges in China, and the offer reached Chinese readers in March 1920.
ops.reading: Wilson's principles raised a hope, his bargain broke it, and the Leninist offer arrived in the gap it left. The Party dates its own origins to the May Fourth Movement, a birth in the disappointment the defenders caused.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defenders proclaimed self-determination and then traded a Chinese province to hold a coalition together.
ops.fix: Apply stated principles evenly or say plainly where they stop, because an adversary recruits in the gap between the two.

ops.title: The Comintern's Section
ops.brief: In late July 1921 thirteen delegates met in a house in the French Concession of Shanghai to found the Chinese Communist Party, with two Comintern agents in the room.
ops.record: Hendricus Sneevliet, known as Maring, represented the Communist International at the first congress. The Party joined the Comintern as its Chinese section in 1922 and took its directives. Chen Duxiu reported to Moscow in June 1922 that the Comintern had supplied almost all of the Party's spending since the previous October.
ops.reading: The Party began as a foreign-funded section of a foreign organization, a fact its own histories record. The Party now treats foreign funding of Chinese civil society as a security threat, as its 2017 law on foreign NGOs shows.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The Republic's government kept no registry of foreign money in its politics.
ops.fix: Register foreign funding of political organizations and enforce the registry, the job FARA and Section 117 exist to do.

ops.title: The Bloc Within
ops.label: 1924 to 1927
ops.brief: In January 1924 Communist delegates took seats at the Nationalist Party's first national congress in Canton as members of both parties at once.
ops.record: The Comintern directed Party members to join the Nationalists as individuals while keeping their own organization, and the Soviet adviser Mikhail Borodin helped rebuild the Nationalist Party on Leninist lines. Communists rose to posts in its propaganda, peasant and labor departments. Chiang Kai-shek struck in Shanghai on April 12, 1927, and the purge that followed killed thousands of Communists and labor activists.
ops.reading: The bloc within is Stratagem 30 in its founding form. The guest joined the host, took its departments and prepared to set its agenda, and the host answered with a massacre rather than a design.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The Nationalist Party admitted members who answered to another organization and had no rule for dual loyalty until it chose violence.
ops.fix: Require disclosure of outside organizational duties at the door and act on the disclosure through process, never purge.

ops.title: Futian
ops.brief: In December 1930 soldiers of the Twentieth Army at Futian in Jiangxi rose against the Party's purge commission after it tortured their officers into naming members of a counterrevolutionary league.
ops.record: The purge targeted an alleged Anti-Bolshevik League inside the Jiangxi Soviet and drew confessions by torture. The Party executed thousands of its own members and soldiers in the Jiangxi base in the months after. Later official Party histories describe the campaign as an error of excess.
ops.reading: The Party learned early that a named enemy inside the ranks produces obedience, and it ran the pattern again at Yan'an and after 1949. The first victims of the method were Party members and the peasants who followed them.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No authority outside the purge commission could test a confession.
ops.fix: Keep review of any charge outside the body that makes it, the separation a free society builds into its courts.

ops.title: Red Star Over China
ops.brief: In July 1936 Edgar Snow sat with Mao Zedong in a cave at Bao'an and wrote down the life story that Mao chose to tell him.
ops.record: The Party arranged Snow's passage into its base in the summer of 1936, and he stayed about four months. Red Star Over China appeared in London in 1937 and in New York in January 1938, and a Chinese translation drew young volunteers to Yan'an. The book set the Western picture of the Party for a decade.
ops.reading: One curated visit wrote the adversary's first Western profile, and the host chose every interview. The Party still grants access to the visitors it expects to carry its picture home.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The defenders held one source on the Party's base and no means to test it.
ops.fix: Treat any access an adversary grants as a curated feed, and test it against sources the adversary does not control.

ops.title: The Nanjing Safety Zone
ops.brief: In December 1937 Minnie Vautrin stood at the gate of Ginling College in Nanjing and turned back Japanese soldiers who came for the women sheltering inside.
ops.record: Imperial Japanese forces took Nanjing on December 13, 1937, and killed civilians and prisoners on a mass scale in the weeks after. A committee of about two dozen Westerners ran a safety zone, and Vautrin's campus sheltered about ten thousand women and children at its peak. The missionary John Magee filmed victims in the city's hospital, and George Fitch smuggled the film to Shanghai sewn into his coat.
ops.reading: The zone saved lives, and its records outlasted every denial that followed. The Party builds its patriotic education on Nanjing's dead and erases the records of deaths it caused, the Cultural domain run selectively.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No government owned the protection of the city's civilians, so a handful of private foreigners held it with flags and paperwork.
ops.fix: Keep evidence that outlives the event, because a documented record is the one defense a victim keeps after the guns stop.

ops.title: The Special Commodity
ops.label: 1941 to 1945
ops.brief: In March 1941 Wang Zhen marched the 359th Brigade into the valley of Nanniwan to reclaim wasteland, the start of a production drive the Party still celebrates in song.
ops.record: The Party's border region grew poppy under the euphemism of a special product, bought the harvest through its own agencies and sold the opium into Nationalist-held territory. It banned opium use inside its own areas. Senior leaders argued over the policy in writing, as Xie Juezai's diary published in China records.
ops.reading: Chen Yung-fa's archival study puts the trade near forty percent of the border region's revenue in the war years, a finding from research through the records rather than an admission. The Party banned the drug at home and sold it outside, the same asymmetry its platforms run today between Douyin and TikTok.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The trade's revenue share rests on archival research because the Party has never published its accounts.
ops.fix: Demand audited accounts from any party or state that asks for trust, and treat their absence as a finding.

ops.title: Wang Shiwei and Rectification
ops.brief: In March 1942 Wang Shiwei published an essay called Wild Lilies in the Party's Liberation Daily that mocked the privileges of senior cadres at Yan'an.
ops.record: Mao launched the Rectification Movement that spring, and Party meetings denounced Wang as a Trotskyite through May and June 1942. The Party expelled Wang and held him under guard, and its security forces executed him in 1947. The Ministry of Public Security concluded in 1991 that the Trotskyite charge had no basis.
ops.reading: Rectification made one writer the example for every writer, which is Stratagem 26. The Party learned at Yan'an to manufacture coherence by study, confession and purge, and Robert Lifton later drew his criteria of totalism from people who went through the same method.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No body inside the Party could protect a member who told the truth about its privileges.
ops.fix: Protect the internal critic by rule, because an organization that punishes accurate reports soon receives none.

ops.title: The Magnuson Act
ops.brief: On December 17, 1943, Franklin Roosevelt signed the law that ended sixty-one years of Chinese exclusion.
ops.record: Japanese propaganda cited the exclusion laws to tell Chinese audiences that their American ally despised them. Roosevelt asked Congress to repeal the laws as a war measure, and the Magnuson Act allowed Chinese immigrants to naturalize. It set a quota of 105 entries a year.
ops.reading: Repeal answered an enemy's information operation by removing its true material. The move echoes Emancipation, a coherence move that closed a door the adversary had pried open, and it cost little because the quota stayed token.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The ally's own statute supplied the enemy's best propaganda for a decade.
ops.fix: Audit the statute book for grievances an adversary can quote, and fix them before the adversary uses them.

ops.title: Chien-Shiung Wu
ops.brief: In March 1944 Chien-Shiung Wu, a physicist from Jiangsu who had earned her doctorate at Berkeley, joined the Manhattan Project's Substitute Alloy Materials Laboratory at Columbia.
ops.record: Wu worked on radiation detection and the enrichment of uranium. When the Hanford production reactor stalled in 1944, Enrico Fermi's team consulted her unpublished work on xenon, the fission product that was poisoning the reactor. She became a citizen in 1954, and her experiment of 1957 overturned the conservation of parity.
ops.reading: The arsenal of 1941 to 1945 ran on talent the country's own laws had tried to keep out. Wu's work is the 442nd lesson in a laboratory.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender recruited a scientist whom its naturalization law had barred until the year before she joined.
ops.fix: Recruit by skill and screen by conduct, the rule the Military-Civil Fusion chapter sets for research security.

ops.title: The Dixie Mission
ops.brief: On July 22, 1944, Colonel David Barrett stepped off a C-47 at Yan'an at the head of the United States Army Observation Group.
ops.record: The Party hosted the observers with open access to its leaders and its base, and Mao told John Service that the Party wanted American cooperation after the war. Service's reports praised the Party's discipline and contrasted it with Nationalist corruption. Ambassador Patrick Hurley opposed working with the Party, and the mission's advocates later lost their careers in the purge of the China hands.
ops.reading: Yan'an ran the Attract stage on American officers, and the warmth was real enough to persuade honest men. The Party welcomed the observers it could host and leaned to the Soviet Union once it held power, which is Stratagem 10 on a five-year clock.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The observers saw what their host showed them, and no other channel tested it.
ops.fix: Pair every hosted visit with independent collection and read the host's access as an operation.

ops.title: Yalta's Far East Clause
ops.brief: On February 11, 1945, Franklin Roosevelt signed a secret agreement at Yalta that promised Joseph Stalin rights in Manchuria without telling Chiang Kai-shek.
ops.record: The agreement promised the Soviet Union a lease on Port Arthur, preeminent interests in Dairen and joint operation of the Manchurian railways. Roosevelt undertook to obtain Chiang's concurrence later. Soviet forces entered Manchuria on August 9, 1945, and the Party's troops moved in behind them as the Kwantung Army collapsed.
ops.reading: Washington traded an ally's province for a partner's entry into the war, which is Stratagem 11 run against a friend. The Party then stood where the windfall fell, and the extent of Soviet arms transfers to it remains a real dispute among historians.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The alliance had no rule that bound its leaders to consult the ally whose territory they traded.
ops.fix: Write consultation into the alliance's architecture contract, so no partner's sovereignty moves without the partner at the table.

ops.title: Amerasia
ops.brief: FBI agents arrested the Amerasia editor Philip Jaffe and five others in June 1945.
ops.record: Agents had found hundreds of classified government documents in the magazine's New York office. Earlier warrantless entries by OSS officers and FBI agents weakened the case, and a grand jury declined to indict the diplomat John Service. Jaffe paid a fine of $2,500, and no one went to prison.
ops.reading: The first China leak case failed on the defender's own procedure, and the failure fed a decade of suspicion that ruined careers more than it protected secrets. Bad process on a real breach produces both a free culprit and a purge.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The defenders could not show how documents left their channels, and their own illegal entries spoiled the evidence.
ops.fix: Log access to classified material by person and time, so a leak case rests on records rather than break-ins.

ops.title: The Marshall Mission
ops.brief: On January 10, 1946, George Marshall watched Nationalist and Communist negotiators announce a ceasefire in Chongqing.
ops.record: Marshall set up truce teams of American, Nationalist and Communist officers to police the ceasefire. Fighting resumed in Manchuria that spring as both sides raced for the ground the Soviets left. Marshall left China in January 1947 and blamed extremists on both sides for the failure.
ops.reading: A truce with no enforcement served the side with the longer horizon, and the Party used the pause to build its forces in the northeast. Both sides broke the truce, and the record supports no claim that either one alone destroyed it.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The mediator had verification teams and no power to act on what they found.
ops.fix: Tie any ceasefire to verification with consequences agreed before signature, or treat it as a pause the patient side will use.

ops.title: The Gold Yuan
ops.brief: In August 1948 Chiang Ching-kuo arrived in Shanghai to enforce the gold yuan, a new currency that citizens had to buy with their gold and foreign cash.
ops.record: The Nationalist government issued the gold yuan on August 19, 1948. It froze prices and ordered citizens to exchange their gold, silver and foreign currency. Chiang Ching-kuo arrested speculators, the price freeze broke within weeks, and the currency collapsed before the year was out.
ops.reading: The regime spent its middle class to buy three months of stable prices, and the Party took the cities that followed partly on the regime's own collapse. A government that confiscates its citizens' savings in a crisis teaches them to wait for the other side.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. The Financial capability had no discipline the government could not override.
ops.fix: Keep money under rules a crisis government cannot suspend, because savers who lose everything stop defending the system.

ops.title: The Ward Affair
ops.label: 1948 to 1949
ops.brief: On November 20, 1948, Communist authorities in Mukden sealed the American consulate general and confined Consul General Angus Ward and his staff inside.
ops.record: The Party held Ward and his staff under house arrest for about a year. In October 1949 it arrested Ward on a charge of assaulting a Chinese employee, convicted him and expelled him that December. Washington protested and could do nothing else.
ops.reading: The Party's first act toward American officials was detention, and it set the template for Downey, Fecteau and the Two Michaels. A hostage costs the taker little and freezes the other side's options.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The United States had no response package for detained diplomats, so each case waited for a fresh decision.
ops.fix: Decide the response to a detained diplomat or citizen before it happens, and publish the price the jailer will pay.

ops.title: The China Hands
ops.label: 1950 to 1954
ops.brief: The State Department fired John Service in December 1951 after the Loyalty Review Board found reasonable doubt about his loyalty.
ops.record: Joseph McCarthy's speech at Wheeling in February 1950 opened a campaign against the diplomats who had reported on the Party. The department dismissed John Paton Davies in 1954, and John Carter Vincent and O. Edmund Clubb also left under charges of disloyalty that no one proved. The Supreme Court restored Service's case in 1957, after the department had lost its China specialists.
ops.reading: The defender purged the officers who had seen the Party up close, and it lost the knowledge layer it needed for the next twenty years. The Party did nothing to cause the loss and gained from it anyway.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The defender treated accurate reporting on the adversary as evidence of sympathy with it.
ops.fix: Protect analysts whose assessments prove unwelcome, and judge them on accuracy and conduct alone.

ops.title: Land to the Tiller
ops.brief: In 1948 William Hinton, an American tractor technician, watched a Party work team run land reform in the Shanxi village of Long Bow and later wrote it up as Fanshen.
ops.record: The Agrarian Reform Law of June 30, 1950, carried the base-area practice across the mainland. Work teams classified every household by class and staged mass accusation meetings against landlords, many of which ended in beatings and executions. Scholarly estimates of the dead run from several hundred thousand to two million or more.
ops.reading: Land to the tiller was a frequency the Nationalists could not transmit, and the class labels it assigned became a permanent sorting of the population. The same sorting later ran in Xinjiang with algorithms in place of work teams.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No court stood between a class label and a death sentence.
ops.fix: Keep every sanction tied to individual conduct proven in a forum the accuser does not control.

ops.title: The Volunteers and the Panikkar Warning
ops.fullTitle: The Volunteers and the Panikkar Warning (1950)
ops.brief: Shortly after midnight on October 3, 1950, Zhou Enlai warned the Indian ambassador K. M. Panikkar that the People's Republic would enter the war if American troops crossed the 38th parallel.
ops.record: Washington discounted the message, and American troops crossed the parallel in early October. The Party's forces crossed the Yalu under the name Chinese People's Volunteers from October 19 and struck United Nations troops at Unsan and later at the Chosin Reservoir. The name let the Party fight a war it never declared.
ops.reading: The warning reached Washington through a channel it distrusted and triggered no response, the same gap the Hong Kong case records in 2017. The volunteer label shows the Legal domain at work before the first shot.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. A warning arrived with no owner and no trigger, so it fed a report rather than a decision.
ops.fix: Map each warning to a response agreed in advance, whatever channel carries it, and log who judged it.

ops.title: Five-Anti and the Red Capitalist
ops.fullTitle: Five-Anti and the Red Capitalist (1952 to 1956)
ops.label: 1952 to 1956
ops.brief: In January 1956 Rong Yiren, heir to one of Shanghai's largest textile and flour businesses, handed his family's factories to joint state ownership in a ceremony the Party celebrated.
ops.record: The Party launched the Five-Anti campaign in January 1952 against five offenses it charged to private business, from bribery and tax evasion to theft of economic information. Work teams and employees denounced owners in mass meetings, and many business owners killed themselves under the pressure. By 1956 the Party had brought private industry under joint state ownership, and Rong later founded CITIC in 1979 to court foreign capital.
ops.reading: Five-Anti consumed the private sector that had stayed to work with the new state, and the Party later called on its survivor to attract the foreign capital it needed. The actions of 2020 and 2021 against private platforms run the same instrument with regulators in place of work teams.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No law protected property from a campaign, so compliance bought nothing.
ops.fix: Price the risk that a party-state will consume any private partner it no longer needs, and write that risk into every investment review.

ops.title: The Germ Weapons Charge
ops.brief: In the summer of 1952 the British biochemist Joseph Needham toured sites in the northeast with an international commission and signed a report accusing the United States of germ warfare.
ops.record: North Korea's foreign minister and then Zhou Enlai accused the United States in early 1952 of dropping infected insects and other agents. Captured American airmen signed confessions under duress, and the International Scientific Commission endorsed the charge that September. Soviet documents published in 1998 showed that officials had fabricated the evidence.
ops.reading: The campaign borrowed a scientist's standing to certify a fiction, which is Stratagem 14. A lie certified by a respected foreign name survives long after the archives expose it, and the Party has never withdrawn the charge.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The defender had no fast, independent investigation the accusers would admit.
ops.fix: Keep standing agreements for independent inspection of alleged biological attacks and invite inspectors at once when accused.

ops.title: Downey and Fecteau
ops.label: 1952 to 1973
ops.brief: On the night of November 29, 1952, John Downey and Richard Fecteau were aboard a CIA plane that Party forces shot down over Manchuria.
ops.record: The Party announced their sentences in November 1954, life for Downey and twenty years for Fecteau. Washington insisted they were Army civilians and denied the CIA link for two decades. Fecteau walked out in December 1971, and Downey went free in March 1973 after Richard Nixon publicly acknowledged his CIA employment.
ops.reading: The Party held two men for leverage and waited out five American presidents. The American denial protected a secret the Party already knew and cost the prisoners years.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender's cover story outlived its purpose and became part of the prisoners' sentence.
ops.fix: Review cover and denial policy on a clock once an adversary holds the person, because a secret the captor knows protects no one.

ops.title: The 14,000
ops.label: 1953 to 1954
ops.brief: On May 7, 1952, Harry Truman said the United States would not buy an armistice by turning over human beings for slaughter or slavery.
ops.record: About two thirds of the roughly 21,000 Chinese prisoners in United Nations Command camps refused repatriation. Many were former Nationalist soldiers the Party had absorbed. The dispute over voluntary repatriation kept the war going for more than a year, and about 14,000 of the prisoners reached Taiwan in January 1954.
ops.reading: The Party's own soldiers voted with their feet, and the United States paid in months of war to honor the vote. Shield the people was policy before it was a guardrail.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The principle held, and soldiers who fought on during the deadlock paid for it.
ops.fix: Decide the rule on repatriation before the war ends, so negotiators defend it rather than invent it.

ops.title: The Code of Conduct
ops.brief: In January 1954 twenty-one American prisoners of war in Korea refused to come home and chose to go to the People's Republic.
ops.record: Captors had subjected American prisoners to daily indoctrination and pressure to inform on one another, and some prisoners signed confessions. The journalist Edward Hunter had popularized the word brainwashing in 1950. Dwight Eisenhower signed Executive Order 10631 on August 17, 1955, and gave every service member the Code of Conduct.
ops.reading: The Code turned a lesson learned in the camps into a design rule every service member carries into captivity. Robert Lifton's study of 1961 drew its criteria of totalism from people who went through the same method.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. No routine prepared prisoners for captors who ran a psychological campaign rather than an interrogation.
ops.fix: Train every service member and every traveler at risk in the captor's method before capture, the job survival schools now do.

ops.title: The Formosa Resolution
ops.brief: Party forces stormed the island of Yijiangshan off the Zhejiang coast on January 18, 1955.
ops.record: The shelling of Kinmen had begun the previous September, and the United States had signed a mutual defense treaty with the Republic of China in December 1954. Congress passed the Formosa Resolution within days of Yijiangshan and authorized the president in advance to use force to defend Taiwan and the Pescadores. Eisenhower signed it on January 29, 1955.
ops.reading: Congress decided before the next event, which is the Phase principle a republic can run without surrendering oversight. The Hong Kong chapter finds the same rule in Britain's pledge of 2020, sixty-five years later.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender closed its Phase gap for one theater and let the authority lapse in 1974.
ops.fix: Pass standing authorities for defined triggers, with sunsets and reporting, so the answer lands in hours without a new vote.

ops.title: Qian Xuesen
ops.label: 1950 to 1955
ops.brief: In August 1950 federal agents in Los Angeles seized the crates of notes that Qian Xuesen, a founder of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, had packed for a trip home.
ops.record: The government had revoked Qian's clearance that June on suspicion of Communist Party ties, a charge he denied. Officials held him under restrictions close to house arrest for five years and let him sail for the mainland in September 1955, in a trade tied to the release of American prisoners. Qian went on to lead the People's Republic's missile program.
ops.reading: The United States deported the scientist it had trained on a charge it never proved, and it handed the Party a founder of its missile program. Suspicion by association rather than conduct cost more than any theft.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender judged a scientist by association and gave the adversary the talent it feared losing.
ops.fix: Judge researchers on documented conduct and keep them, because a talent expelled on suspicion becomes the adversary's gain.

ops.title: The Chinese Confession Program
ops.label: 1956 to 1965
ops.brief: In December 1955 Everett Drumright, the American consul general in Hong Kong, reported to Washington that fraud ran through Chinese immigration and that the Party could exploit it.
ops.record: The Immigration and Naturalization Service offered Chinese Americans who had entered on false papers a chance to confess in exchange for possible adjustment of status. A confession had to name every relative in the same paper family, and the service used the files against people it suspected of leftist politics. About thirty thousand people confessed before the program ended in 1965.
ops.reading: The program traded legal status for a registry of families, the Data and Surveillance domain that the United States ran on its own residents. The Party runs the same join today through relatives at home, and the guardrail answers both.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The defender collected family data under an amnesty and then used it for political screening.
ops.fix: Bind any amnesty's data to its stated purpose by law, so a relief program never becomes a surveillance program.

ops.title: The Hundred Flowers
ops.brief: In May 1957 the student Lin Xiling stood before a crowd at Peking University and told them the Party had become a privileged class.
ops.record: Mao invited criticism of the Party in the spring of 1957, and intellectuals answered with posters and speeches. On June 8 the People's Daily turned on the critics, and the Anti-Rightist Campaign labeled more than 550,000 people rightists. Many spent two decades in labor camps and internal exile.
ops.reading: The invitation mapped the critics before the strike fell, which is Stratagem 13 run on a nation's intellectuals. The Party had fewer honest reporters when the famine came two years later.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No rule protected speech the Party itself had invited.
ops.fix: Make invited criticism safe by law, because a system that punishes feedback loses its sensors.

ops.title: Kinmen
ops.brief: Party artillery opened fire on Kinmen on August 23, 1958.
ops.record: Tens of thousands of shells fell on the island on the first day. The Seventh Fleet escorted Nationalist resupply convoys from early September, and Nationalist pilots scored the first combat kills with American Sidewinder missiles on September 24. In October the Party announced it would shell only on odd-numbered days, and the ritual lasted until January 1, 1979.
ops.reading: The Party turned artillery into a calendar, and the calendar carried a message about its claim on Taiwan with less risk than an assault. The Taiwan chapter's named exercises run the same Phase routine at larger scale.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender left its commitment to the offshore islands ambiguous, and the Party probed the ambiguity.
ops.fix: State which positions a guarantee covers before the probe, and let ambiguity be a choice rather than a gap.

ops.title: Lushan
ops.brief: On July 14, 1959, Marshal Peng Dehuai sent Mao a private letter at the Lushan conference warning that the Great Leap Forward was failing.
ops.record: Mao circulated the letter and attacked Peng on July 23, and the conference purged him as the leader of an anti-Party clique. The campaign against right opportunism that followed punished cadres who reported shortfalls, and grain procurement continued at inflated targets. Scholarly estimates of deaths in the famine of 1959 to 1961 range from about fifteen million to forty-five million.
ops.reading: Lushan proves that coherence and entropy are separate dimensions. Every institution pulled one way, and the system produced the deadliest famine in recorded history because it punished the one signal that could have stopped it.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The Party had perfect vertical alignment and no horizontal feedback, so false reports moved up and grain moved out.
ops.fix: Protect the channel that carries bad news, and verify reports against independent measures before they drive policy.

ops.title: Lhasa and Camp Hale
ops.brief: On March 17, 1959, the Dalai Lama slipped out of the Norbulingka palace in Lhasa in disguise and began a two-week flight to India.
ops.record: Tibetans had risen against Party rule in Lhasa on March 10, and Party artillery shelled the city after the Dalai Lama left. Two CIA-trained Tibetans radioed news of his flight, and the agency trained Tibetan fighters at Camp Hale in Colorado from 1958 to 1964. Washington wound the program down as it moved toward the Party in the late 1960s and early 1970s.
ops.reading: The United States ran the borrowed knife on the Party's frontier and withdrew it when strategy changed, and the Tibetans who fought paid the cost. A patron who arms a resistance and then leaves teaches every later partner what the patronage is worth.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender's commitment ran on a policy clock rather than a treaty, and it ended when the policy did.
ops.fix: Match any commitment to people in harm's way with a horizon and an exit plan decided before they fight.

ops.title: Kennedy's Parole
ops.brief: On May 23, 1962, John Kennedy told reporters that the United States would admit several thousand refugees who had fled the mainland into Hong Kong.
ops.record: Famine and a loosened border sent tens of thousands of people from Guangdong into Hong Kong in April and May 1962, and Hong Kong's government returned most of them. Kennedy used the attorney general's parole power to admit refugees outside the quota system. About fifteen thousand arrived over the next three years.
ops.reading: The parole answered a famine the Party would not admit with a door the quota law would not open. The executive shielded people by decision because the statute had no rule for them.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The quota system had no category for people fleeing a famine their government denied.
ops.fix: Keep a standing refugee authority with published criteria, so rescue does not depend on a press conference.

ops.title: Lop Nur and the Pre-Announcement
ops.brief: On September 29, 1964, Secretary of State Dean Rusk told the press that the People's Republic might explode its first nuclear device in the near future.
ops.record: American intelligence had tracked the test site at Lop Nur and judged a test likely within months. The Party detonated its first device on October 16, 1964, two days after Nikita Khrushchev lost power in Moscow. Lyndon Johnson's statement that day said the test came as no surprise to the government.
ops.reading: The defender decided before the event and spent the surprise in advance, so the test landed as a confirmed forecast rather than a shock. Pre-announcement is the Phase principle run against a psychological effect.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The warning held because an owner mapped it to a public statement before the event.
ops.fix: Pre-announce what intelligence judges likely when surprise is the adversary's aim, as the United States did again before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

ops.title: The Hidden Divisions
ops.label: 1965 to 1969
ops.brief: In April 1965 Le Duan traveled to Beijing to ask the Party for support troops, and Liu Shaoqi agreed.
ops.record: The Party sent engineering, railway and anti-aircraft units to North Vietnam from June 1965 and withdrew them by 1969. Chinese sources put the total who served at about 320,000, with a peak near 170,000 in 1967. American intelligence tracked the deployments, and Washington kept them out of public view.
ops.reading: Both governments preferred silence, the Party to avoid a wider war and Washington to avoid a demand to fight one. Attribution managed by both sides is still Asymmetry, and it let the Party fight the United States at low cost.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender kept a combatant's role secret, so its public never weighed the true adversary.
ops.fix: Decide attribution policy on a published standard, so silence is a choice with owners rather than a habit.

ops.title: Sidney Rittenberg
ops.brief: In February 1968 Party security arrested Sidney Rittenberg, an American Party member who had worked for its broadcasters, and put him in solitary confinement.
ops.record: Rittenberg came to China as an Army linguist in 1945 and stayed to serve the Party. The Party had already imprisoned him from 1949 to 1955 on a false spy charge, and it held him again from 1968 to 1977. He left for the United States in 1980 and later advised American firms on business in China.
ops.reading: The Party consumes its allies as readily as its enemies, and a foreigner's loyalty buys no exemption. Rittenberg's decades of service ended in sixteen years of prison, the Consume stage applied to a true believer.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No government could reach an American held by a state with which the United States had no relations.
ops.fix: Keep consular channels open even with adversaries, because the absence of relations leaves citizens with no advocate.

ops.title: Lin Zhao
ops.brief: Party authorities in Shanghai executed Lin Zhao on April 29, 1968.
ops.record: The Party had labeled Lin a rightist at Peking University in 1957 and arrested her in 1960. In prison she wrote essays and letters, some in her own blood, rejecting the Party's claim on her conscience. Her family learned of her death when an official came to collect a fee for the bullet, according to accounts the filmmaker Hu Jie gathered.
ops.reading: The Party killed the writer and failed to kill the writing, which survived in archives and reached readers through Hu Jie's documentary of 2004. Memory is a domain the Party contests for decades, and it loses when records survive.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No court, press or church could stand between a young woman and a state that punished belief.
ops.fix: Fund archives that hold victims' records outside the Party's reach, so memory has a home the Party cannot raid.

ops.title: Ping-Pong
ops.brief: On April 4, 1971, the American table tennis player Glenn Cowan boarded the Chinese team's bus in Nagoya by mistake.
ops.record: Zhuang Zedong, a three-time world champion, greeted him on the bus and gave him a silk-screen of the Huangshan mountains. Mao Zedong approved an invitation to the American team two days later, and the players crossed from Hong Kong on April 10. Zhou Enlai received them in the Great Hall of the People on April 14. Richard Nixon announced steps to ease the trade embargo on the same day.
ops.reading: The Party chose a sport it dominated and players it controlled, so a chance meeting became a signal it could stage and withdraw at will. American audiences saw friendship between peoples, while the Party sent a message between governments. Zhuang later ran the sports commission under the Gang of Four, and after their fall the Party jailed him for four years. The signal belonged to the Party, and so did the messenger.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Americans read a staged gesture as the voice of a people who had no free channel to speak.
ops.fix: Welcome every exchange and credit the goodwill to the people who take part, while reading the state's intent from its acts alone.

ops.title: Polo I
ops.brief: Henry Kissinger feigned a stomach illness in Pakistan and flew in secret to Beijing on July 9, 1971.
ops.record: The flight ran through the channel of Yahya Khan, Pakistan's military ruler, whose army had begun a crackdown in East Pakistan that March. Kissinger spent about seventeen hours in talks with Zhou Enlai, and Nixon announced on July 15 that he would visit the People's Republic. On April 6 the consul general in Dacca, Archer Blood, had cabled a formal dissent against American silence on the killings. The State Department recalled Blood that June.
ops.reading: Washington routed a strategic shift through one intermediary, and that intermediary's war then shaped American policy in South Asia for the rest of the year. Kissinger's illness was Stratagem 6 run by an American. The Party chose the channel and the timing, and secrecy kept Congress and the allies out of the terms until Nixon went on television.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No one outside the White House owned the terms of the opening, so a single channel set the price for the whole government.
ops.fix: Brief the committees of jurisdiction in confidence before a secret channel commits the country, and keep the channel secret from everyone else.

ops.title: Resolution 2758
ops.brief: On October 25, 1971, the Republic of China's delegation walked out of the General Assembly before the vote that expelled it.
ops.record: The Assembly adopted Resolution 2758 by 76 votes to 35 with 17 abstentions. The text seated the representatives of the People's Republic and expelled the representatives of Chiang Kai-shek. It never mentions Taiwan and decides nothing about the island's status. The Party now cites the resolution as proof of its claim to Taiwan and uses it to keep Taiwanese passport holders and journalists out of United Nations buildings and meetings. In 2024 the State Department and several legislatures rejected that reading.
ops.reading: The Party turned a decision on credentials into a claim of sovereignty by repeating the claim until agencies wrote it into their rules, which is Stratagem 14. Time did the work, because each year of silence let the reading harden into practice.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The text stayed fixed, while each agency's access rules carried the Party's reading into daily practice.
ops.fix: State the plain text of the resolution in every forum, and hold each agency to what the members voted.

ops.title: The Communiqué's Verb
ops.brief: In Shanghai in February 1972, Richard Nixon approved a communiqué in which the United States acknowledged a position without adopting it.
ops.record: The Shanghai Communiqué of February 28, 1972 states that the United States acknowledges that all Chinese on either side of the Taiwan Strait maintain there is but one China, and that it does not challenge that position. The Chinese text renders the verb as renshi dao, which means to come to understand. The Chinese text of the 1979 normalization communiqué used chengren, the word for diplomatic recognition. When senators raised the change in 1979, the administration answered that the English text governed.
ops.reading: The Party reads each American text through its own translation and then cites the translation as the American position, which is Stratagem 25. The Party works in the space between an American One China policy and its own One China principle, and each new text widens that space.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Two governments kept two texts of one agreement, and nothing required the Party's text to carry the verb Washington chose.
ops.fix: Publish the governing text of every joint statement in both languages, and answer each divergent rendering on the record.

ops.title: Democracy Wall
ops.label: 1978 to 1979
ops.brief: On December 5, 1978, the zoo electrician Wei Jingsheng posted The Fifth Modernization on the Xidan wall in Beijing.
ops.record: The poster argued that the Party's Four Modernizations would fail without democracy. Deng Xiaoping tolerated the wall while its posters attacked his rivals and told foreign visitors that the constitution allowed them. In March 1979 Wei warned that Deng was becoming a new dictator, and police arrested him on March 29. A court sentenced him to fifteen years in October. In December the city moved the wall to a park and required every writer to register a name and workplace. In 1980 the National People's Congress struck the right to write big-character posters from the constitution.
ops.reading: The Party let speech run while it served a struggle among leaders and closed the channel once the speech turned on the new leader, which is Stratagem 16. Wei's arrest came seven weeks after Deng left the United States, once normalization and the state visit had closed.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Washington read tolerance as reform and set no test for when the tolerance would end.
ops.fix: Judge openness by what the state does to its critics after the visit ends, and say so in public.

ops.title: The Hat in Texas
ops.brief: Deng Xiaoping put on a ten-gallon hat at a rodeo outside Houston on February 2, 1979.
ops.record: The photograph ran on front pages across the country during a visit that began with the signing of the Agreement on Cooperation in Science and Technology on January 31. The agreement framed four decades of joint research under dozens of agency protocols. It reached its renewal date in August 2023. After short extensions the State Department renewed it in December 2024 with a narrower scope that leaves out critical and emerging technologies.
ops.reading: The hat bought goodwill on the evening news, while the agreement bought access to American laboratories for forty years, which is Stratagem 17. Americans enjoyed the gesture and seldom counted what the framework carried.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. No agency owned the total cost of the agreement, so each protocol answered only to its own sponsor.
ops.fix: Renew science agreements on fixed terms with a published list of closed fields, and review every protocol against it.

ops.title: The Punitive War after the Visit
ops.fullTitle: The Punitive War after the Visit (1979)
ops.brief: On January 29, 1979, Deng Xiaoping told Jimmy Carter in the Oval Office that the People's Republic would teach Vietnam a lesson.
ops.record: Carter handed Deng a letter the next morning that urged restraint. The People's Liberation Army crossed the Vietnamese border on February 17, twelve days after Deng left the United States, and withdrew in March after heavy losses on both sides. Washington called for the army to leave Vietnam and for Vietnamese troops to leave Cambodia.
ops.reading: Deng timed the war to follow the visit, so the American welcome read as consent in Moscow and Hanoi. The Party punished Vietnam to warn the Soviet Union, which is Stratagem 26, and Washington's hospitality supplied the cover.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Washington received advance notice of an invasion and had no principle that separated hosting a leader from lending him cover.
ops.fix: Answer advance notice of force with a public position before the force moves, so hospitality never reads as consent.

ops.title: The Taiwan Relations Act
ops.brief: On April 10, 1979, Jimmy Carter signed a law that Congress had written to fill the space his normalization left open.
ops.record: Recognition of the People's Republic on January 1, 1979 put the defense treaty with Taipei on a year's notice. The administration sent Congress a bill that said little about security, and Congress rewrote it. The Act treats any effort to decide Taiwan's future by other than peaceful means, including boycotts and embargoes, as a threat to the peace of the Western Pacific and of grave concern to the United States. It commits Washington to provide defensive arms, and it created the American Institute in Taiwan to carry relations without an embassy. The House passed the final bill 339 to 50, and the Senate 85 to 4.
ops.reading: The Party's three conditions for normalization aimed to pull the firewood from under Taipei's defense, which is Stratagem 19, and Congress put the firewood back by statute. The Act has outlasted every administration since, because a statute binds each executive whatever the preference of the day.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Congress took ownership of a commitment the executive had set aside and wrote it into law.
ops.fix: Write every security commitment that must outlast an administration into statute, with a named office to carry it.

ops.title: The Six Assurances
ops.brief: On July 14, 1982, James Lilley of the American Institute in Taiwan carried six assurances to President Chiang Ching-kuo in Taipei.
ops.record: The United States had set no date to end arms sales to Taiwan and would not consult the Party on them. It would not mediate, revise the Taiwan Relations Act, change its position on sovereignty or press Taipei to negotiate. Five weeks later the Joint Communiqué of August 17 said Washington intended to reduce arms sales over time. Ronald Reagan wrote in a memo the same day that any reduction depended on the Party's commitment to a peaceful solution. The memo stayed classified until 2020.
ops.reading: The Party reads the communiqué with its condition removed and cites it as a pledge to end arms sales, which is Stratagem 25. One president kept the condition in writing, and that page gave later officials a text to stand on.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The condition that governed the policy sat in a classified file for 38 years while the Party's reading ran in public.
ops.fix: Publish the conditions of every commitment with the commitment itself.

ops.title: Vincent Chin
ops.brief: A Chrysler plant supervisor and his laid-off stepson beat Vincent Chin with a baseball bat in Highland Park on June 19, 1982.
ops.record: Chin was Chinese American, and witnesses said Ronald Ebens blamed him for auto jobs lost to Japanese imports. He died four days later, days before his wedding. A Wayne County judge gave Ebens and his stepson Michael Nitz three years' probation and fines of $3,000 each. A federal jury convicted Ebens of a civil rights crime in 1984, but an appeals court overturned the verdict, and a second jury acquitted him in 1987.
ops.reading: Anger over lost jobs landed on a man who had nothing to do with them, because his killers read ancestry as allegiance. Every defender who repeats that error hands the Party the argument its United Front work makes, that the United States will never accept Americans of Chinese descent.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The court weighed the killing as a quarrel and had no principle that named the motive.
ops.fix: Keep ancestry out of every judgment of loyalty, and prosecute violence that turns on it as the crime it is.

ops.title: Hu Na
ops.label: 1982 to 1983
ops.brief: On July 20, 1982, the nineteen-year-old tennis player Hu Na left her team's hotel in Santa Clara and later sought asylum in the United States.
ops.record: She told American officials she feared persecution at home and had resisted pressure to join the Party. The Party demanded her return and warned of harm to relations. The Reagan administration granted her asylum on April 4, 1983. Three days later the Party canceled nineteen sports and cultural exchanges planned for the rest of the year.
ops.reading: The Party punished a whole program for one woman's choice, which is Stratagem 26, and it priced every future defection in lost access. The pressure ran down a gradient from a single athlete to every American institution that valued the exchanges.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. No one owned the exchanges as a whole, so the Party could cancel them at no cost to itself.
ops.fix: Plan exchanges so that a cancellation costs the side that cancels, and state in advance that asylum decisions will not bend to reprisal.

ops.title: Peace Pearl
ops.brief: In June 1984 Zhang Aiping became the first defense minister of the People's Republic to visit the United States.
ops.record: Washington had already approved the sale of 24 Sikorsky Black Hawk helicopters, and artillery radars and torpedoes followed. In 1986 the two governments agreed on Peace Pearl, a program worth about $550 million to fit American radar and fire-control systems to 55 J-8II interceptors. George H. W. Bush suspended military sales on June 5, 1989. The Party withdrew from Peace Pearl in 1990 and bought Soviet Su-27 fighters instead.
ops.reading: Each sale assumed a partnership that would outlast the program, and the army absorbed what it could before the partnership broke, which is Stratagem 12. The helicopters kept flying for the People's Liberation Army long after the American spare parts stopped.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. The program put American fire control on a platform the defender would never control, with no plan for the day the partnership ended.
ops.fix: Price every transfer of military technology on the assumption that the partnership ends, and keep the parts and the software on the American side.

ops.title: Fang Lizhi
ops.brief: On February 26, 1989, security police stopped the astrophysicist Fang Lizhi on his way to George H. W. Bush's banquet in Beijing.
ops.record: The embassy had invited Fang, whose speeches had inspired the student protests of 1986, and the Party kept him from the President's table. After the massacre Fang and his wife Li Shuxian took refuge in the American embassy on June 5. The Party charged them with counterrevolutionary crimes and issued warrants for their arrest. They stayed inside for more than a year until the Party let them fly to Britain in June 1990.
ops.reading: Individual officials made the choices that mattered, first by inviting a critic to a state dinner and then by opening the door when his life was at risk. The Party named Fang the black hand behind the movement, which is Stratagem 18, and the embassy denied it the ringleader it wanted.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The design held because the embassy applied the same principle in February and in June, that a guest the Party hunts is still a guest.
ops.fix: Write the refuge decision into doctrine so it rests on principle rather than on the courage of one ambassador.

ops.title: The Footage
ops.brief: In the days after June 4, 1989, a worker named Xiao Bin described the killings to an ABC News crew in Beijing.
ops.record: State television rebroadcast his interview with a number for citizens to call, and two women reported him within hours. He appeared on television under arrest and recanted. A court sentenced him to ten years. On June 13 the Ministry of Public Security issued a wanted list of 21 student leaders, and state television showed their photographs for days.
ops.reading: Foreign cameras gave the world its record of the massacre and gave the police their identifications. The asymmetry ran one way, because the network that aired a witness could not protect him once the Party turned his face into evidence.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Newsrooms treated a witness's face as content and had no rule for what a hostile state could do with it.
ops.fix: Protect sources in the edit as well as in the notebook, and obscure the faces of witnesses who remain within the state's reach.

ops.title: The Scowcroft Mission
ops.brief: Brent Scowcroft and Lawrence Eagleburger flew in secret to Beijing at the start of July 1989.
ops.record: George H. W. Bush had suspended military sales on June 5 and high-level exchanges on June 20. The trip broke his own suspension. Deng Xiaoping met the envoys and blamed the United States for the damage to relations. The White House kept the trip hidden until December, when the same two men made a second and public visit and reporters traced the first.
ops.reading: The mission accepted the Party's frame that the massacre was an internal affair and worked to keep the relationship whole. Bush trusted a personal channel to Deng that dated from his years in Beijing, and the Party learned that a massacre would cost it months of American coldness rather than years.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The sanctions stated a principle in public while the envoys set it aside in private.
ops.fix: Keep private channels open, and hold them to the terms the public sanctions state.

ops.title: Desert Storm Seen from Beijing
ops.brief: In January 1993 Jiang Zemin told the Central Military Commission that the army must prepare to win local wars under high-technology conditions.
ops.record: Coalition forces had broken Iraq's army in 1991 after six weeks of air war and a hundred hours on the ground. Party military journals spent the years after on precision strike, satellites and battlefield networks. The 1993 guidelines made local war under high-technology conditions the basis for planning. A 2004 revision changed the phrase to informatized conditions, and later defense white papers kept it.
ops.reading: The Party watched an American victory from across the river, which is Stratagem 9, and learned from it faster than the victors did. The lesson it drew was asymmetry, so it built missiles, satellites and cyber units to strike the networks that made American precision possible.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The United States showed its method to the world and assumed its lead would hold.
ops.fix: Design every American advantage on the assumption that the opponent studies it, and harden the networks it depends on first.

ops.title: The Chinese Student Protection Act
ops.brief: On November 30, 1989, George H. W. Bush vetoed a bill that would have let Chinese students stay in the United States after the massacre.
ops.record: Bush said he would protect the students by executive action, and his Executive Order 12711 of April 11, 1990 deferred their departure. The House voted to override the veto, and the Senate fell four votes short. In 1992 Congress passed the Chinese Student Protection Act, which let tens of thousands of students and scholars from the People's Republic apply for permanent residence.
ops.reading: Both branches chose to shield the people rather than return them to the Party's reach, and they argued only over the instrument. The Party later built talent programs aimed at this generation of graduates, programs that treat ancestry as a claim on loyalty that American law rejects.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The design held because Congress kept pressing after the veto and the President answered with an order of his own.
ops.fix: Keep a standing path to stay for students and scholars whose home state turns on them, so protection never waits for a veto fight.

ops.title: The Yinhe
ops.brief: In the summer of 1993 Captain Zhang Bingxi sailed the freighter Yinhe toward the Persian Gulf with American warships and aircraft shadowing it.
ops.record: American intelligence reported that the ship carried thiodiglycol and thionyl chloride, two precursors of mustard gas, bound for Iran. Washington asked the Gulf states to deny the ship port entry, and it waited at sea for weeks. A joint Saudi and American inspection at Dammam in early September found neither chemical in its 628 containers. The United States declined to apologize.
ops.reading: Washington accused in public before it verified, and the Party has taught the incident ever since as proof of American hegemony. The error muddied later accusations, including the 1997 sanctions on firms in the People's Republic that did sell chemical weapons precursors to Iran, which is Stratagem 20.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. A single intelligence report moved to a public accusation with no second source and no plan for a miss.
ops.fix: Verify before accusing in public, and publish the evidence and any correction with equal weight when a charge fails.

ops.title: Delinking
ops.brief: On May 26, 1994, Bill Clinton renewed the People's Republic's trade status and ended the link between trade and human rights.
ops.record: A year earlier his Executive Order 12850 had tied renewal to emigration and prison labor and to overall significant progress in five other areas. The Party rearrested Wei Jingsheng on April 1, 1994, weeks after he met Assistant Secretary of State John Shattuck. Warren Christopher reported that the Party had met the two required conditions and fallen short on the rest. American business groups lobbied hard for renewal, and Clinton chose trade.
ops.reading: The Party tested the linkage by jailing its best-known critic during the review and paid nothing for it. American companies carried the Party's case in Washington, which is Stratagem 3, and the Party learned that its market could outvote its prisoners.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The policy stated a condition and had no principle for what followed when the condition failed.
ops.fix: Attach human rights terms to specific tools that can bite, and publish the test and the result each year.

ops.title: Harry Wu and the Laogai
ops.brief: On June 19, 1995, border guards at Horgos detained Harry Wu as he entered from Kazakhstan on an American passport.
ops.record: Wu had spent nineteen years in the Party's labor camps before he left for the United States in 1985. He went back several times under cover and filmed camps whose goods reached export markets, and CBS aired his footage on 60 Minutes in 1991. A court convicted him of espionage in August 1995 and sentenced him to fifteen years, and the Party expelled him the same day. Hillary Clinton flew to the women's conference in Beijing two weeks later.
ops.reading: The camps ran a production line with a prison at one end and an export market at the other, and each camp carried a company name to cross the sea, which is Stratagem 1. Wu proved the link with a hidden camera, work the defender's own customs service had left undone.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Importers could not see a camp behind a company name, and customs kept no record that linked the two.
ops.fix: Require importers to trace goods to the factory floor, and publish the list of known camp enterprises.

ops.title: Magnequench
ops.brief: In 1995 the investment banker Archibald Cox Jr. led a group that bought Magnequench, the magnet division of General Motors in Anderson, Indiana.
ops.record: Two state firms of the People's Republic held most of the equity, and relatives of Deng Xiaoping by marriage ran both. The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States approved the sale on a pledge to keep production in the United States for at least five years. The company moved its lines to Tianjin and closed the Anderson plant in 2002. Congressional testimony tied its magnets to the guidance systems of American precision bombs.
ops.reading: The pledge ran on a clock the buyer could outwait, and the capability left once the clock ran out. The move lured a strategic industry away from its home ground, which is Stratagem 15, and the magnet line joined the Party's growing hold on rare-earth processing.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The review board accepted a promise with an expiry date and kept no power to stop the move once it lapsed.
ops.fix: Tie approval of foreign purchases in critical supply chains to terms that last as long as the capability matters, with a named office to enforce them.

ops.title: The Panchen Lama
ops.brief: On May 14, 1995, the Dalai Lama named six-year-old Gedhun Choekyi Nyima the eleventh Panchen Lama.
ops.record: Security forces took the boy and his parents into custody within days. The Party jailed Chadrel Rinpoche, the abbot who led the search. In November it staged a lottery with a golden urn and installed its own candidate, Gyaincain Norbu. Gedhun has not appeared in public since 1995. In 2020 Congress passed the Tibetan Policy and Support Act, which states that the choice of the next Dalai Lama belongs to Tibetan Buddhists alone.
ops.reading: The Party took a child to control a succession decades away, so Time became the weapon. It borrowed a Qing court urn to dress a political choice as a religious rite, which is Stratagem 14.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender voiced concern for twenty-five years before it wrote the principle of religious succession into law.
ops.fix: Name the officials who hold a disappeared person and apply the sanctions the law already allows, year after year.

ops.title: The Cornell Visit and the Carriers
ops.fullTitle: The Cornell Visit and the Carriers (1995 to 1996)
ops.label: 1995 to 1996
ops.brief: Lee Teng-hui returned to Cornell University on June 9, 1995 to speak at the school where he had earned his doctorate.
ops.record: Congress had pressed for his visa by votes of 396 to 0 in the House and 97 to 1 in the Senate. The Party answered with missile tests in the waters off Taiwan in July 1995 and again in March 1996, days before the island's first direct presidential election. Bill Clinton sent two aircraft carrier groups to the area, and Lee won the election.
ops.reading: The missile tests beat the grass to startle Taiwan's voters, which is Stratagem 13, and the voters did not startle. The army could not threaten the carriers in 1996, so the Party built the missiles, sensors and submarines that now hold carriers at risk far from the mainland.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. American power in the strait rested on platforms whose freedom of action the adversary could study and erode.
ops.fix: Plan the next crisis against the forces the adversary built after the last one.

ops.title: The Campaign Finance Scandal
ops.brief: In 1998 the fundraiser Johnny Chung told federal investigators that a lieutenant colonel in the People's Liberation Army had given him $300,000 for American campaigns.
ops.record: Chung said the money came from Liu Chaoying, a state aerospace executive and the daughter of the army's senior general. He pleaded guilty to campaign finance violations. The Senate Governmental Affairs Committee reported in 1998 that Party officials had planned to influence American elections, and its minority disputed how far the plan went. The Democratic National Committee returned about $2.8 million in questionable donations and then called donors with Asian surnames to question their citizenship.
