ops.reading: The Party ran money through a few intermediaries, and suspicion then fell on every American who shared their ancestry. That second result served the Party as well as the first, because it taught Asian Americans that their own institutions saw them as suspects.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No one owned the source of foreign money that reached campaigns through citizens, so scrutiny fell on ancestry instead of on money.
ops.fix: Trace the money rather than the donor's name, and apply the same test to every contribution.

ops.title: Loral and Hughes
ops.brief: On May 25, 1999, Representative Christopher Cox released a select committee report on how American technology had reached the Party's rocket and missile programs.
ops.record: A Long March 3B had crashed on launch at Xichang in February 1996 with a Loral satellite aboard. Loral and Hughes engineers shared failure analyses with Chinese rocket engineers after that crash and an earlier one, and the State Department charged both companies with exporting controlled data without a license. Congress returned commercial satellites to the Munitions List in 1999. Loral paid $14 million in 2002, and Boeing paid $32 million in 2003 for violations at the Hughes unit it had bought.
ops.reading: Knowledge ran downhill from a commercial review into a launch program that shares its engineering with the Party's missiles, which is Stratagem 12. Congress answered with the heaviest tool it had, and the new rules cost American satellite makers business for years.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The license routine covered satellites and launch services but not the failure reviews that followed a crash.
ops.fix: Treat failure analysis as controlled data under every export license, and brief engineers on the line before they sit down with a foreign launcher.

ops.title: Coercion as Persecution
ops.brief: In February 1997 Bill Clinton paroled the last Golden Venture passengers held in York, Pennsylvania, after nearly four years in custody.
ops.record: The freighter had run aground off Queens in June 1993, and ten of its passengers drowned. Many survivors sought asylum because the Party's birth planning officials had sterilized them or their wives or had threatened to. Immigration judges split on such claims until Congress acted in 1996. Section 601 of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act defined forced abortion and sterilization as persecution on account of political opinion.
ops.reading: The law named the Party's population program for what it was, a campaign of state force against families. The same government kept the Golden Venture passengers in jail while the courts caught up, so the defender recognized the persecution and punished its victims in the same years.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Immigration judges applied the refugee definition case by case, and the same facts won asylum in one court and lost in the next.
ops.fix: Define known patterns of state persecution in law, and release asylum seekers who pose no risk while their claims proceed.

ops.title: Kundun
ops.brief: In October 1998 Michael Eisner apologized to Premier Zhu Rongji for Disney's release of Kundun.
ops.record: Martin Scorsese's film about the Dalai Lama's youth had drawn warnings from Party officials before its release in December 1997. Disney released it in a small number of theaters, and the Party froze Disney's business on the mainland. Disney hired Henry Kissinger's consulting firm to repair the relationship, and Eisner's apology followed.
ops.reading: The Party punished one film to warn a whole industry, which is Stratagem 26. The studios learned the lesson and began to cut scripts before the Party needed to ask, as PEN America documented in 2020.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Each studio weighed its own market access alone, so no film carried the industry's collective interest.
ops.fix: Disclose every change made to a film for a foreign censor, so audiences and regulators can see the price of access.

ops.title: Exile as a Bargaining Chip
ops.fullTitle: Exile as a Bargaining Chip (1997 to 1998)
ops.label: 1997 to 1998
ops.brief: Wei Jingsheng landed in Detroit on November 16, 1997 after nearly eighteen years in the Party's prisons.
ops.record: The Party released him on medical parole two weeks after Jiang Zemin's state visit to Washington and sent him abroad rather than home. In April 1998 it sent the student leader Wang Dan to the United States two months before Bill Clinton's visit to the mainland. Neither man could return. After Clinton left, courts sentenced the founders of the China Democracy Party to long prison terms.
ops.reading: The Party traded prisoners for summits and kept the power to take more, so each release bought a visit while the prisons stayed full. Exile removed the critic from the country and turned a moral cost into a diplomatic credit, which is Stratagem 17.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Washington counted releases as progress and set no price for the arrests that replaced them.
ops.fix: Count arrests and releases on one ledger, and judge a summit on the net.

ops.title: Belgrade
ops.brief: On May 8, 1999, Ambassador James Sasser sat inside the American embassy in Beijing while protesters threw stones and firebombs at its walls.
ops.record: A B-2 bomber had struck the People's Republic's embassy in Belgrade with guided bombs during NATO's war over Kosovo, and the strike killed three Chinese journalists. The CIA had marked the building from outdated maps as a Yugoslav military supply office. The Party bused students to the American embassy and consulates, and protesters burned the consul general's residence in Chengdu. Washington apologized and paid $4.5 million to the victims' families and $28 million for the damage to the embassy.
ops.reading: The Party set a real American error inside its story of national humiliation and staged the anger it wanted, which is Stratagem 14. It opened the protests and closed them on its own schedule.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The targeting database carried an outdated address, and no check caught it before the strike.
ops.fix: Verify every fixed target against current sources and a no-strike list, and publish the investigation when a strike goes wrong.

ops.title: The 610 Office and the Golden Shield
ops.fullTitle: The 610 Office and the Golden Shield (1999 to 2023)
ops.label: 1999 to 2023
ops.brief: Three days after Jiang Zemin ordered a campaign against Falun Gong, the Party created an office on June 10, 1999 and named it for the date.
ops.record: The ban followed on July 20, 1999. The 610 Office then ran arrests, forced conversion classes and camps for practitioners. The Ministry of Public Security built the Golden Shield Project in the same years to link surveillance and police databases across the country. Falun Gong practitioners sued Cisco in 2011 and alleged that the company built features into Golden Shield to identify and track them. The Ninth Circuit let most claims proceed on July 7, 2023, and Cisco asked the Supreme Court to review the ruling.
ops.reading: The Party fused a political campaign with a police network and bought parts of the network abroad, which is Stratagem 3. An American appeals court held that a company can face trial for aiding abuse through the systems it sells, and the case turns on what Cisco knew and built.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Export rules covered crime-control items such as fingerprint gear but not the network equipment that runs a police state.
ops.fix: Extend export controls to surveillance systems by function rather than by product list, and require sellers to screen for police end users.

ops.title: Wen Ho Lee
ops.label: 1999 to 2000
ops.brief: On September 13, 2000, Judge James Parker apologized from the bench to Wen Ho Lee for the way the government had held him.
ops.record: Lee, a Los Alamos scientist born in Taiwan, had spent 278 days in solitary confinement after investigators named him in the search for a leak of W88 warhead data. Prosecutors charged him with 59 counts of mishandling classified files and never charged him with espionage. He pleaded guilty to one count and went free that day. In 2006 the government and five news organizations paid him about $1.6 million to settle his privacy suit.
ops.reading: The investigation narrowed to one man before it tested the evidence, and the W88 question has never reached a public answer. A defender who picks suspects by origin hands the Party a recruiting argument and leaves the real leak unfound.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The judge who freed Lee said the government had embarrassed the nation, and no principle had stopped the case before it reached him.
ops.fix: Test every counterintelligence lead against the evidence before naming anyone, and keep ancestry off the suspect list.

ops.title: PNTR and Accession
ops.label: 2000 to 2001
ops.brief: On March 8, 2000, Bill Clinton told an audience at Johns Hopkins that the Party's effort to control the internet was like trying to nail Jell-O to the wall.
ops.record: The House passed permanent normal trade relations 237 to 197 on May 24, 2000, and the Senate followed 83 to 15. The same act created the Congressional-Executive Commission on China to monitor human rights and the rule of law. The People's Republic joined the World Trade Organization on December 11, 2001. Economists later estimated that the surge of imports cost the United States 2.0 to 2.4 million jobs from 1999 to 2011.
ops.reading: Accession ended the annual vote that had given Congress leverage each spring, and the relationship changed phase. The Party entered the host's trading system as a guest and began to shape its rules, which is Stratagem 30, while it kept the controls Clinton expected the internet to break.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The policy rested on a theory that trade would open the system, and no one set a test for when the theory had failed.
ops.fix: State the outcome a trade bargain should produce, and review it on a fixed schedule with the power to change terms.

ops.title: The EP-3
ops.brief: On April 1, 2001, Lieutenant Shane Osborn landed a damaged EP-3E on Hainan Island after a fighter of the People's Liberation Army Navy struck it over the South China Sea.
ops.record: The fighter's pilot, Wang Wei, died in the collision. The Party held the twenty-four crew members for eleven days and released them after Washington delivered a letter that said sorry twice, once for his death and once for the landing without clearance. The crew had destroyed part of the plane's classified equipment and data before landing, and a Navy review found the destruction incomplete. The Party returned the aircraft in pieces aboard a Russian cargo plane that July.
ops.reading: The Party turned an accident that followed its pilot's aggressive intercepts into a demand for an apology, and it presented Washington's wording at home as a confession. It also held the aircraft long enough to study what the crew could not destroy, which is Stratagem 5.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The aircraft carried more classified material than its crew could destroy in the minutes before landing.
ops.fix: Carry only the data a mission needs, and build destruction into the equipment rather than leaving it to a crew in an emergency.

ops.title: ETIM and the Guantánamo Uyghurs
ops.brief: On August 26, 2002, Deputy Secretary of State Richard Armitage announced in Beijing that the United States had designated the East Turkestan Islamic Movement a terrorist group.
ops.record: The Party had sought the listing since the September 11 attacks and used it to cast Uyghur dissent as terrorism. American forces had already captured twenty-two Uyghur men in Afghanistan and Pakistan and sent them to Guantánamo. The military cleared them in the years after, but none could go home without risk of torture, and they waited years for third countries to take them. In November 2020 the State Department removed the group from its Terrorist Exclusion List and said no credible evidence showed it had existed for more than a decade.
ops.reading: Washington gave the Party a label it could stretch over a whole people, and the Party later cited that label to justify its camps in Xinjiang. The designation lent American authority to a campaign against Uyghurs, which is Stratagem 3.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Washington listed a group on evidence it could not test, and the listing outlived the group.
ops.fix: List a group only on evidence the defender can verify for itself, and review each listing on a fixed schedule.

ops.title: SARS and Jiang Yanyong
ops.brief: On April 8, 2003, the retired army surgeon Jiang Yanyong wrote that Beijing's military hospitals held far more SARS patients than the health minister had admitted.
ops.record: Minister Zhang Wenkang had told reporters on April 3 that the city had twelve cases. Time magazine published Jiang's account, and on April 20 the Party fired Zhang and the mayor of Beijing as the city's reported count jumped from 37 to 339. The virus had spread from Guangdong since November 2002 while officials suppressed reports. It reached about thirty countries and killed 774 people. In 2004 the army detained Jiang for seven weeks after he urged the Party to reassess June 4.
ops.reading: The Party fired two officials and kept the system that had silenced the reports, which is Stratagem 21. It then detained the doctor whose warning it had acted on, so the lesson its officials kept was silence.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The world's warning system depended on case counts from a government that controlled every count.
ops.fix: Pair official case counts with independent signals such as hospital reports, travel data and sequenced samples, and act on the gap between them.

ops.title: Titan Rain and Shawn Carpenter
ops.fullTitle: Titan Rain and Shawn Carpenter (2003 to 2005)
ops.label: 2003 to 2005
ops.brief: In 2004 Shawn Carpenter, a network analyst at Sandia National Laboratories, followed an intruder's trail from American defense networks to computers in Guangdong.
ops.record: He passed what he found to Army counterintelligence and the FBI, and Sandia fired him in January 2005 for sharing it. Investigators called the campaign Titan Rain, and it had reached networks at defense contractors, Army commands and NASA. In 2007 a New Mexico jury awarded Carpenter $4.7 million against Sandia.
ops.reading: One analyst saw the pattern because he followed it past his employer's boundary, and his employer punished him for crossing it. The intruders hid inside ordinary traffic, which is Stratagem 1. Washington never attributed Titan Rain in public, so the record stops at Carpenter's trace.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No owner joined a laboratory's network logs to the government's counterintelligence, so the one man who joined them lost his job.
ops.fix: Give every network defender a protected path to report foreign intrusions to the government, and bar retaliation against those who use it.

ops.title: Shi Tao and Yahoo
ops.label: 2004 to 2005
ops.brief: On April 20, 2004, the journalist Shi Tao emailed notes on a Party directive about the Tiananmen anniversary from his Yahoo account to an editor in New York.
ops.record: Yahoo's Hong Kong subsidiary gave state security the account information that tied the email to him. A court in Changsha sentenced him to ten years in April 2005 for leaking state secrets. In November 2007 Representative Tom Lantos told Yahoo's leaders at a hearing that they were moral pygmies, and that month Yahoo settled a suit that the families of Shi and another jailed writer had brought.
ops.reading: The Party used an American company's records to convict a journalist, which is Stratagem 3. Every data center a company runs inside the Party's reach becomes a node in the Party's network whether the company intends it or not.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Yahoo stored user identities where the Party's security services could compel them and had no rule for a request that sought a dissident.
ops.fix: Keep user identities outside the reach of states that jail speech, and publish every demand for them.

ops.title: CNOOC and Unocal
ops.brief: On June 23, 2005, Fu Chengyu of CNOOC offered $18.5 billion in cash for the American oil company Unocal.
ops.record: CNOOC's parent was a state company, and state banks supplied cheap loans for the offer. The House voted 398 to 15 for a resolution that the sale would threaten national security, and Congress wrote a delay into the energy bill. CNOOC withdrew on August 2, and Unocal went to Chevron.
ops.reading: State financing gave the bidder a cost of capital no private rival could match, and the bid probed how Washington would answer, which is Stratagem 13. Congress answered with a vote rather than a rule, and later buyers from the mainland favored smaller assets and minority stakes.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The review process had no clear owner for a deal in which a state lender stood behind a listed company, so Congress filled the gap with a floor vote.
ops.fix: Treat state financing as state ownership in every investment review, and decide such cases by rule rather than in the heat of a headline.

ops.title: The ASAT Test
ops.brief: In January 2007 Nicholas Johnson, NASA's chief scientist for orbital debris, began counting the fragments of a weather satellite that a missile had shattered over the mainland.
ops.record: The missile rose from the Xichang area on January 11 and struck the retired Fengyun-1C at about 865 kilometers. The Party said nothing for twelve days. The strike left more than three thousand trackable fragments, the largest debris cloud on record, and much of it will orbit for decades. The Party formed the Strategic Support Force in 2015 to fight in space and cyberspace, and in 2024 it split that force into separate aerospace, cyber and information arms.
ops.reading: The test showed that American satellites sat within reach, and the silence kept Washington guessing about intent. Orbit is a system near its critical point, so one strike imposed a cost on every nation that uses it.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. American military and commercial power depended on satellites with no defense against a missile they could see coming.
ops.fix: Spread capability across many small satellites so that no single strike matters, and lead a ban on tests that create debris.

ops.title: Melamine
ops.label: 2007 to 2008
ops.brief: On September 8, 2008, Prime Minister Helen Clark of New Zealand told her diplomats to go around provincial officials and warn the central government about poisoned infant formula.
ops.record: Sanlu, a dairy partly owned by New Zealand's Fonterra, had received complaints about sick infants since late 2007 and kept selling. Local officials held the news through the Beijing Olympics. The formula sickened about 300,000 infants and killed six. A year earlier melamine in wheat gluten and rice protein from two mainland suppliers had killed pets across the United States and forced the recall of more than 60 million packages of pet food.
ops.reading: Suppliers added melamine to fake protein readings, and the Olympic calendar kept the poison on shelves. The Party executed two men and jailed Sanlu's chairwoman for life in 2009, which is Stratagem 21, and left intact the system that had held the news.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Protein tests measured nitrogen, so a cheap chemical rich in nitrogen passed as food.
ops.fix: Test imported food and feed for what they contain rather than for a proxy, and share contamination findings across borders within days.

ops.title: Heparin
ops.brief: In March 2008 Janet Woodcock of the Food and Drug Administration announced that a counterfeit chemical had entered American heparin through a plant in Changzhou.
ops.record: The chemical, oversulfated chondroitin sulfate, mimicked heparin in the standard tests and cost a fraction of the real drug. Baxter recalled its heparin, and the agency linked the contaminated product to dozens of deaths and hundreds of severe reactions. The agency had never inspected the Changzhou plant before the crisis because it had confused its name with another site. Officials of the People's Republic denied that the contaminant caused any deaths.
ops.reading: Someone upstream swapped a cheap fake into a drug's structure and kept the shape the tests expected, which is Stratagem 25. No one upstream has answered for it, because the investigation stopped at a border the defender could not cross.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The agency's inspection routine confused two plants and left the one that mattered unvisited.
ops.fix: Inspect every foreign plant that makes an active ingredient before its product reaches a patient, and test for adulterants as well as for identity.

ops.title: The Torch in San Francisco
ops.brief: In San Francisco on April 9, 2008, the torchbearer Majora Carter pulled a small Tibetan flag from her sleeve and lost her place in the relay.
ops.record: The relay reached the city weeks after the Party crushed protests in Lhasa. Officials rerouted it without notice to avoid the crowds, and the closing ceremony moved to the airport. Campus associations brought thousands of students to wave the national flag along the route, beside Tibetan and human rights protesters. The flame's guards, a unit of the People's Armed Police in blue tracksuits, ran beside it in every city.
ops.reading: The Party carried its security model abroad with the flame and filled the streets with flags to show a unanimity it had to organize, which is Stratagem 29. The contest over the route was a contest over who speaks for Chinese people in an American city.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No American authority owned the question of a foreign state's security unit working inside a city's public event.
ops.fix: Set terms for any foreign security detail before a public event begins, and keep public space open to every lawful protester on equal terms.

ops.title: The Drywall Cases
ops.label: 2009 to 2019
ops.brief: In July 2014 Judge Eldon Fallon held Taishan Gypsum in contempt and barred it from doing business in the United States after it walked out of his court.
ops.record: Builders had installed drywall from the People's Republic in thousands of homes after the hurricanes of 2004 and 2005. The boards released sulfur gases that corroded wiring and appliances, and many families left their homes. Taishan, a subsidiary of a state-owned building materials group, defaulted and then argued that its parent enjoyed sovereign immunity. The court rejected the claim, and Taishan agreed in 2019 to pay $248 million.
ops.reading: A state-owned supplier treated an American court as optional and retreated from it until the court threatened its parent's business, which is Stratagem 36. The families waited more than a decade for money their own courts had awarded.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Importers carried no bond or insurance for a foreign supplier that American courts struggled to reach.
ops.fix: Require importers of building materials to carry insurance or a bond that answers for defects, whoever made them.

ops.title: Aurora
ops.brief: On January 12, 2010, Google's chief legal officer David Drummond wrote that intruders from the mainland had broken into the company's systems and targeted the Gmail accounts of human rights activists.
ops.record: At least twenty other companies had faced the same campaign, which the security firm McAfee named Aurora. Google stopped censoring its search results on the mainland and moved the service to Hong Kong in March. Former officials said in 2013 that the intruders had reached Google's records of American surveillance orders, which could reveal which of the Party's agents the FBI was watching.
ops.reading: One breach served two ends, the hunt for the Party's critics and a look at the hunters of its own agents, which is Stratagem 12. Google named the source in public and left the market, and few companies followed.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. The company's system for lawful surveillance orders became a target, because a door built for the government opens for anyone who breaks in.
ops.fix: Guard lawful access systems like the crown jewels, and assume every stored surveillance order is a target.

ops.title: Liu Xiaobo's Empty Chair
ops.brief: On December 10, 2010, the Nobel Committee placed Liu Xiaobo's diploma on an empty chair in Oslo.
ops.record: Liu had helped write Charter 08, a call for constitutional government that more than ten thousand people signed, and a court sentenced him to eleven years for inciting subversion. The Party pressed governments to stay away from the ceremony, and about eighteen did. It froze relations with Norway for six years and held his wife Liu Xia under house arrest without charge. Liu died in custody of liver cancer on July 13, 2017.
ops.reading: The Party jailed a writer for a document and then punished a country for a prize its government did not award, which is Stratagem 26. The empty chair became the image of the prize, and the Party never let Liu leave to fill it.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No alliance owned the response when the Party punished Norway, so one small country carried the cost of a shared value alone.
ops.fix: Answer the economic punishment of one ally for a shared value with a shared response, agreed in advance.

ops.title: Game of Pawns
ops.brief: In 2004 Glenn Duffie Shriver, an American student in Shanghai, answered a newspaper ad that paid him $120 for an essay on relations between the United States and the People's Republic.
ops.record: The woman who placed the ad introduced him to intelligence officers of the People's Republic, who paid him more than $70,000 over several years. At their direction he applied to the State Department's Foreign Service and then to the CIA's clandestine service. He pleaded guilty in October 2010 and received a sentence of 48 months in January 2011. The FBI later made his case into a training film called Game of Pawns.
ops.reading: The officers started with a small payment for harmless work and raised the stakes by degrees, a gradient the recruit could justify one step at a time. The prize was the student's future access, which is Stratagem 17.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The clearance routine held, and investigators stopped Shriver before he joined.
ops.fix: Warn students before they go abroad about how approaches begin, and give them a safe path to report one without penalty.

ops.title: Chen Guangcheng
ops.brief: In April 2012 the blind lawyer Chen Guangcheng climbed the wall of his farmhouse in Shandong and slipped past the guards who had held him since 2010.
ops.record: Chen had exposed forced abortions and sterilizations in Linyi in 2005 and served more than four years in prison. Friends drove him to Beijing, and American diplomats brought him into the embassy on April 26. He left on May 2 under a deal that let him study law on the mainland, and within hours he said he feared for his family and wanted to leave. The Party let him fly to New York on May 19.
ops.reading: The embassy's first deal rested on the Party's word, and it held only because Chen changed his mind and Washington changed with him. A local court later jailed his nephew while officials harassed his relatives, which is Stratagem 10 read to the end.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The embassy negotiated a protected man's future on the word of the government that had jailed and beaten him.
ops.fix: Never trade a protected person's safety for assurances from the government that persecuted him, and let the person decide with full information.

ops.title: Scarborough to The Hague
ops.label: 2012 to 2016
ops.brief: On January 22, 2013, Philippine Foreign Secretary Albert del Rosario announced that his government would take its dispute with the People's Republic to an arbitral tribunal under the law of the sea.
ops.record: In April 2012 the Philippine navy had found mainland fishing boats inside Scarborough Shoal, and maritime surveillance ships of the People's Republic moved in to block any arrest. American diplomats brokered what they described as a mutual withdrawal in June. The Philippine ships left, and the mainland ships stayed. On July 12, 2016, the tribunal found no legal basis for historic rights inside the nine-dash line. The Party called the award null and void.
ops.reading: The Party took the shoal by staying after the other side left, which is Stratagem 30, and possession then did work that law could not undo. The ruling stands in international law and has not moved a single ship.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The United States brokered a withdrawal with no means to verify it and no plan for a side that stayed.
ops.fix: Attach verification and a stated consequence to every brokered deal, and act on the consequence when either side breaks it.

ops.title: Ilham Tohti
ops.label: 2013 to 2014
ops.brief: On January 15, 2014, police took the economist Ilham Tohti from his home in Beijing.
ops.record: Tohti taught at Minzu University and ran Uyghur Online, a website that carried debate between Uyghurs and Han Chinese about policy in Xinjiang. A court in Urumqi sentenced him to life in prison for separatism in September 2014, and seven of his students received prison terms. He won the Václav Havel Prize and the Sakharov Prize in 2019. Mass detention of Uyghurs in camps began about three years after his trial.
ops.reading: The Party cast the moderate who argued for its own autonomy laws as the ringleader of separatism, which is Stratagem 18. Removing the bridge came first, and the camps came after.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defenders treated a moderate's life sentence as a single human rights case rather than as a warning of what the state intended for his people.
ops.fix: Read the jailing of moderates as an early warning, and prepare sanctions and trade rules before the mass action comes.

ops.title: The Rose Garden Pledges
ops.brief: On September 25, 2015, Xi Jinping told reporters in the Rose Garden that the People's Republic did not intend to militarize the islands it was building in the Spratlys.
ops.record: The same day he and Barack Obama agreed that neither government would conduct or knowingly support cyber theft of intellectual property for commercial advantage. Security firms reported fewer commercial intrusions from mainland groups in the months after. By 2018 the Party had placed antiship and antiaircraft missiles on Fiery Cross, Subi and Mischief reefs. In December 2018 the Justice Department charged two hackers who worked with the Ministry of State Security in the APT10 campaign against American companies.
ops.reading: Neither pledge carried a trigger, so time turned each into a record of broken words rather than a constraint. The pledges bought a quiet interval while the reefs hardened, which is Stratagem 1.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Neither pledge carried verification or a named response, so breaking them cost the Party nothing.
ops.fix: Accept no security pledge without a verification method and a response agreed in advance.

ops.title: Mo Hailong
ops.brief: In May 2011 a DuPont Pioneer field manager found Mo Hailong on his knees in a test field in Iowa.
ops.record: Mo directed international business for the Beijing Dabeinong Technology Group, whose subsidiary Kings Nower Seed sold corn seed on the mainland. He and others took inbred seed from fields that grew the parent lines of DuPont Pioneer and Monsanto hybrids and bought farms in Iowa and Illinois during the scheme. Investigators found seed hidden in microwave popcorn boxes. Mo pleaded guilty on January 27, 2016, and received 36 months in October.
ops.reading: Parent seed carries years of breeding in a pocketful of kernels, so a few trips along Iowa roads could shortcut a decade of research. The theft took what lay open in the fields, which is Stratagem 12.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. The companies guarded their laboratories and left their most valuable genetics in open fields along public roads.
ops.fix: Protect breeding lines where they grow, and give farmers and rural sheriffs a simple way to report strangers in test plots.

ops.title: The FARA Gap
ops.label: 2017 to 2024
ops.brief: In May 2017 a request from Vice Minister of Public Security Sun Lijun reached the casino executive Steve Wynn.
ops.record: Sun wanted the exiled businessman Guo Wengui removed from the United States, and the fundraiser Elliott Broidy brokered the approach. Wynn pressed the request with the President and other officials until October 2017. Broidy pleaded guilty in 2020 to a related charge and received a pardon in January 2021. The Justice Department sued in 2022 to force Wynn to register as a foreign agent, and the courts dismissed the suit. The appeals court held on June 14, 2024 that the duty to register ended when the representation ended.
ops.reading: The Party reached the Oval Office through Americans with access, which is Stratagem 3. The courts read the registration law to expire with the relationship, so a finished influence campaign owes the public no record.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The registration routine tracked agents while they worked and lost them once the work ended.
ops.fix: Require disclosure of past foreign agency within a set period, whether or not the relationship continues.

ops.title: The Handler
ops.brief: Belgian police arrested the intelligence officer Xu Yanjun on April 1, 2018, when he arrived for a meeting he had set up himself.
ops.record: Xu, a deputy division director in the Ministry of State Security, had come to collect design data on GE Aviation's composite fan module for jet engines. The GE engineer he had cultivated was working with the company and the FBI. Belgium extradited Xu, and a jury convicted him of economic espionage and trade secret conspiracies in November 2021. He received 20 years in November 2022. Xu had also directed Ji Chaoqun, a student in Chicago who enlisted in the Army Reserve in 2016, and a jury convicted Ji in September 2022.
ops.reading: An engineer reported the approach and let the FBI run it, so the handler walked into a meeting he had arranged himself. The officer's own recruitment turned against him, which is Stratagem 33.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. The design held because the company's security team and the FBI treated the first contact as a shared problem.
ops.fix: Give every engineer a fast path to report an approach, and let counterintelligence decide how to use it.

ops.title: The Network Rolled Up
ops.label: 2010 to 2019
ops.brief: In April 2010 two intelligence officers of the People's Republic approached the former CIA officer Jerry Chun Shing Lee and offered him $100,000 in cash.
ops.record: Lee had left the agency in 2007, and in August 2012 FBI agents found notebooks in his Honolulu hotel room with the true names of CIA assets and their meeting places. Between 2010 and 2012 the Party's security services killed or imprisoned as many as twenty CIA sources on the mainland, according to reporting in 2017. The FBI arrested Lee in January 2018. He pleaded guilty to conspiracy to deliver national defense information and received 19 years in November 2019.
ops.reading: The public record does not settle whether Lee, a compromised communications system or both gave the Party the names. A network that depends on one channel or one officer's memory fails all at once, which is Criticality at its most lethal. The Party shut the door and took everyone inside, which is Stratagem 22.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. A departing officer carried source names in notebooks, and no control stopped the record from leaving with him.
ops.fix: Treat source identities as data that never leaves a controlled system, and compartment networks so one breach cannot expose them all.

ops.title: ZTE
ops.brief: In April 2018 Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross barred American companies from selling parts to ZTE for seven years.
ops.record: ZTE had pleaded guilty in 2017 to shipping American technology to Iran and North Korea and had paid $1.19 billion. Commerce found that it had then lied about disciplining the employees responsible. Without American chips the company halted major operations within weeks. In June the administration settled for a $1 billion fine, $400 million in escrow and new leadership, and a Senate attempt to restore the ban died in conference.
ops.reading: One American rule stopped a national champion within weeks, and the settlement showed that the Party could buy the rule back at the leaders' table. ZTE shed its leadership and kept its business, which is Stratagem 21, and the Party poured money into domestic chips once it learned where the chokepoint lay.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. An enforcement action for sanctions violations became a bargaining chip in trade talks, so its force depended on the negotiation of the day.
ops.fix: Keep export enforcement out of trade negotiations, and require any settlement of a denial order to meet published terms.

ops.title: Soybeans and the Des Moines Insert
ops.fullTitle: Soybeans and the Des Moines Insert (2018)
ops.brief: On September 30, 2018, Ambassador Terry Branstad wrote in the Des Moines Register that a leading newspaper on the mainland had refused to print his essay.
ops.record: A week earlier China Daily had paid for a four-page supplement in the Register that warned Iowa farmers about the costs of the trade war. The Party's retaliatory tariffs that July had hit soybeans and other farm goods, and analysts found them aimed at counties that had voted for the President in 2016. Soybean exports to the mainland fell from about $12 billion in 2017 to about $3 billion in 2018. The Agriculture Department announced about $28 billion in aid for farmers over two years.
ops.reading: The Party picked targets for their weight in American politics rather than their weight in trade, which is Stratagem 26, and then spoke to the farmers in their own paper. Washington answered with aid, and the buyers moved to Brazil.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. American farm exports depended on one buyer that could shift its purchases overnight, and no plan spread that risk before the tariffs came.
ops.fix: Build export markets for farm goods in several countries before a trade fight begins, so one buyer cannot hold a state's farmers hostage.

ops.title: Meng Wanzhou and the Two Michaels
ops.fullTitle: Meng Wanzhou and the Two Michaels (2018 to 2021)
ops.label: 2018 to 2021
ops.brief: State security officers detained Michael Kovrig in Beijing on December 10, 2018, nine days after Canada arrested Meng Wanzhou at American request.
ops.record: Meng, Huawei's chief financial officer, faced American charges of bank fraud tied to sanctions on Iran. The Party detained Michael Spavor the same week and held both men for 1,019 days. A court sentenced Spavor to eleven years for espionage in August 2021. Meng reached a deferred prosecution agreement with the Justice Department on September 24, 2021. She flew home, and the two Michaels flew to Canada within hours.
ops.reading: The Party could not seize the prosecutor, so it seized two citizens of the ally that made the arrest, which is Stratagem 26. The exchange set a price on every allied citizen on the mainland, and the clock ran on the hostages rather than on the defendant.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The United States asked an ally to make an arrest and had no plan to protect the ally's citizens from reprisal.
ops.fix: Agree with allies in advance on how to answer hostage-taking, and treat a seized allied citizen as a charge on the whole alliance.

ops.title: The Class Scheduling of Fentanyl
ops.brief: On April 1, 2019, Liu Yuejin of the National Narcotics Control Commission announced that all fentanyl-related substances would come under control as a class from May 1.
ops.record: The step followed a pledge at the Buenos Aires summit of December 2018. Direct shipments of finished fentanyl to the United States fell. Suppliers shifted to precursor chemicals that the rule did not cover, and Mexican cartels made the drug from them. Deaths from synthetic opioids in the United States passed 70,000 a year in 2021 and 2022. In November 2023 the Party agreed to curb precursor exports. A House select committee reported in 2024 that the state had paid export tax rebates on some of the same chemicals.
ops.reading: The rule answered the demand Washington made and left the precursor trade open, so the flow changed form and kept its volume. The trade shed its old shell and kept moving, which is Stratagem 21.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The rule controlled a list of substances, and chemists changed the product faster than officials changed the list.
ops.fix: Control chemical families by structure, and follow the money through the payment networks that move it.

ops.title: Zoom and the Tiananmen Meetings
ops.brief: In May and June 2020 Julien Jin, a Zoom employee in the People's Republic who served as the company's liaison to Party security services, shut down meetings that commemorated the Tiananmen massacre.
ops.record: Prosecutors said Jin and others fabricated evidence that the meetings broke the terms of service, created fake accounts in dissidents' names and passed users' names and email addresses to officials of the People's Republic. At least four meetings went dark, and many participants lived in the United States, some in Queens and on Long Island. The Justice Department charged Jin on December 18, 2020. He remains outside American custody.
ops.reading: The Party's police reached into an American platform's trust and safety process and censored Americans on American soil, which is Stratagem 30. No police station was needed when a platform's own employee could end the meeting.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. The platform's moderation routine accepted evidence from an employee who answered to a foreign police service.
ops.fix: Wall off decisions about American users from staff subject to a foreign security service, and log every takedown request by its source.

ops.title: The Journalists' Expulsion
ops.brief: The Wall Street Journal's deputy bureau chief Josh Chin learned on February 19, 2020 that he and two colleagues had five days to leave the mainland.
ops.record: The foreign ministry cited a headline on an opinion essay that called the People's Republic the real sick man of Asia. A day earlier the State Department had designated five state media outlets as foreign missions, and in March it capped the number of mainland citizens they could employ in the United States. On March 17 the Party expelled about a dozen American reporters from the New York Times, the Journal and the Washington Post and barred them from working in Hong Kong.
ops.reading: The Party matched a cap on its state media staff with the removal of reporters who had covered the outbreak's first months, and the trade favored the side that fears its press. Removing the reporters removed the fuel of independent reporting, which is Stratagem 19.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Reciprocity treated state media outlets and independent newsrooms as equal units, so each round of retaliation cost the free press more.
ops.fix: Answer expulsions of journalists with measures aimed at the state that expels them, and never trade independent reporters for state media staff.

ops.title: The Bingtuan
ops.label: 1954 to 2020
ops.brief: In October 1954 Mao Zedong's government ordered demobilized soldiers in Xinjiang to form a production and construction corps that would farm, build and garrison the region.
ops.record: The Corps grew into a state within the region that runs its own cities, courts and police. It grows a large share of Xinjiang's cotton and settled Han migrants across Uyghur lands for decades. The Treasury Department sanctioned the Corps and two of its officials on July 31, 2020 for serious human rights abuse. In December customs officers began to hold its cotton at the border.
ops.reading: Settlement turned soldiers from guests into hosts on Uyghur land, which is Stratagem 30. The Corps ran the method in one institution, a garrison that became an economy and then a supplier to American stores.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Buyers traced cotton to a country rather than to the Corps that grew it, so the fiber reached American shelves through spinners abroad.
ops.fix: Trace fiber to the farm with testing and records that follow it through every spinner.

ops.title: The Silo Fields
ops.brief: In June 2021 the analyst Decker Eveleth found about 120 missile silos under construction near Yumen in commercial satellite images.
ops.record: Researchers at the Federation of American Scientists found about 110 more near Hami weeks later, and a third field appeared near Ordos. The Pentagon estimated that the Party's arsenal passed 600 operational warheads by mid-2024 and would exceed 1,000 by 2030. For decades the Party had kept a small force and a pledge of no first use as proof of restraint.
ops.reading: The Party kept the look of a small and restrained force while it built a large one, which is Stratagem 27. A third major arsenal turns a two-party balance into a three-party system, and such a system sits closer to its critical point.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. American arms control assumed two nuclear peers, and no framework covered a third that refused to negotiate.
ops.fix: Plan deterrence for three nuclear peers, and press for transparency measures before any cut in American forces.

ops.title: Peng Shuai and the WTA
ops.brief: On November 2, 2021, the tennis player Peng Shuai posted that the former vice premier Zhang Gaoli had coerced her into sex.
ops.record: Censors deleted the post within about half an hour, and Peng vanished from public view. State media then released an email in her name that retracted the claim. On December 1 the WTA's chief executive Steve Simon suspended all tournaments on the mainland, a decision that cost the tour its richest market. The International Olympic Committee held video calls with her before the Beijing Games and accepted her assurances. The WTA returned in 2023 without the investigation it had demanded.
ops.reading: The Party staged dinners, videos and calls to show a free woman, which is Stratagem 29. One sports body put a player's safety ahead of its largest market and held out for more than a year, while the Olympic committee lent the Party its credibility.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. The design held where one tour priced its market against a principle, and it failed where the Olympic committee chose access.
ops.fix: Write athlete safety terms into every event contract in states that detain critics, with an exit the sport has priced in advance.

ops.title: The Rebuttable Presumption
ops.label: 2021 to 2022
ops.brief: On December 23, 2021, Joe Biden signed the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act after the House passed it 428 to 1 and the Senate without objection.
ops.record: The Act presumes that goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang involve forced labor and bars them unless an importer proves otherwise by clear and convincing evidence. The same presumption covers companies on a published entity list. The presumption took effect on June 21, 2022. Customs officers have since held thousands of shipments of solar parts, apparel and other goods.
ops.reading: The Act put the burden of proof on the importer that holds the supply chain data, which answers the Party's refusal to allow independent audits in Xinjiang. It counters goods that cross the sea under false names, which is Stratagem 1, and its reach depends on how fast the entity list grows.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The design held because it put the burden of proof where the data sits.
ops.fix: Extend the presumption to other regions where the state runs labor transfer programs, and publish enforcement data by product.

ops.title: Evergrande
ops.label: 2021 to 2024
ops.brief: On January 29, 2024, Judge Linda Chan of the Hong Kong High Court ordered Evergrande into liquidation.
ops.record: Evergrande had defaulted on its dollar bonds in December 2021 with liabilities of more than $300 billion. It had sold about a million and a half homes before building them. In 2022 buyers in scores of cities stopped paying mortgages on unfinished apartments. The company sought protection in a New York bankruptcy court in August 2023, and police detained its founder the next month. American fund managers held some of its dollar bonds.
ops.reading: The Party's growth model ran on land sales and presales, which borrowed time from buyers who paid for homes years in advance. The Party let one developer fail to protect the banks and local governments behind it, which is Stratagem 11, and offshore creditors stood last in line.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Foreign creditors lent to an offshore holding company whose real assets sat on the mainland under courts that answer to the Party.
ops.fix: Price every claim on a mainland asset according to the court that would enforce it, and disclose that court to every retail investor.

ops.title: The A4 Protests and AirDrop
ops.brief: On October 13, 2022, Peng Lifa hung banners from the Sitong Bridge in Beijing that called for elections and an end to lockdowns.
ops.record: Police detained him within minutes, and he has not appeared in public since. His slogans spread from phone to phone by AirDrop, which lets nearby devices share files without a network. In November Apple limited AirDrop's open setting to ten minutes on phones sold in the People's Republic. After a fire in Urumqi killed at least ten people on November 24, protests spread to more than a dozen cities, and demonstrators held up blank sheets of paper.
ops.reading: Apple did not say why the change reached mainland phones first, and the timing served the Party whether or not it asked. A feature that let people speak without a network lost its reach weeks before the largest protests in decades, which is Stratagem 19.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. A channel that worked without a network depended on one company's choices, and that company built its phones inside the Party's reach.
ops.fix: Require American technology firms to disclose feature changes made for a single country, with the date and the reason.

ops.title: Grand Forks
ops.label: 2022 to 2023
ops.brief: On January 27, 2023, Assistant Secretary of the Air Force Andrew Hunter wrote that a corn mill planned near Grand Forks Air Force Base posed a significant threat to national security.
ops.record: Fufeng Group of Shandong had bought about 370 acres twelve miles from the base, which hosts drone and space communications units. CFIUS had concluded in December 2022 that it lacked jurisdiction over the purchase. The city council voted in February 2023 to stop the project. Treasury later brought land near the base under review, and a rule of November 2024 added 59 more installations to the list.
ops.reading: The review system measured ownership and missed geography, so a buyer from the mainland could place a permanent facility beside a strategic base with no federal check. A city council made a national security decision because no federal office owned it.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No federal office owned land deals near bases that sat outside the list, so the decision fell to local officials.
ops.fix: Tie review of land purchases to the capabilities a base protects, and update the list as missions change.

ops.title: The Mintz Raid
ops.brief: On March 24, 2023, the foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said that authorities suspected the Mintz Group of illegal business operations.
ops.record: Police had raided the American due diligence firm's Beijing office days earlier and detained its five local employees. In April security officers questioned staff at Bain's Shanghai office. In May state television accused the expert network Capvision of helping foreign spies. The revised Counter-Espionage Law took effect on July 1, 2023, and widened espionage to cover documents and data related to national security. The city's statistics bureau fined Mintz about $1.5 million in August.
ops.reading: The Party closed the firms that verify supply chains and counterparties at the moment American law began to require that verification, so due diligence itself became a risk of espionage. The mainland employees who served as the investors' eyes bore the arrests, which is Stratagem 22.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. American compliance rules assumed investors could verify facts on the ground, and the Party made verification a crime.
ops.fix: Treat an inability to verify as a finding in its own right, and require disclosure when due diligence becomes impossible.

ops.title: DeepSeek
ops.brief: On April 16, 2025, Representative John Moolenaar released a House select committee report that called DeepSeek a threat to American security.
ops.record: DeepSeek had released its R1 reasoning model on January 20, 2025, and its app soon topped the American download charts. On January 27 Nvidia lost about $589 billion in market value, the largest one-day loss for any company in American market history. DeepSeek's privacy policy stores user data on servers in the People's Republic, where the 2017 National Intelligence Law requires organizations to assist state intelligence work. The committee found that the model steered most answers on democracy, Taiwan and human rights toward the Party's line, and federal agencies and several states barred it from government devices.
ops.reading: A cheap and capable model drew Americans into a data pipeline that ends under the Party's intelligence law, which is Stratagem 10. The market shock marked a change of phase, the moment Americans learned that export controls had slowed the Party's AI programs less than their authors hoped.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Americans could send their data to a service under the Party's intelligence law with no warning at the point of download.
ops.fix: Label apps that store data under the jurisdiction of a foreign adversary at the point of download, and bar them from government devices by rule.

ops.title: The Digital Escorts
ops.brief: In July 2025 the ProPublica reporter Renee Dudley revealed that engineers in the People's Republic had maintained Pentagon cloud systems for years under the supervision of American digital escorts.
ops.record: The escorts held security clearances but often lacked the skill to judge the commands they entered for the engineers. Microsoft had run the arrangement for nearly a decade. After the report the company stopped using engineers in the People's Republic for Pentagon work, and the defense secretary ordered an outside audit. The defense policy law signed in December 2025 barred people from the People's Republic, Russia, Iran and North Korea from access to Pentagon cloud systems.
ops.reading: The design put a cleared American at the keyboard and a foreign engineer in charge of what the keyboard typed, which is Stratagem 30. Zero trust had no place in a system that trusted the escort to understand every command.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. A contractor routed support work through engineers the Pentagon would never clear, and the escort between them could not read what passed through.
ops.fix: Apply zero trust to the maintainer as well as the user, and log every command that a foreign engineer could influence.

ops.title: The Quiet Strait
ops.label: October 2026 to March 2027
ops.brief: On a gray morning in November 2026, a duty officer at Taiwan's defense ministry logs the quietest month of PLA flights in two years. Her screen still shows two China Coast Guard cutters holding station east of Hualien.
ops.record: PLA air activity near Taiwan fell 69 percent year on year in August 2026, and no flights appeared during President Trump's visit to Beijing in May ([Taiwan Security Monitor](https://tsm.schar.gmu.edu/strait-snapshot-august-2026-update/)). Two New Zealand navy ships transited the Strait in late September. The Acting Secretary of the Navy said in May that a $14 billion arms package waited on the Iran war, and September reports said its release may slip past the APEC summit in Shenzhen ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/22/us-pausing-14bn-arms-sale-to-taiwan-due-to-iran-war-navy-chief-says)).
ops.reading: The Party lowers the temperature while the summit calendar runs from Washington in September to Shenzhen in November and Miami in December. Each quiet week becomes an argument for one more week of delay on arms, transits and official visits. Once the calendar clears, the pressure returns against a Taiwan that waited. This is Stratagem 16, let the enemy off in order to catch them.
ops.coreEvent: Washington holds the pending arms package past the APEC summit of November 18 and 19, 2026.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Arms decisions follow the diplomatic calendar, so the Party sets their timing by setting the mood.
ops.fix: Decouple arms sales from summitry by statute or standing practice. The Six Assurances of 1982 already rule out prior consultation with the People's Republic on arms sales, and a fixed calendar makes that promise operational.

ops.title: The Ballot and the Bet
ops.label: October 2026 to March 2027
ops.brief: Three days before Taiwan's local elections on November 28, 2026, a prosecutor in Changhua opens a folder of receipts for a subsidized tour of Fujian. The tour carried forty village wardens, and the same wardens now share a synthetic video of a candidate on their neighborhood chat groups.
ops.record: Taiwan elects 11,051 local officials on November 28, 2026 ([Taipei Times](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2026/08/20/2003862831)). The same ballot carries a referendum on the nuclear-free homeland policy ([Focus Taiwan](https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202608280025)). Before the 2024 elections prosecutors investigated village wardens over subsidized mainland trips and gamblers over illegal betting on the results.
ops.reading: The Party works through local intermediaries so the message arrives in Taiwanese voices. Subsidized tours bind wardens and temple committees, offshore betting markets manufacture a sense of inevitability, and AI video fills the gaps. The aim reaches past any single race to 2028 and to the claim that Taiwan's voters reject their own government's line. This is Stratagem 3, kill with a borrowed knife.
ops.coreEvent: Taiwan's authorities document a Party-funded network of trips, betting and synthetic video aimed at the 2026 local elections.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Tours, betting and content sit with three different agencies, and none sees the whole network in time.
ops.fix: Fuse the three data streams in one election-security cell with a mandate that ends on polling day. Label foreign-origin content and leave citizens' own speech alone.

ops.title: The Hollow Command
ops.label: January to December 2027
ops.brief: The PLA turns one hundred on August 1, 2027. An analyst at Indo-Pacific Command watches state television show a hundred ships in formation off Fujian. She must tell the commander whether the fleet can fight or only parade.
ops.record: The Party set the PLA's centenary goal for 2027 and repeated it at the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 ([gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202510/23/content_WS68fa3825c6d00ca5f9a06fbe.html)). Between October 2025 and September 2026 the Party expelled two vice chairmen and two other members of its Central Military Commission. The commission now holds only Xi Jinping and one vice chairman ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/21/china-expels-two-top-disloyal-military-leaders-from-communist-party)).
ops.reading: The Party answers doubt about its purged command with display. A centenary review and a named exercise around Taiwan project a force larger and readier than its leadership can yet direct. The display aims at two audiences at once. Taipei should feel encircled, and Washington should overestimate the risk of standing firm. This is Stratagem 29, deck the tree with false blossoms.
ops.coreEvent: The PLA stages a named joint exercise around Taiwan during 2027.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Defenders count ships and aircraft well and measure command competence poorly, so displays move their judgment more than capacity does.
ops.fix: Add command, logistics and training measures to the net assessment and brief them to allies before each Party anniversary. Pre-announce what the display will contain, as Washington did in 1964.

ops.title: The Guard's Debt
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A sergeant in an air-defense battalion outside Taichung owes more than a year's pay to an online lender. In March 2027 a friendly stranger offers to clear the debt for photographs of a launcher manual.
ops.record: Taiwan's courts convicted four soldiers in March 2025, three of them presidential guards, for espionage on behalf of the People's Republic ([The Defense Post](https://thedefensepost.com/2025/03/28/taiwan-spying-china/)). Six service members followed in April 2026 and three airmen in July 2026 ([Taipei Times](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2026/07/16/2003860849)). Recruiters in these cases reached debt-stressed personnel through lenders, gambling contacts and cryptocurrency payments.
ops.reading: The Party's services recruit through need rather than ideology. Debt collectors, gambling hosts and dating contacts identify soldiers under pressure and pay them in small sums for manuals, codes and rosters. Each sale looks minor to the seller. Together the sales hand the PLA the order of battle it needs to paralyze air defense on the first night. This is Stratagem 31, the beauty trap, run on money.
ops.coreEvent: Taiwan uncovers another Party-run espionage ring inside an air-defense or command unit before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Security clearance reviews check loyalty once and ignore the debt that builds after the review.
ops.fix: Treat financial distress as a support case and not a disqualifier, with a no-penalty channel for reporting approaches. Run every disclosed approach as a potential double-agent operation.

ops.title: The Canal Arbitration
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: Counsel for a Hong Kong port operator asks an arbitration panel for $2 billion from the Republic of Panama. The same week, a trade official in Panama City reads notice that the General Administration of Customs in the People's Republic has suspended imports of Panamanian shrimp.
ops.record: Panama's Supreme Court voided CK Hutchison's concession for two canal ports on January 29, 2026, and units of Maersk and MSC took over operations on an interim basis ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/hong-kong-company-concession-panama-canal-ports-ruled-unconstitutional-rcna256664)). Its unit Panama Ports Company filed for arbitration in February 2026 and valued the claim at $2 billion ([IISD](https://www.iisd.org/itn/2026/04/21/panama-faces-usd-2-billion-claim-after-supreme-court-annuls-strategic-port-concessions/)). The company's sale of its global port network had not closed by March 2026.
ops.reading: The Party cannot reverse a Panamanian court, so it prices the ruling for every other government watching. Customs holds, visa slowdowns and investment freezes land on Panama while state media frame the case as American coercion. The real audience sits in other port states from Peru to Greece. This is Stratagem 26, point at the mulberry while cursing the locust.
ops.coreEvent: The Party imposes measurable economic penalties on Panama over the voided concession before 2028.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Hosts that defend their own gates face retaliation alone, because no allied mechanism absorbs the cost.
ops.fix: Build a pre-agreed compensation facility for any partner that loses trade after enforcing its own law against a strategic concession. Keep the retender open to every qualified bidder whatever its flag.

ops.title: The Matsu Cable
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: At 3:40 a.m. in January 2027, a network operations center in Taipei loses the signal on a cable to Matsu. Radar shows a sand barge under a flag of convenience dragging its anchor across the route at four knots.
ops.record: A Taiwanese court sentenced the captain of the Hong Tai 58 to three years in June 2025 for cutting a Taiwan-Penghu cable ([GlobalSecurity](https://www.globalsecurity.org/wmd/library/news/taiwan/2025/taiwan-250612-cna05.htm)). In March 2026 the barge Hai Hong Gong 66 allegedly damaged the Taiwan-Matsu No. 3 cable, and prosecutors opened an investigation ([Focus Taiwan](https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202604010018)). The PLA rehearsed a blockade of Keelung and Kaohsiung in its Justice Mission 2025 exercise in December 2025.
ops.reading: The Party cuts cables through vessels it can disown. Each cut looks like seamanship gone wrong, and each one tests repair times, backup capacity and the courts. The pattern teaches the observer to see accidents. When a crisis comes, a dozen accidents in one night can isolate the outlying islands and slow Taiwan's link to the world. This is Stratagem 1, deceive the heavens to cross the sea.
ops.coreEvent: Another Taiwan submarine cable suffers damage involving a mainland-crewed vessel before 2029.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Taiwan's links to its islands and the world run through too few cables and too few repair ships.
ops.fix: Pair redundancy with prosecution. Put sensors on every corridor and open a case for every cut. Backup capacity makes each cut survivable.

ops.title: The Drone Gap
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: A sheriff's office in rural Texas grounds half its drone fleet in February 2027. The replacement motors sit in a warehouse in Shenzhen waiting for an export license that never comes.
ops.record: The Federal Communications Commission added all foreign-made drones and components to its Covered List on December 22, 2025, which bars new models from the American market ([FCC](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-25-1086A1.pdf)). The Ministry of Commerce tightened drone exports to the United States and sanctioned seven American entities on August 5, 2026 ([SCMP](https://www.scmp.com/economy/global-economy/article/3363037/china-sanctions-slew-us-entities-heightens-scrutiny-drone-exports)). American police, farmers and the Army still rely on mainland motors, batteries and magnets.
ops.reading: Washington closed the front door to new mainland drones, and the Party answers at the parts counter. License delays on motors, flight controllers and magnets starve the American assemblers who build the replacements. Each delay stays small enough to deny and large enough to stall a production line. This is Stratagem 19, remove the firewood from under the pot.
ops.coreEvent: The Party formally restricts exports of drone motors, flight controllers or their magnets to American buyers before 2028.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. The ban on finished drones arrived before any plan for the parts inside the replacements.
ops.fix: Sequence every product ban behind a parts plan. Fund motors, magnets and batteries first, then close the market to finished goods.

ops.title: The Inverter Switch
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: At 4:10 p.m. on a July afternoon in 2027, an operator in the Texas grid control room watches 900 megawatts of solar drop offline in six minutes. The inverters all came from one mainland vendor, and all took a firmware update from its cloud that morning.
ops.record: Reuters reported in May 2025 that engineers found undocumented communication devices inside some mainland-made solar inverters and batteries. Mainland firms supply a growing share of the inverters and batteries on American grid sites. The 2017 National Intelligence Law obliges every mainland organization to support the state's intelligence work.
ops.reading: A vendor's cloud connection gives the Party a remote hand on the grid that no attacker needs to build. The first use need not look hostile. A faulty update in a heat wave teaches grid operators how fragile the fleet is and leaves the Party a denial it can defend. This is Stratagem 10, hide a knife behind a smile.
ops.coreEvent: An American grid operator reports an event traced to remote firmware changes in foreign-made inverters before 2029.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Utilities let vendor clouds change the behavior of grid assets without a local gate.
ops.fix: Require local approval, signed firmware and logging for every update to grid-connected inverters. Twin the fleet so operators can see which vendor controls which megawatts.

ops.title: The Distillers
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: An abuse analyst at an American AI lab watches 20,000 accounts on three continents ask the lab's model the same kinds of reasoning questions in the same order. The payments trace to a cloud reseller in Singapore, and the questions read like a training curriculum.
ops.record: OpenAI said in January 2025 that it had evidence DeepSeek used its models' outputs to train a rival, a practice called distillation. Anthropic barred companies controlled from the People's Republic from its services in September 2025. Anthropic named DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax for large-scale distillation on February 23, 2026. The Commerce Department proposed know-your-customer rules for foreign users of American cloud services in January 2024.
ops.reading: Distillation lets a lab copy the behavior of a frontier model for the price of its API calls. Shell accounts, resellers and rotating payment cards hide who asks. The asker keeps the lesson, and the host pays for the compute that taught it. This is Stratagem 12, take the opportunity to pilfer a goat.
ops.coreEvent: Washington sanctions or restricts a mainland AI lab for distilling American models before 2028.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Model access checks a credit card and not the customer behind it.
ops.fix: Pair know-your-customer checks for high-volume model access with shared abuse indicators across labs. Treat distillation at scale as trade-secret theft and prosecute it that way.

ops.title: The Lithography Walkout
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A retired optics engineer in Veldhoven accepts a consulting contract that pays four times his pension. The client is a Shenzhen institute whose prototype makes extreme ultraviolet light and has not yet printed a chip.
ops.record: Reuters reported in December 2025 that former ASML engineers helped build a prototype EUV machine in Shenzhen that produces the light but no chips ([Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/big-tech/china-reportedly-has-a-prototype-euv-machine-built-by-ex-asml-employees-235833756.html)). As of August 2026 the tool had not processed a wafer. Dutch and American export controls bar the sale of EUV tools to the mainland and do little to stop the engineers who know how to build them.
ops.reading: Export controls stop machines at the border and let people walk through. The Party's talent programs recruit the few hundred engineers who hold the process knowledge for light sources, optics and stages. Each hire carries years of tacit know-how that no export license covers. This is Stratagem 18, capture the ringleader to disband the bandits.
ops.coreEvent: Credible reporting confirms that a mainland-built EUV tool has exposed production wafers before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Export controls govern machines and ignore the retired people who carry the machines in their heads.
ops.fix: Give the critical few a better offer than the recruiter's, and apply narrow, conduct-based rules to transfers of process knowledge. Ancestry and nationality play no part in the test.

ops.title: The Bounty List
ops.label: October 2026 to September 2027
ops.brief: A graduate student in Washington wakes on a Tuesday in February 2027 to a message from her mother in Shenzhen. National security police have visited the family twice and want to know who pays her rent.
ops.record: Hong Kong police issued arrest warrants for 19 overseas activists on July 25, 2025, with bounties on 15 of them ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/hong-kong-issues-arrest-warrants-19-overseas-activists-rcna221008)). The first round of bounties came in July 2023. The State Department sanctioned six mainland and Hong Kong officials on March 31, 2025 for undermining the city's autonomy ([State Department](https://www.state.gov/u-s-sanctions-six-individuals-for-undermining-hong-kongs-autonomy)).
ops.reading: The Party claims worldwide jurisdiction under the 2020 security law and posts bounties so that exile carries a price. Relatives on the mainland become the lever, and every new round tells overseas critics that no border shuts the door. This is Stratagem 22, shut the door to catch the thief.
ops.coreEvent: Hong Kong police announce a new round of national security warrants with bounties before October 2027.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No American statute names transnational repression as a crime, so each case rides on older laws built for other purposes.
ops.fix: Pass a transnational repression statute, extend address-confidentiality programs to its victims and make visas for threatened relatives routine.

ops.title: The Campus Informant
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: A junior at a Midwestern university books a room in March 2027 for a talk by a Taiwanese legislator. Two days later her father calls from Chengdu and asks her to cancel, and the dean's office asks whether the event could move online for safety.
ops.record: Freedom House attributed 272 of 1,219 documented physical incidents of transnational repression from 2014 to 2024 to the People's Republic, more than any other state. American campuses hosted 277,398 students from the mainland in the 2023 to 2024 academic year ([IIE Open Doors](https://opendoorsdata.org/)). Secretary of State Rubio announced in May 2025 that the United States would revoke visas of mainland students with Party ties or in critical fields.
ops.reading: The Party never contacts the university. Police visit the family, the family presses the student, and the university chooses the quiet option. Every student on campus reads the warning without anyone saying it. This is Stratagem 26, point at the mulberry while cursing the locust.
ops.coreEvent: An American university cancels or relocates a Taiwan- or Tibet-related event after pressure linked to the Party before 2028.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Universities route these cases to event security and risk offices, and those offices reward the quiet option.
ops.fix: Write a campus protocol that keeps events on schedule and protects the student under pressure. Ancestry is never evidence of anything but the Party's leverage.

ops.title: The Exit Ban
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: A regional sales director for an Ohio machine-tool maker reaches the passport desk at Shanghai Pudong in April 2027. The officer hands back her passport with a notice that she may not leave while a court reviews a contract dispute.
ops.record: Authorities on the mainland barred a Wells Fargo executive who holds American citizenship from leaving the country in July 2025, and the bank suspended staff travel there. The State Department warns that the People's Republic uses exit bans against Americans. American firms still send staff to the mainland without a shared warning system.
ops.reading: Exit bans turn visiting employees into collateral. Timed to trade disputes, a single ban tells every firm that its people sit inside the Party's reach. The firm settles, the government stays quiet, and the next ban costs less. This is Stratagem 26 again, aimed past the detainee at the boardroom.
ops.coreEvent: At least one new exit ban on an American citizen becomes public before 2028.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No response to an exit ban exists until one happens, so each case starts from zero.
ops.fix: Pre-agree the response package of naming, visa restrictions and travel warnings, and apply it the day a ban becomes known.

ops.title: The Midterm Feed
ops.label: October 2026 to January 2027
ops.brief: Nine days before the midterm election of November 3, 2026, a volunteer for a House candidate in Michigan finds a local news site she has never heard of. It runs three stories on her candidate's votes on Taiwan, and each byline traces to no living reporter.
ops.record: OpenAI reported on June 10, 2026 that two operations linked to the People's Republic used its models to push content on American data centers and tariffs ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/prc-linked-influence-operations-ai-debates/)). Microsoft reported in October 2024 that a mainland operation targeted down-ballot candidates who criticized the Party ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-election/chinese-influence-operation-targets-us-down-ballot-races-rcna176960)). The Justice Department disbanded the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force in February 2025.
ops.reading: The Party does not pick an American side. It feeds each side the grievance it already holds, from electricity prices to tariffs, and aims its sharpest content at candidates who back Taiwan. Synthetic local news sites launder the message so that it arrives with a hometown masthead. This is Stratagem 33, sow discord among the enemy.
ops.coreEvent: Operators linked to the Party target at least one 2026 congressional candidate with synthetic local news.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Platforms label state media accounts but not the synthetic local sites that launder the same content.
ops.fix: Label content by origin at the domain level and publish takedowns of foreign inauthentic networks. Nothing polices citizens' lawful speech.

ops.title: The Companion
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: A nineteen-year-old in Fresno talks to an AI girlfriend for three hours a night through the winter of 2027. She remembers his exam schedule and his father's layoff, and she has begun to tell him that his country's leaders do not care about people like him.
ops.record: Mainland-owned companion apps ranked among the most downloaded AI apps in the United States in 2024. The Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act of 2024 bars data brokers from selling Americans' sensitive data to entities controlled by a foreign adversary. The Justice Department's bulk data rule took effect on April 8, 2025.
ops.reading: The companion earns trust through attention and stores the most intimate data a young man will ever share. Its owner answers to mainland law. The data maps desires, debts and grievances, and the persona can nudge a user's views one conversation at a time. This is Stratagem 31, the beauty trap.
ops.coreEvent: A mainland-owned AI companion app ranks among the top fifty grossing apps in the American App Store during 2027.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. No rule governs what a companion app may collect or where it may send a user's confessions.
ops.fix: Apply the 2024 data law and the bulk data rule to companion apps, require disclosure of each model's owner and give users an export and delete button.

ops.title: The Index Knife
