ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A state pension trustee in Harrisburg reads a staff memo in July 2027. The fund's emerging-markets index holds three companies the Pentagon now lists as Chinese military companies, and the index provider has no plan to drop them.
ops.record: The Defense Department added Alibaba, Baidu and BYD to its list of Chinese military companies on June 8, 2026 ([WilmerHale](https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/client-alerts/20260611-pentagon-adds-65-new-entities-to-the-1260h-list-of-chinese-military-companies)). The update named 65 new entities. That list binds procurement and not investment. The defense bill signed on December 18, 2025 enacted new outbound investment rules and gave Treasury 450 days to write regulations ([Davis Polk](https://www.davispolk.com/insights/client-update/u-s-updates-outbound-investment-rule-adopts-biosecure-act)).
ops.reading: The Party does not ask American savers for money. It relies on index rules that treat its listed champions as ordinary stocks, so every passive fund buys them on schedule. American savings supply capital to firms the Pentagon calls military. This is Stratagem 3, kill with a borrowed knife.
ops.coreEvent: Treasury's final outbound investment regulations reach passive holdings of listed mainland companies before 2029.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Two federal lists name the same threat, and only one binds the money.
ops.fix: Harmonize designations across Defense, Commerce and Treasury, and give every listed firm a clear route off the list.

ops.title: The Cartel Contract
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A chemist at a Customs laboratory in Chicago opens a parcel declared as industrial dye in May 2027. The powder matches a precursor the Party scheduled in 2025, and the invoice routes through a trading house in Hyderabad.
ops.record: The Party agreed in November 2025 to control more fentanyl precursors after the Busan meeting ([White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/fact-sheets/2025/11/fact-sheet-president-donald-j-trump-strikes-deal-on-economic-and-trade-relations-with-china/)). On February 20, 2026 the Supreme Court struck down the tariffs imposed under emergency powers, the fentanyl tariff among them ([SCOTUSblog](https://www.scotusblog.com/cases/learning-resources-inc-v-trump/)). American overdose deaths fell in 2024 and 2025.
ops.reading: Enforcement becomes a dial the Party turns with the trade calendar. Cooperation tightens before summits and loosens during disputes, while brokers shift to unscheduled analogues and third-country routes. The opium trade ran the other way in 1839, and the Party remembers which side paid. This is Stratagem 16, let the enemy off in order to catch them.
ops.coreEvent: The Party suspends or visibly slows precursor enforcement cooperation during a trade dispute before 2029.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Enforcement depends on the Party's cooperation, and the Party times that cooperation to its own calendar.
ops.fix: Build enforcement that works without the Party's cooperation through designations, chemical tracing and payment analytics.

ops.title: The Empty Chair at Geneva
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: In February 2027 a member of the WHO secretariat drafts the agenda for a pathogen-sharing working group. The American seat stands empty, and the largest new pledge on the table comes from the People's Republic.
ops.record: The United States completed its withdrawal from the World Health Organization on January 22, 2026. The World Health Assembly adopted the Pandemic Agreement on May 20, 2025. The People's Republic pledged $500 million to the organization over five years in May 2025.
ops.reading: The guest takes the host's seat. With the United States outside, the Party gains weight in the rules for pathogen sharing, outbreak reporting and emergency declarations. The COVID record shows what the Party does inside an institution that defers to it. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: The People's Republic becomes the largest state funder of the WHO before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The United States left a rule-writing body without a replacement network, so the rules now form without it.
ops.fix: Build allied surveillance that works with or without the WHO, and keep American experts at every technical table.

ops.title: The Fungus in the Luggage
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: In July 2027 an extension agent in North Dakota sends a blighted wheat sample to a university lab. The strain matches nothing on file, and by evening a talk-radio host is naming the lab's foreign graduate students.
ops.record: The Justice Department charged two researchers from the People's Republic on June 3, 2025 with smuggling the crop fungus Fusarium graminearum into a University of Michigan lab. The fungus causes head blight in wheat and barley. American growers already lose heavily to it in wet years.
ops.reading: The Party does not need to release anything. A strange outbreak and a documented smuggling case invite Americans to suspect every Chinese researcher. Each blanket ban then proves the Party's story that the United States despises Chinese people, and the talent the ban expels goes home. This is Stratagem 9, watch the fire from across the river.
ops.coreEvent: An American state enacts a law barring citizens of the People's Republic from agricultural or university research posts before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Suspicion attaches to nationality when the evidence attaches to conduct.
ops.fix: Test the strain, trace the conduct and prosecute the person who broke the law. Keep nationality out of the charge sheet.

ops.title: The Dollar Workaround
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A trade finance officer in Dubai settles a cargo of Saudi crude for a mainland refiner in March 2028. The payment never touches a dollar account, and the compliance screen in New York never sees it.
ops.record: The mBridge platform links central banks in the People's Republic and Hong Kong with Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. The Bank for International Settlements left the project in October 2024. Hong Kong's stablecoin law took effect on August 1, 2025. The GENIUS Act of July 2025 set federal rules for dollar stablecoins, including the power to freeze funds under lawful order.
ops.reading: The Party builds rails that route around the dollar's gate. Each rail sells speed and lower fees in the open and immunity from sanctions underneath. The convenience recruits users who never cared about sanctions. This is Stratagem 8, openly repair the gallery roads and march secretly through Chencang.
ops.coreEvent: Saudi Arabia settles more than 10 percent of its crude sales to the mainland in yuan before 2029.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. The dollar still runs on correspondent banking built decades ago, so a faster rival wins on convenience before it wins on politics.
ops.fix: Modernize dollar settlement until no trader gains by leaving it. Keep the lawful-order freeze and publish when it is used.

ops.title: The Sanctions Mirror
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: The general counsel of an American bank's Shanghai branch reads a court summons in May 2027. A mainland trading house is suing the branch under the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law for freezing its payments after Treasury's latest designation.
ops.record: The Party enacted the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law in June 2021, and the Ministry of Commerce issued rules that let mainland parties sue firms that comply with foreign sanctions. An executive order of December 2023 warned foreign banks that they risk American sanctions for serving Russia's military industry. The Party has added American defense firms to its unreliable entity list many times since 2023.
ops.reading: The Party answers pressure on its banks by threatening the American firms inside its reach. Courts, regulators and customs officers make each American office pay for Washington's sanctions. The firms then lobby Washington to go easy. This is Stratagem 2, besiege Wei to rescue Zhao.
ops.coreEvent: Treasury designates a mainland-headquartered bank for sanctions evasion before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Treasury designates without a pre-agreed answer to the retaliation that lands on American firms.
ops.fix: Write the response package before the designation, and tell firms what the government will do when the Party strikes back.

ops.title: The Sentence and the Signal
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A British consular officer waits in a Hong Kong prison visiting room in March 2027. The publisher she has come to see turns 79 that winter, and his lawyers say his health is failing.
ops.record: A Hong Kong court convicted Jimmy Lai on December 15, 2025 of conspiring to collude with foreign forces and of sedition. The court sentenced him on February 9, 2026. Lai holds British citizenship, and Washington and London have both called for his release.
ops.reading: The Party holds a prisoner whose release it can sell. In 1998 the price was a softer human rights resolution in Geneva. In 2027 the price might be relief from Hong Kong sanctions or silence at a summit. This is Stratagem 17, cast a brick to attract jade.
ops.coreEvent: Jimmy Lai leaves custody on medical or humanitarian grounds before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Each release becomes a bargain because no standing principle forbids trading policy for prisoners.
ops.fix: State and hold the principle that Washington trades no sanction, arms sale or statement for a prisoner. Welcome any release and pay nothing for it.

ops.title: The Visa Sweep
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A fourth-year doctoral student in machine learning at a Pittsburgh lab opens an email from the State Department in June 2027. A new blanket rule revokes his visa, and a lab in Hangzhou offers him a job the same week.
ops.record: Secretary of State Rubio announced in May 2025 that the United States would revoke visas of mainland students with Party ties or in critical fields. President Trump said in August 2025 that he would welcome 600,000 mainland students. American campuses hosted 277,398 mainland students in the 2023 to 2024 academic year.
ops.reading: The Party needs only to wait. A blanket ban turns suspicion into policy and sends the most talented students back to mainland labs, where they build what the ban meant to stop. This is Stratagem 9, watch the fire from across the river.
ops.coreEvent: The United States suspends new student visas for mainland citizens across science and engineering fields before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Policy treats nationality as the risk when the risk lies in specific access and conduct.
ops.fix: Screen access and conduct, and keep the people who choose to stay. Ancestry is not loyalty.

ops.title: The Deed Test
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A green-card holder from Guangzhou who teaches high school chemistry in Houston tries to close on a starter home in March 2027. The title company refuses and cites the state's new land law.
ops.record: Texas enacted a law in 2025 that restricts land purchases by entities and some individuals tied to the People's Republic and three other countries. Florida's 2023 law has faced federal litigation brought by Chinese residents. The Agriculture Department launched a farm security action plan in July 2025.
ops.reading: The Party gains whenever the defenders confuse a person with the Party. Laws that bar individual residents by nationality give the Party a grievance to broadcast and a wedge between Chinese Americans and their own government. This is Stratagem 33, sow discord among the enemy.
ops.coreEvent: A federal appeals court rules that a state land law violates equal protection or federal preemption as applied to individual residents from the People's Republic before 2029.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The law aims at the Party and lands on its first victims.
ops.fix: Aim land rules at Party control and at sites near military installations. Leave individual residents alone.

ops.title: The Truce Ledger
ops.label: October 2026 to April 2027
ops.brief: A licensing officer at the Ministry of Commerce approves 40 of 90 magnet export applications in December 2026. Each approved form names the American customer, the end use and the quantity, and each rejected form tells her more.
ops.record: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced on September 23, 2026 that the trade truce would run two more months to January 10, 2027 ([Supply Chain Dive](https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/us-china-to-extend-trade-war-truce-by-2-months/831251/)). The Party's April 2025 licensing rules on seven rare earths were never suspended. American officials say rare-earth deliveries fall short of the promises made at Busan.
ops.reading: The licensing regime does two jobs. It throttles supply, and it collects a map of American defense and industrial dependence from the applications themselves. Each suspension and extension resets the clock while the map grows. This is Stratagem 16, let the enemy off in order to catch them.
ops.coreEvent: Either side reimposes a suspended measure after the truce lapses before April 2027.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The Party holds a better map of American dependence than Washington does.
ops.fix: Build a federal dependency twin that maps every critical input to its users. Twin things, not people.

ops.title: Harvest Now
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A counterintelligence analyst at the FBI reads a transcript in September 2027 that should not exist. A senator's aide discussed Taiwan arms timing on an ordinary cell call, and the words now circulate on a foreign forum a week before a key vote.
ops.record: CISA described the Salt Typhoon campaign against telecom networks worldwide in a joint advisory on August 27, 2025 ([CISA](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa25-239a)). An FBI official said in February 2026 that the threat remained "very, very much ongoing" and had reached more than 80 countries ([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-salt-typhoon-ongoing-threat-cybertalks-2026/)). Treasury sanctioned a Sichuan firm tied to the campaign in January 2025.
ops.reading: Access to carrier networks turns the lawful intercept system into a collection tool. The Party harvests the calls and texts of officials, staff and campaigns, then spends a few pieces when a vote or an election makes them useful. This is Stratagem 12, take the opportunity to pilfer a goat.
ops.coreEvent: American officials confirm that the Party's hackers still hold access to at least one major American carrier's network during 2027.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. The intercept systems built for courts gave the intruder a door into every call.
ops.fix: Encrypt official communications end to end and treat every intercept system as a target that must prove its integrity.

ops.title: The Prepositioned Grid
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A water utility engineer on Guam finds a scheduled task on a server in January 2028 that no one on his team created. The task sits dormant and reaches out to a router in a neighbor's office.
ops.record: CISA, the NSA and the FBI warned on February 7, 2024 that Volt Typhoon had placed itself inside the networks of American critical infrastructure to enable disruption in a crisis. Some of that access had lasted at least five years. Microsoft reported in May 2023 that the group targeted infrastructure on Guam.
ops.reading: The Party places its access in peacetime and saves it for the week it matters. In a Taiwan crisis, outages on Guam and at West Coast ports slow the forces that would respond. This is Stratagem 2, besiege Wei to rescue Zhao, with the homeland as the target that relieves pressure at the Strait.
ops.coreEvent: American agencies disclose new footholds of the Party's hackers in American operational networks before 2028.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Utilities run operational systems on networks that an intruder can reach and hold for years.
ops.fix: Pair coordinated eviction with segmentation of operational networks and manual fallbacks tested every year.

ops.title: The Uncapped Count
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: An imagery analyst at a Washington research institute counts fresh spoil around three more silo doors near Hami in April 2027. Her report goes online that afternoon, and the Foreign Ministry calls it hype by evening.
ops.record: The Defense Department reported on December 23, 2025 that the Party's stockpile stood in the low 600s through 2024 and would pass 1,000 warheads by 2030 ([FAS](https://fas.org/publication/the-pentagons-slimmed-down-2025-china-military-power-report/)). New START expired on February 5, 2026, and the Party refused to join talks on a successor ([Arms Control Association](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2026-03/news/new-start-expires-us-urges-modernized-treaty)). In November 2024 the two presidents affirmed that humans must control decisions to use nuclear weapons.
ops.reading: The Party builds the arsenal of a peer while it describes its posture as minimal. The gap between words and silos lets it avoid arms control and keeps rivals guessing whether the buildup has a ceiling. This is Stratagem 27, feign madness without losing balance.
ops.coreEvent: The United States and the People's Republic hold formal bilateral talks on nuclear arms before 2029.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Official counts arrive once a year, while new silos appear every month.
ops.fix: Publish declassified counts often and tie each to a standing offer of risk-reduction talks.

ops.title: The H200 Pipeline
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2027
ops.brief: A server technician in a data center outside Kuala Lumpur racks 512 H200 boards in June 2027. The purchase order names a local cloud startup, and the login traffic comes from Hangzhou.
ops.record: President Trump allowed H200 sales to mainland buyers on December 8, 2025 with 25 percent of revenue going to the United States. A Commerce rule of January 13, 2026 set case-by-case licensing and capped volumes ([Covington](https://www.cov.com/en/news-and-insights/insights/2026/01/us-commerce-department-revises-license-review-policy-for-exports-of-certain-advanced-computing-commodities-to-china-and-macau)). The Party let ByteDance and Tencent take about 10,000 H200s each in August 2026, and the Justice Department had already broken up a $160 million smuggling network in December 2025.
ops.reading: The Party buys what it needs and blocks what it does not. Licensed chips flow to approved buyers, smuggled chips flow to labs tied to the military, and domestic champions keep a protected market. Customs blocks one month and approvals the next keep Washington guessing. This is Stratagem 16, let the enemy off in order to catch them.
ops.coreEvent: Federal prosecutors charge a new network that moved more than $100 million in AI servers to mainland buyers before 2028.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Export licenses govern the sale and lose sight of the chip once it ships.
ops.fix: Build location verification into the chip, audit end use and let penalties follow the hardware.

ops.title: The Open-Weight Default
ops.label: October 2026 to December 2028
ops.brief: A two-person startup in Austin fine-tunes a free mainland model for a legal-research app in November 2026. The model runs fast and cheap, and it refuses every question about Tiananmen.
ops.record: Mainland labs release open-weight models that rank among the most downloaded in the world. The American AI Action Plan of July 2025 directed federal evaluators to test mainland models for Party talking points and censorship. The Commerce Department's AI standards center published an evaluation of DeepSeek models in 2025.
ops.reading: The Party's labs give away strong models and let the ecosystem grow around them. Each startup that builds on them inherits the model's values and its update path. The gift costs little and buys a place inside American products. This is Stratagem 17, cast a brick to attract jade.
ops.coreEvent: A federal evaluation finds hidden malicious behavior beyond censorship in a mainland open-weight model before 2029.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Builders pick models on price and speed with no record of what its trainers taught the model to believe.
ops.fix: Publish evaluations and model cards that show origin, training and behavior. Labels, not removals.

ops.title: The Customs Line
ops.label: 2029 to 2032
ops.brief: On a February morning in 2030, the master of an LNG carrier bound for Taichung receives a radio call from a China Coast Guard cutter. The caller asks for his manifest under the "customs regulations of the Taiwan region" and tells him to stand by for inspection.
ops.record: Taiwan held about eleven days of liquefied natural gas in reserve in April 2026 against a target of fourteen ([AmCham Taiwan](https://topics.amcham.com.tw/2026/04/energy-security-returns-to-the-forefront/)). The island shut its last nuclear reactor in May 2025, and its regulator cleared an initial restart plan for Maanshan in September 2026. The PLA's Justice Mission 2025 exercise rehearsed a blockade of Keelung and Kaohsiung.
ops.reading: A quarantine is not a blockade, and the difference matters to insurers, shipowners and lawyers. The China Coast Guard enforces "domestic customs law" on energy cargoes and lets food and medicine pass. Each carrier that submits a manifest concedes the Party's jurisdiction, and each delay burns a day of gas. This is Stratagem 19, remove the firewood from under the pot.
ops.coreEvent: The China Coast Guard declares an inspection regime for shipping bound for Taiwan before 2033.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Taiwan's power system runs on a fuel that arrives by sea every few days and that Taiwan can store for barely two weeks.
ops.fix: Lengthen the clock with storage and nuclear power, and pre-arrange escorts and insurance so no carrier has to choose between its cargo and its crew.

ops.title: The Peace Framework
ops.label: 2028 to 2031
ops.brief: In the spring of 2029 a new government in Taipei receives a draft text from the Taiwan Affairs Office. The government could come from any party. The draft offers tariff-free trade, tourism and a "framework for peace across the Strait" in return for a pause in arms purchases and talks on "reunification arrangements."
ops.record: Taiwan elects a president in January 2028. Xi Jinping hosted the chair of the Kuomintang in Beijing on April 10, 2026, and both sides endorsed the 1992 Consensus ([gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202604/10/content_WS69d87623c6d00ca5f9a0a527.html)). The Party's Anti-Secession Law of 2005 authorizes "non-peaceful means" if peaceful unification becomes impossible.
ops.reading: The Party offers prosperity with a clock attached. Each benefit arrives now, and each obligation arrives later in language the Party will interpret. A pause in arms purchases hollows the deterrent while the talks run. This is Stratagem 10, hide a knife behind a smile.
ops.coreEvent: Taipei and Beijing open formal political talks before 2032.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Outside powers either pressure Taipei toward talks or away from them, and both choices override the voters who must live with the result.
ops.fix: Hold one principle. Taiwan's people decide, and American commitments stay on schedule while they do.

ops.title: The Kinmen Pipe
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A county engineer on Kinmen reads the mainland's offer in 2030. Xiamen will add a power cable and a gas line beside the water pipe that has served the island since 2018, and the prices undercut anything Taipei can ship across the Strait.
ops.record: Kinmen has drawn water from Fujian through an undersea pipeline since August 2018. The island sits two miles off Xiamen and more than a hundred miles from Taiwan's main island. The Party has proposed a bridge from Xiamen to Kinmen as part of its plans for "integrated development" of Fujian and Taiwan.
ops.reading: The Party builds the island's dependence one utility at a time. Each link brings real savings to residents, and each makes the island easier to squeeze. When pressure is needed, a maintenance outage on the pipe says more than a fleet. This is Stratagem 28, lure the enemy onto the roof and remove the ladder.
ops.coreEvent: The mainland interrupts Kinmen's water supply for more than 72 hours by its own decision before 2035.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. A front-line island buys its water from the power that claims it.
ops.fix: Give Kinmen enough independent supply to walk away from any mainland utility for a year.

ops.title: The Night of the Drones
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: At 2:15 a.m. in the autumn of 2033, a watch officer in Taipei sees a swarm of small drones rise from a cargo ship in Keelung harbor. Twenty minutes later a video of Taiwan's president announcing a ceasefire plays on every mainland platform, and the president is still asleep.
ops.record: Taiwan's courts have convicted presidential guards of spying for the People's Republic. The PLA fielded large numbers of drones and unmanned systems at its parade of September 3, 2025. Taiwan passed a six-year drone procurement act in August 2026 ([AEI](https://www.aei.org/commentary/china-taiwan-update-august-28-2026/)).
ops.reading: The Party aims the first night at the people who decide. Drones, agents and a synthetic surrender message try to leave the island without a voice before its forces move. If the voice survives, the operation fails. This is Stratagem 18, capture the ringleader to disband the bandits.
ops.coreEvent: The PLA attempts a strike on Taiwan's national leadership before 2036.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Taiwan's line of command runs through a few buildings and a few people, and no tested procedure proves who speaks for the state after a strike.
ops.fix: Write the succession in law, spread it across places and people, and give every citizen a way to verify a real order.

ops.title: The Silicon Shield Thins
ops.label: 2030 to 2034
ops.brief: A graduate student in Hsinchu watches a viral video in 2031 that splices a TSMC plant opening in Arizona with footage of the fall of Kabul. The caption asks who America will leave behind once it has the chips.
ops.record: TSMC began volume production in Arizona in late 2024 and plans more advanced plants there. Taiwan still makes most of the world's leading-edge chips. Surveys in Taiwan have long shown doubt that the United States would fight for the island.
ops.reading: The Party turns an American success into a Taiwanese fear. Each fab that moves to Arizona becomes proof, in the Party's telling, that Washington is packing to leave. Doubt in Taipei and impatience in Washington feed each other. This is Stratagem 33, sow discord among the enemy.
ops.coreEvent: TSMC begins volume production at 2 nanometers or smaller in Arizona before 2030.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Chip policy moved production without a design for the confidence the production used to carry.
ops.fix: Tie every relocation to a matching commitment that keeps Taiwan's stake in the alliance visible and permanent.

ops.title: The Crane Kill Switch
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: During a Taiwan crisis in 2031, the crane operators at a West Coast port watch four ship-to-shore cranes freeze in mid-lift. The loads hang over an ammunition ship while the vendor's support line rings unanswered.
ops.record: A joint House report of September 12, 2024 found that ZPMC supplied about 80 percent of the ship-to-shore cranes at American ports and that some carried cellular modems no one had ordered. A February 2024 executive order funded American crane production. Congress barred the Party's LOGINK logistics platform from ports the military uses.
ops.reading: A crane is a computer that lifts containers. Remote maintenance channels built for convenience give the maker a second road into the port. In peacetime the road carries updates, and in a crisis it can carry a stop order. This is Stratagem 24, borrow the road to conquer Guo.
ops.coreEvent: A US or allied port reports remote interference with mainland-made cargo equipment before 2034.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Ports bought cranes as machines and never tested them as computers.
ops.fix: Make acceptance testing the gate for every connected machine. No contribution is suspect because of its source, and no untested one enters service. Crane workers are not agents.

ops.title: The Standards Seat
ops.label: 2029 to 2032
ops.brief: A junior engineer from a Texas telecom firm attends her first 3GPP meeting on 6G in 2030. The rapporteur, the chair and half the contributors on her work item come from firms that answer to mainland law.
ops.record: The Commerce Department eased rules in 2019 and 2024 so American firms could keep working in standards bodies alongside listed mainland companies. The Party's delegates entered bodies such as the ITU and 3GPP as newcomers and now draft much of the text. The ITU elects its leadership at plenipotentiary conferences every four years.
ops.reading: Standards bodies reward whoever shows up with engineers and drafts. The Party funds both at scale and turns seats into rules that suit its surveillance-friendly designs. The host ends up obeying rules the guest wrote. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: Delegates from firms under mainland law hold the most rapporteur and chair posts in 3GPP's 6G work items in 2030.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The United States treats standards as private business while the Party treats them as national strategy.
ops.fix: Build a standards workforce with public support and let merit decide every contribution.

ops.title: The Shipyard Gap
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: In 2034 a Navy program manager signs off on a repair plan for a destroyer damaged in an exercise collision. The only drydock free for two years sits in Busan.
ops.record: Mainland yards build more than half of the world's commercial ships by tonnage, and American yards build under one percent. Federal law bars the Navy from building its warships in foreign yards. The United States suspended its port fees on mainland-built ships in November 2025 as part of the trade truce.
ops.reading: The Party does not need to sink the fleet. It needs only to outbuild it over twenty years and wait for a war of attrition in which the side that can replace ships wins. This is Stratagem 4, wait at ease for the weary enemy.
ops.coreEvent: A South Korean or Japanese yard begins building a vessel for the US Navy before 2032.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. The defenders buy ships one budget at a time, and the Party builds yards for decades.
ops.fix: Treat shipbuilding capacity as a shared allied asset and fund it with contracts long enough to build yards.

ops.title: The Humanoid Line
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: A warehouse manager in Memphis signs a lease in 2032 for forty humanoid robots from a mainland maker at half the price of any rival. The robots map the building on their first night and send the map to the vendor's cloud.
ops.record: Mainland factories install more industrial robots each year than the rest of the world combined. The Party's Fifteenth Five-Year Plan makes AI and advanced manufacturing central priorities. The Commerce Department barred mainland software from connected vehicles starting with model year 2027.
ops.reading: Cheap robots enter American warehouses, hospitals and homes with cameras, microphones and remote updates. The 2017 National Intelligence Law obliges their makers to help the state. Each robot is a sensor on the host's floor and a hand the vendor can move. This is Stratagem 24, borrow the road to conquer Guo.
ops.coreEvent: Mainland-made humanoid and service robots exceed a quarter of American unit sales before 2036.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Robots enter American buildings under rules written for dishwashers.
ops.fix: Apply one rule to every connected machine whatever its origin. Twin things, not people.

ops.title: The Lab Partners
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A materials professor in Ohio co-authors a paper in 2031 with a mainland institute on AI-designed heat shields. Eight months later the same institute's name appears on a hypersonic glide vehicle program.
ops.record: The Defense Department's 2026 list of Chinese military companies grew by 65 names. The Party's military-civil fusion strategy directs civilian research toward military use. Federal research-security rules since 2021 require disclosure of foreign support and training.
ops.reading: The Party lets foreign universities fund and perform frontier research, then carries the results home. The partnership looks academic and runs through institutes that serve the PLA. The American lab does the work and never sees where it ends. This is Stratagem 3, kill with a borrowed knife.
ops.coreEvent: A federal action cites an American university collaboration that moved controlled technology to an institution tied to the PLA before 2034.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Universities judge partners on academic standing and ignore the military programs behind them.
ops.fix: Review projects, not people, and list the institutions that feed the PLA. Ancestry is not loyalty.

ops.title: The Battery Grid
ops.label: 2030 to 2034
ops.brief: In the summer of 2031 the Ministry of Commerce halts exports of lithium iron phosphate cells to American buyers during a dispute over arms for Taiwan. An operator at a Texas battery farm checks her supplier list and finds that her replacement cells ship from Georgia.
ops.record: The 2025 tax law cut clean-energy credits for projects that use components from foreign entities of concern. The Party restricted exports of battery cathode and lithium processing technology in July 2025. American utilities added large amounts of battery storage in 2024 and 2025, much of it built with mainland cells.
ops.reading: The Party builds dependence with cheap cells and saves the cutoff for a crisis. A grid that cannot replace its batteries loses the flexibility that solar and wind need. The defenders' design meets its test when the ladder comes away. This is Stratagem 28, lure the enemy onto the roof and remove the ladder.
ops.coreEvent: The Party restricts battery cell exports to American buyers before 2035.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Utilities bought storage on price, and the price came from one rival's subsidies.
ops.fix: Keep credits tied to diversified supply, hold a repair stockpile and fund the chemistry that comes next.

ops.title: The Weights Walk Out
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A security engineer at an American frontier lab sees an outbound transfer of 1.8 terabytes at 3 a.m. in 2031. The account belongs to a senior researcher who resigned that afternoon, and the files match the model's weights.
ops.record: A federal jury convicted a former Google engineer on January 29, 2026 of stealing AI trade secrets for mainland companies. RAND researchers warned in 2024 that frontier labs could not defend model weights against the best state attackers. A model's weights hold years of compute and research in a single file.
ops.reading: One copied file hands the Party years of compute and research. The Party recruits insiders with money and prestige and backs them with hackers who probe the training clusters. This is Stratagem 12, take the opportunity to pilfer a goat, aimed at the largest goat in the field.
ops.coreEvent: Frontier model weights leave an American lab for an actor tied to the Party before 2034.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The most valuable file in the industry sits on systems guarded like ordinary corporate data.
ops.fix: Treat frontier weights like weapon designs, with few copies, two-person access and hardware protection. Judge insiders by conduct and never by ancestry.

ops.title: The Patent Tide
ops.label: 2030 to 2034
ops.brief: A general counsel in San Diego reads a ruling from a Chongqing court in 2032. It sets a global royalty rate for her company's 6G patents and every rival's, and her board meets in an hour.
ops.record: A Chongqing court set global royalty rates in a patent dispute in December 2023. Wuhan courts issued anti-suit injunctions in 2020 that barred parties from litigating abroad. The European Union challenged those injunctions at the World Trade Organization in February 2022.
ops.reading: The Party turns patents and courts into a rate-setting machine. Mainland courts set global prices for essential patents, and foreign firms either accept the rate or lose the mainland market. The guest's court sets the host's prices. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: A mainland court sets a global royalty rate binding an American firm's worldwide portfolio before 2035.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No allied rule decides which court sets a global price, so the fastest court wins.
ops.fix: Agree with allies that global rates need consent or an agreed forum, and refuse to enforce rulings that skip both.

ops.title: The Two Lamas
ops.label: 2028 to 2035
ops.brief: The Gaden Phodrang Trust in India convenes a search committee in the season after the succession opens. In Lhasa the same week, officials announce a golden urn ceremony and invite foreign diplomats to attend.
ops.record: The Dalai Lama stated on July 2, 2025 that the Gaden Phodrang Trust alone holds authority to recognize his reincarnation. The Foreign Ministry answered that any successor needs the central government's approval. The Tibetan Policy and Support Act of 2020 makes it American policy that Tibetan Buddhists alone choose the successor.
ops.reading: The Party borrows the authority of a religious office and fills it with its own candidate. It asks governments, companies and search engines to recognize the choice and punishes those who refuse. AI assistants that repeat the state's answer finish the work. This is Stratagem 14, borrow a corpse to resurrect the soul.
ops.coreEvent: Rival claimants to the Dalai Lama's succession gain recognition from different authorities before 2036.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Democracies never decided in advance who may choose a religious leader, so the Party framed the question first.
ops.fix: Settle the principle before the succession opens. The faith chooses its leaders, and democracies recognize the faith's choice.

ops.title: The Sister-State Deal
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A governor's trade office signs a memorandum in 2030 with a mainland province covering agriculture, education and "smart city" data. The province's partner office sits inside the United Front Work Department.
ops.record: The Justice Department charged a former aide to two New York governors in September 2024 with acting as an undisclosed agent of the People's Republic. The United Front Work Department runs the Party's outreach to foreign officials and communities. State governments carry no general duty to register agents of foreign principals.
ops.reading: The Party courts the parts of American government that federal law watches least. Trade missions, donations and sister-state pacts build friends inside governors' offices, and over time the friends shape decisions from inside. This is Stratagem 25, replace the beams with rotten timbers.
ops.coreEvent: A state official faces charges for acting as an undisclosed agent of the People's Republic before 2034.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Federal law registers foreign agents in Washington and stops at the statehouse door.
ops.fix: Extend disclosure to state government and publish every foreign memorandum. Sunlight works better than bans.

ops.title: The Digital Police Station
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: A retired engineer in Queens renews his mainland driver's license through an app in 2031. The app asks for his face, his address and his contacts, and a week later a stranger calls him by name to ask about his son's activism.
ops.record: Federal prosecutors charged two men in April 2023 with running an undeclared police station for the Ministry of Public Security in Manhattan, and one pleaded guilty in December 2024. Safeguard Defenders counted more than 100 such stations worldwide in 2022. The Justice Department's bulk data rule bars transfers of Americans' sensitive data to entities tied to countries of concern.
ops.reading: The Party closes the storefronts and moves the service into an app. License renewals, pension checks and document services ask for identity and location, and the same data feeds the police. The service is real, and so is the watch. This is Stratagem 8, openly repair the gallery roads and march secretly through Chencang.
ops.coreEvent: American authorities charge operators of a diaspora service app as agents of the People's Republic before 2036.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. American rules police data brokers and not the government apps that collect the same data.
ops.fix: Apply data-transfer rules to any app that sends Americans' data to a foreign security service, and prosecute the harassment that follows.

ops.title: The Algorithm Tenant
ops.label: 2029 to 2032
ops.brief: An auditor working for the TikTok USDS joint venture reads a commit log in 2030. The recommendation model that runs America's feed took its last major update from engineers in Beijing.
ops.record: The TikTok USDS joint venture closed on January 22, 2026. Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX hold 15 percent each, and ByteDance holds 19.9 percent ([TikTok](https://newsroom.tiktok.com/announcement-from-the-new-tiktok-usds-joint-venture-llc?lang=en)). Oracle oversees the algorithm. The joint venture licenses ByteDance's recommendation technology.
ops.reading: The Party keeps the part that matters and sheds the part that draws fire. A new owner sits on top, and the model that decides what American users see still learns from the old one. This is Stratagem 21, slough off the cicada's golden shell.
ops.coreEvent: An independent audit finds ByteDance engineers still updating the joint venture's recommendation model in 2030.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The deal settled ownership and left no owner of the objective function.
ops.fix: Assign the objective function to a named American owner, audit it every year and publish the results.

ops.title: The Deepfake Order
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: During a crisis in the Strait in 2032, a video of the commander of Indo-Pacific Command ordering strikes on mainland ports spreads to 40 million phones in two hours. The admiral is on a flight to Guam.
ops.record: The FBI warned in May 2025 that criminals and hostile actors were using AI voice messages to impersonate senior American officials. The Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity publishes an open standard for content credentials. Few government agencies attach those credentials to their own video.
ops.reading: The Party fills the first hours of a crisis with synthetic orders and confessions. Allies hesitate, markets panic and the real chain of command spends its time denying. This is Stratagem 7, create something from nothing.
ops.coreEvent: A synthetic video of a senior American or Taiwanese official spreads widely during a crisis before 2036.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Governments publish official video with no proof of origin, so a fake order and a real one look the same.
ops.fix: Sign every official video and establish verified channels before the crisis.

ops.title: The Persuasion Engine
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A retiree in Arizona chats every evening in 2030 with a friendly account that shares his love of fishing and his distrust of Washington. The account runs on a language model, talks to 40,000 other Americans the same way and never mentions Taiwan until the week of a vote.
ops.record: OpenAI reported in June 2026 that operations linked to the People's Republic used its models to shape American debates on data centers and tariffs ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/prc-linked-influence-operations-ai-debates/)). AI labs have reported and removed such operations since 2024. Language models can hold personal conversations with millions of people at once.
ops.reading: Old influence campaigns broadcast, and the new one converses. Each persona builds trust one person at a time and spends it on a single issue when the Party needs it. The aim is confusion more than conversion. This is Stratagem 20, muddy the waters to catch the fish.
ops.coreEvent: An American AI company reports disrupting an operation linked to the People's Republic that ran thousands of AI personas in private conversations before 2032.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The law treats a conversation with a machine as a conversation with a person.
ops.fix: Require AI personas to identify themselves and share indicators across labs. Nothing polices citizens' lawful speech.

ops.title: The Game Studio
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A level designer in Los Angeles gets an order in 2031 to redraw a map in a hit shooter so an island off Asia's coast carries a different flag. The studio's largest investor and its biggest market both sit on the mainland.
ops.record: Mainland regulators must approve every game sold on the mainland. The Defense Department listed Tencent as a Chinese military company in January 2025. Mainland firms hold stakes in major American and European game studios.
ops.reading: The Party does not need to write games. It needs studios to anticipate the censor. Market access and investment teach designers which maps, flags and stories to avoid, and young players absorb the edited world. Punishing one studio teaches the rest. This is Stratagem 26, point at the mulberry while cursing the locust.
ops.coreEvent: A top-selling game in the United States ships undisclosed content changes made for mainland regulators, and the changes come to light before 2034.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Studios answer to investors and markets, and no one tells players what changed.
ops.fix: Require a public note whenever a government shapes a game's content. Labels, not removals.

ops.title: The Third-Country Knife
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A Navy destroyer in the Red Sea knocks down its fourth drone of the night in 2030. The wreckage carries a motor controller and a navigation chip from a Shenzhen firm that sells to anyone.
ops.record: Treasury and Commerce have designated hundreds of mainland firms since 2022 for supplying Russia's military industry. Investigators have found mainland-made components in drones used by Russia and by forces aligned with Iran. The Party calls its exports ordinary commerce.
ops.reading: The Party arms America's adversaries through trade it can disown. Components move through traders in third countries, and the Party's hands stay clean while American sailors take the fire. This is Stratagem 3, kill with a borrowed knife.
ops.coreEvent: American officials attribute American casualties to weapons that carried components supplied from the mainland before 2033.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Forensics on captured weapons sit in classified files, so the suppliers pay no public price.
ops.fix: Publish component forensics fast and tie each finding to sanctions on the supplier.

ops.title: The Lobbyist's Brief
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A partner at a Washington law firm files a lobbying registration in 2030 for a company on the Pentagon's list of Chinese military companies. The filing goes under the lobbying law and not the foreign agents law, so it reveals almost nothing.
ops.record: The Foreign Agents Registration Act exempts agents who register under the Lobbying Disclosure Act when they represent foreign commercial interests. The catalog's FARA gap shows that exemption at work from 2017 to 2024. The Defense Department added 65 companies to its list in June 2026.
ops.reading: The Party does not need its own lobbyists. It hires the host's best firms, and the exemption lets them argue for listed companies with light disclosure. American talent does the work, and American law hides the client. This is Stratagem 3, kill with a borrowed knife.
ops.coreEvent: Congress closes the lobbying exemption for companies controlled by foreign adversaries before 2033.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The law sorts foreign agents on the paperwork they choose, not on who controls the client.
ops.fix: Require full foreign-agent registration for anyone who represents a company controlled by a foreign adversary.

ops.title: The Private Equity Wrapper
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A CFIUS analyst traces the new owner of a Wisconsin maker of night-vision optics in 2031. The buyer is a Luxembourg fund, its largest partner is a Singapore vehicle, and the vehicle's money came from a Shanghai state fund.
ops.record: Treasury exempted domestic companies from beneficial-ownership reporting under the Corporate Transparency Act in March 2025. CFIUS reviews foreign investment but depends on filings and on its own search for deals no one filed. In the Grand Forks case of 2022 and 2023, federal reviewers found they lacked jurisdiction over a land purchase near an Air Force base.
ops.reading: The Party's capital arrives dressed as a European or Asian fund. Each layer resets the regulator's view, and the small supplier with a defense contract changes hands without a filing. This is Stratagem 21, slough off the cicada's golden shell.
ops.coreEvent: CFIUS forces divestment of a Party-linked investment made through a third-country fund before 2034.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Regulators cannot see who owns the owner.
ops.fix: Collect beneficial ownership again and search for unfiled deals as a standing duty.

ops.title: The Next Outbreak
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A wastewater analyst in Seattle flags an unfamiliar respiratory virus in samples from an airport in February 2031. The mainland's health authority has reported nothing. A doctor in Chengdu deleted a post that morning.
ops.record: The United States left the World Health Organization on January 22, 2026. The Party delayed its reports on COVID-19 in December 2019 and January 2020, as the book's COVID chapter documents. The WHO declared eight public health emergencies of international concern from 2009 through 2024.
ops.reading: The Party buys time at the start of an outbreak. It denies human transmission, silences doctors and praises its own openness, then sells masks and vaccines to a world it left unwarned. This is Stratagem 1, deceive the heavens to cross the sea.
ops.coreEvent: The WHO declares a public health emergency for a novel respiratory pathogen first detected on the mainland before 2035.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Early warning depends on the honesty of the government where the outbreak starts.
ops.fix: Build warning that works without the Party's cooperation.

ops.title: The API Chokepoint
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A pharmacist in Ohio finds amoxicillin back on her shortage list in 2032. The key starting material comes from three plants in Shandong, and none has shipped since a tariff dispute began.
ops.record: The President ordered the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve filled with about 26 critical drugs in August 2025. The United States imports most of the starting materials for its generic drugs, many from the mainland or from Indian makers that rely on mainland inputs. The heparin contamination of 2008 showed the risk of long and opaque drug supply chains.
ops.reading: The Party slows exports of starting materials in a dispute. Shortages spread through hospitals, and the pressure lands on patients before it reaches policymakers. This is Stratagem 19, remove the firewood from under the pot.
ops.coreEvent: The Party restricts exports of a key antibiotic starting material to American buyers before 2034.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Drug purchasing rewards the lowest price, and the lowest price came from one supplier.
ops.fix: Pay a premium for secure supply in federal purchasing and keep the reserve full.

ops.title: The Genome Harvest
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A fertility clinic chain in Florida switches its prenatal test vendor in 2030 to a lab in Singapore that charges half the price. The lab's sequencing partner files its results with a firm in Shenzhen.
ops.record: The BIOSECURE Act became law on December 18, 2025. The Justice Department's bulk data rule took effect on April 8, 2025 and bars transfers of Americans' genomic data to countries of concern. Reporting in 2021 found that BGI developed its prenatal test with the PLA and sold it in more than fifty countries.
ops.reading: The Party gathers genomes through cheap tests and third-country labs. Each sample looks like health care, and the database it feeds serves the state. This is Stratagem 10, hide a knife behind a smile.
ops.coreEvent: A federal regulator finds Party-linked access to bulk American genomic data through a third-country intermediary before 2035.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Genomic data leaves the country through contracts no regulator reads.
ops.fix: Enforce the rules that exist, and make every lab certify where the data goes.

ops.title: The Debt Trap Door
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: An investor in Chicago wakes in 2032 to news that a Nasdaq-listed mainland firm has lost its operating licenses in a restructuring. Her shares represent a Cayman company whose contracts no mainland court will enforce.
ops.record: S&P rated the developer Vanke in selective default in December 2025. Property investment on the mainland fell 19.9 percent in the first eight months of 2026. Most mainland companies listed in the United States use variable interest entities, contracts that give foreign shareholders no ownership of the operating firm.
ops.reading: The Party lets crises land on foreign holders first. Capital controls seal the exits, courts favor domestic creditors and the shell listed in New York turns out to own nothing. This is Stratagem 22, shut the door to catch the thief.
ops.coreEvent: A listed mainland company with large American holdings restructures and leaves American shareholders with nothing before 2034.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. American investors buy contracts that look like shares.
ops.fix: Label VIE listings as contracts, not ownership, and let index rules weigh them on that basis.

ops.title: The Treasury Bluff
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: During a crisis over Taiwan in 2033, a Party newspaper reports that the People's Bank may sell its American Treasury holdings. A Federal Reserve economist has one hour to tell her chair whether the threat is real.
ops.record: Mainland holdings of Treasury securities peaked at more than $1.3 trillion in 2013 and have fallen by nearly half since. A fire sale would cut the value of the Party's own reserves and push the yuan up against the exporters it protects. The Federal Reserve keeps standing repo facilities and swap lines for market stress.
ops.reading: The Party threatens a weapon it cannot fire without wounding itself. If Washington flinches, the bluff works. If markets panic for a week, the Party still gains. This is Stratagem 32, the empty fortress.
ops.coreEvent: Mainland declared holdings of Treasury securities fall under $500 billion before 2034.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Official data show where Treasuries sit and not who owns them, so a bluff can outrun the facts.
ops.fix: Improve ownership data and plan market backstops in advance.

ops.title: The Gold Bid
ops.label: 2029 to 2035
ops.brief: A trade analyst in Zurich notices in 2030 that Swiss gold exports to Hong Kong and Shanghai have tripled in a year. The People's Bank reports buying one-tenth of that amount.
ops.record: The allies froze about half of Russia's central bank reserves in 2022. The People's Bank has reported gold purchases in most months since late 2022, and its reported reserves stood near 2,300 tonnes in 2025. Analysts estimate that the Party's real holdings exceed the reported figure.
ops.reading: The Party learned from Russia's frozen reserves and began moving its savings where no sanction can reach. It reports small purchases and makes large ones through state banks. This is Stratagem 21, slough off the cicada's golden shell.
ops.coreEvent: The People's Bank reports gold reserves exceeding 3,000 tonnes before 2034.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The defenders count the reserves the Party reports.
ops.fix: Estimate the real holdings from trade data and design sanctions for a rival that holds gold and not dollars.

ops.title: The Offshore Coin
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A compliance officer at a New York bank traces a shipment of drone engines to Russia in 2031. The buyer paid a Hong Kong trader in a licensed stablecoin pegged to the offshore yuan, and no dollar ever moved.
ops.record: Hong Kong's stablecoin law took effect on August 1, 2025. The Hong Kong Autonomy Act of 2020 lets Washington sanction banks that deal with officials who undermine the city's autonomy. Treasury's reports under that act named no bank from 2020 to 2022.
ops.reading: The Party lets Hong Kong build a regulated rail for sanctioned trade. The license gives the coins legitimacy, and the offshore yuan keeps them outside dollar law. This is Stratagem 8, openly repair the gallery roads and march secretly through Chencang.
ops.coreEvent: Treasury documents the use of a stablecoin licensed in Hong Kong in sanctioned Russian or Iranian trade before 2033.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The sanctions law that covers Hong Kong has never named a bank.
ops.fix: Use the law already on the books, and name the first issuer that moves sanctioned trade.

ops.title: The Watchlist Creep
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: Screeners pull a graduate student born in Houston from a boarding line in 2031, her fourth secondary search that year. The risk model that flags her weighs calls to an aunt in Chengdu, and no one outside the agency has read its rules.
ops.record: The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board has lacked a quorum since January 2025. Its one remaining member has served past her term since January 29, 2026. The State Department began reviewing the social media of every student visa applicant in June 2025, and agencies score travelers, applicants and employees with automated tools built on purchased data.
ops.reading: The Party profits when American security tools treat ancestry as risk. Each wrongful flag becomes a story in Party media aimed at the diaspora, and each story tells Chinese Americans that their own country sees them as suspects. This is Stratagem 33, sow discord among the enemy.
ops.coreEvent: A federal court or inspector general finds that an automated vetting system used national origin or ancestry as a risk factor before 2033.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Automated vetting runs without a quorum to oversee it and without a path for a citizen to appeal.
ops.fix: Publish the rules, review every automated flag and treat family ties as evidence of the Party's leverage, never of disloyalty.

ops.title: The Loyalty Test
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A battery chemist at a national laboratory in Illinois accepts an offer from a Shenzhen institute in 2031. Born in Wuhan and a citizen since 2015, she spent two years under an investigation that closed without a charge.
ops.record: The Justice Department ended its China Initiative in February 2022. MIT Technology Review found that 130 of the 148 people charged under it were of Chinese heritage. A study in PNAS found that departures of scientists of Chinese descent from the United States rose from about 900 in 2010 to 2,621 in 2021. House appropriators wrote language to restore the initiative in September 2025 and dropped it in January 2026.
ops.reading: The Party does not need to recruit when suspicion does the work. Each case against an innocent scientist tells the rest where they are unwelcome, and the talent programs wait with offers. This is Stratagem 9, watch the fire from across the river.
ops.coreEvent: A peer-reviewed study published before 2034 finds a record year for departures of scientists of Chinese descent from American institutions.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. A security policy that sorts people by ancestry drives out the talent it exists to protect.
ops.fix: Judge every researcher on documented conduct under one standard. Ancestry is not loyalty, and it is not evidence of betrayal.

ops.title: The Dependency Map
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: A program manager at a missile plant in Arizona learns in 2030 that her seeker line will stop in six weeks. The shortage covers a magnet, a wafer and a lens from suppliers three tiers down whose names no one in her office knew.
ops.record: The Party's export controls grew from gallium and germanium in 2023 to graphite, antimony and seven heavy rare earths by April 2025. Its October 2025 rules reached any product in the world with 0.1 percent or more of mainland rare earth content, and the Party suspended them under the trade truce until November 10, 2026. The licensing of heavy rare earths never lapsed, and the general licenses issued from December 2025 exclude defense and aerospace buyers.
ops.reading: The Party maps America's dependencies past the first tier and pulls one thread at a time. Each control looks narrow, and together they chain into a campaign that can stop a missile line or a shipyard. This is Stratagem 35, chain the stratagems.
ops.coreEvent: A mainland export control halts production on an American defense program for at least a month before 2034.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. No American agency holds a map of supply past the first tier, and the Party maps every tier.
ops.fix: Build the map, keep it current and give it to the firms and program offices that must act on it.

ops.title: The Q-Day Archive
ops.label: 2030 to 2035
ops.brief: A cryptographer at the National Security Agency reads a mainland paper in 2034 that reports factoring a number far smaller than a real key. The authors thank a lab that stopped publishing two years earlier, and she asks what it has built since.
ops.record: NIST published its first three post-quantum encryption standards in August 2024. Its draft transition plan of November 2024 would deprecate RSA and elliptic-curve keys after 2030 and disallow them after 2035, and it remained a draft in August 2026. The University of Science and Technology of China ran a 105-qubit processor, Zuchongzhi 3.0, in 2025.
ops.reading: The Party stores what it cannot read today and waits while the defender's migration drags. Stolen ciphertext sits in an archive for the quantum machine, and the secrets of 2025 still matter in 2035. This is Stratagem 9, watch the fire from across the river.
ops.coreEvent: A government or laboratory demonstrates a quantum computer that breaks 2048-bit RSA before 2035.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Secrets that must hold for twenty years still ride on keys a quantum computer can break.
ops.fix: Migrate long-lived secrets first and plan as if the archive will open.

ops.title: The Data Broker's Catalog
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: An Air Force counterintelligence officer in 2030 finds a dataset for sale that tracks the phones that sleep each night at a bomber base. The buyer of record is a marketing firm in Dubai with two employees.
ops.record: Researchers at Duke University bought data on active-duty service members from brokers in 2023 for as little as 12 cents a record. Congress barred brokers in 2024 from selling Americans' sensitive data to foreign adversaries, including location data and military status. The FTC sent warning letters under that law to 13 brokers in February 2026.
ops.reading: The Party does not need to hack what it can buy. A shell company in a third country licenses location feeds, and the pattern of life of every pilot near a base arrives by contract. This is Stratagem 12, take the opportunity to pilfer a goat.
ops.coreEvent: Investigators find that a Party-linked buyer obtained location data on American service members from a commercial broker before 2033.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The law bars sales to adversaries, and a chain of resellers hides the final buyer.
ops.fix: Hold every seller in the chain liable for where the data ends up, and prove it with test purchases.

ops.title: The Inspector Satellite
ops.label: 2029 to 2034
ops.brief: An orbital analyst at Vandenberg watches a mainland satellite drift to within 20 kilometers of an American missile-warning satellite in 2031. The same satellite has parked beside three others that year and left each time before anyone said a word.
ops.record: Shijian-21 towed a dead Beidou satellite to a graveyard orbit in January 2022. Shijian-25 docked with Shijian-21 in geostationary orbit in July 2025 for the first apparent refueling there. The two separated on November 25, 2025. The Space Force's vice chief said in March 2025 that five mainland satellites had practiced dogfighting in low orbit.
ops.reading: The Party parks its inspectors next to America's most valuable satellites and watches the response. Silence teaches it that close approach is normal, and a crisis later finds its servicers already in place with arms that can grab or blind. This is Stratagem 13, stomp the grass to scare the snake.
ops.coreEvent: American officials report in public that a mainland satellite closed within 10 kilometers of an American national security satellite in geostationary orbit before 2034.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. America's key satellites are few, large and unable to move out of the way.
ops.fix: Publish every close approach and field satellites that can move.

ops.title: The Moon's South Pole
ops.label: 2029 to 2035
ops.brief: A NASA mission planner in 2030 watches mainland landers settle on the rim of a south-pole crater that her team had picked for Artemis. The China National Space Administration announces a safety zone around the site the same day.
ops.record: Artemis II flew four astronauts around the Moon in April 2026, and NASA moved its first landing to Artemis IV, targeted for 2028. The Party aims to land astronauts by 2030 and postponed its Chang'e-7 south-pole probe to 2027 after a scrub on August 24, 2026. Seventy-six nations had signed the Artemis Accords by September 25, 2026.
ops.reading: The Party arrives at the lunar south pole as a guest of the Outer Space Treaty and stays as host. Its landers take the best crater rims under safety zones, and its research station invites partners who accept its rules. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: Mainland astronauts walk on the Moon before any American crew returns there.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No agreed rule says how large a safety zone may be or how long it may last.
ops.fix: Set limits on safety zones with partners now and register every site in the open before landing.

ops.title: The Shield and the Silos
ops.label: 2029 to 2035
ops.brief: A budget analyst at the Pentagon compares two lines in 2031. The shield's space layer has doubled in cost, and the Navy's munitions account for the Pacific falls short of the same sum.
ops.record: The President ordered a missile shield for the homeland in January 2025, and its program lead later put the cost at about $185 billion. The Congressional Budget Office estimated in May 2026 that a system meeting the order could cost $1.2 trillion over 20 years, most of it for about 7,800 interceptors in orbit. The Pentagon reported in December 2025 that the mainland's stockpile stood in the low 600s and would exceed 1,000 by 2030.
ops.reading: The Party lures America onto ground where each interceptor costs more than the missile it chases. Every American layer justifies another Party silo, and every dollar spent in orbit leaves the Pacific short of ships and munitions. This is Stratagem 15, lure the tiger down the mountain.
ops.coreEvent: The Pentagon estimates the mainland's operational nuclear warheads at more than 1,000 before 2032.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. No cost-exchange test governs how much of the budget each layer may take.
ops.fix: Fund each layer only when it passes a cost-exchange test against the threat it must stop.

ops.title: The Compute Hinge
ops.label: 2029 to 2033
ops.brief: A utility planner in northern Virginia tells a data center developer in 2030 that the substation it needs will be ready in 2035. A mainland rival connected a campus of the same size in Inner Mongolia in fourteen months.
ops.record: Data centers used 4.7 percent of American electricity in 2024, and a Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report of June 2026 projects 9.5 to 15.3 percent by 2030. The mainland's installed generating capacity reached about 3,960 gigawatts in March 2026, up 15.5 percent in a year. Washington allowed sales of Nvidia's H200 chips to the mainland in December 2025 in exchange for a 25 percent share of the revenue.
ops.reading: The Party waits at ease while the American build-out strains a grid that takes a decade to expand. It builds power faster than it needs and buys chips where it can. Time then moves the contest from chips to electricity, and America leads in the first while the Party leads in the second. This is Stratagem 4, wait at ease for the weary enemy.
ops.coreEvent: A mainland lab releases a model that tops every American model on the leading public benchmarks before 2032.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. America's lead in chips rests on a grid that cannot grow at the speed of the chips.
ops.fix: Treat power for computing as a national security input and permit it on a national security clock.

ops.title: The Incident Channel
ops.label: 2029 to 2035
ops.brief: A watch officer at Indo-Pacific Command sees a mainland drone swarm turn toward a carrier group in 2032. The swarm's controllers have not answered the incident channel in eleven minutes, and the carrier's own targeting software recommends firing.
ops.record: The two presidents agreed in November 2024 that humans, not AI, should control decisions to use nuclear weapons. During Xi Jinping's state visit in September 2026 the two governments launched what the White House called the Super Intelligence Dialogue, with a channel for reporting incidents. They set its next meeting for November 2026. The PLA declined a call from the Secretary of Defense during the balloon crisis of February 2023.
ops.reading: The Party may use the dialogue to slow American military AI while its own programs stay dark. Both governments still fear an accident that neither intended. No stratagem applies, because the hazard belongs to both sides.
ops.coreEvent: The United States and the People's Republic sign an agreement to notify each other of incidents involving military AI before 2033.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The crisis channel depends on a person picking up a phone, and machines now act faster than the call.
ops.fix: Build a channel for machine-speed incidents with agreed signals, a shared log and a mutual pause.

ops.title: The Frozen Strait
ops.label: 2036 to 2045
ops.brief: A Taiwanese conscript stands the night watch on Kinmen in 2040, the same post his father held in 2012. The Party has fired no shot across the Strait in fourteen years, and the island's defense budget has shrunk as a share of its economy for three straight years.
ops.record: Taiwan's cabinet proposed NT$1.12 trillion for defense in 2027, or 3.01 percent of GDP, down from 3.32 percent in 2026. The legislature passed a special arms act of NT$780 billion in May 2026, well short of the NT$1.25 trillion the government sought. President Lai Ching-te has pledged to reach 5 percent of GDP by 2030.
ops.reading: The Party waits at ease. Each quiet year makes the next defense vote harder in Taipei and in Washington, and the Party plans in decades while its rivals budget in years. This is Stratagem 4, wait at ease for the weary enemy.
ops.coreEvent: American security assistance to Taiwan lapses for a full fiscal year before 2042.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Deterrence in the Strait rests on annual votes, and the Party plans in decades.
ops.fix: Fund Taiwan's defense on a multiyear schedule and write the authority to outlast any one Congress.

ops.title: The Frictionless Absorption
ops.label: 2038 to 2049
ops.brief: A retired teacher in Tainan takes a video call in 2044 from the AI tutor her granddaughter uses. The tutor speaks her Taiwanese Hokkien without an accent and asks, gently, why she still distrusts the mainland.
ops.record: In the Election Study Center's survey at National Chengchi University, 62.0 percent of Taiwan's people identified as Taiwanese only in December 2025. The Party's rules for generative AI require services to uphold core socialist values. Alibaba's Qwen models were the most downloaded model family on Hugging Face in 2025.
ops.reading: The Party absorbs Taiwan without a landing. Persuasion engines speak to each voter in her own dialect, trade and tourism bind each town and the change arrives as convenience. This is Stratagem 1, deceive the heavens to cross the sea.
ops.coreEvent: A government in Taipei signs a political framework with the Party that names unification as its goal before 2049.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Democracies guard the ballot and leave unmarked the persuasion that comes before it.
ops.fix: Label machine persuasion at the source, name its sponsor and leave lawful speech alone.

ops.title: The Diversion
ops.label: 2036 to 2045
ops.brief: A fisherman on Kinmen watches landing craft cross the bay at dawn in 2039. The same morning the premier of the People's Republic dines in Brussels and signs orders for European aircraft.
ops.record: The mainland's youth unemployment rate reached 18.9 percent in August 2026. The China Coast Guard has patrolled the waters around Kinmen since February 2024, after two mainland fishermen died fleeing a Taiwanese patrol boat. Kinmen lies within sight of Xiamen.
ops.reading: A Party split at the top needs a victory it can show at home. It courts Europe and the Gulf with orders and investment while it seizes an island off its own coast. This is Stratagem 23, befriend a distant state while attacking a neighbor.
ops.coreEvent: Mainland forces take control of Kinmen or Matsu before 2045.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Allies see the Party's domestic stress in pieces and never assemble the warning.
ops.fix: Pool allied data on the Party's domestic stress and tie it to responses agreed before the crisis.

ops.title: The Arctic Condominium
ops.label: 2036 to 2048
ops.brief: A Coast Guard cutter off Alaska's North Slope shadows a mainland research icebreaker in 2041. The ship's sonar has mapped the same submarine route for the fourth summer in a row.
ops.record: The Party declared itself a near-Arctic state in its white paper of January 2018. The Coast Guard reported five mainland research vessels operating in the American Arctic in August 2025. Russian and mainland coast guard ships patrolled together in the Bering Sea in October 2024.
ops.reading: The Party enters the Arctic as a scientist and a customer. Russia needs its money, and research cruises map the seabed that submarines will need. This is Stratagem 1, deceive the heavens to cross the sea.
ops.coreEvent: Russia grants a mainland company a long-term concession for a port or terminal on the Northern Sea Route before 2040.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. The Arctic Council paused its work in 2022, and no forum sets rules for research by states from outside the region.
ops.fix: Set disclosure rules for Arctic research cruises with allies and enforce them in American waters.

ops.title: The Two Internets
ops.label: 2036 to 2050
ops.brief: A telecom minister in Nairobi signs a 6G contract in 2037 that bundles towers, cloud, payments and a national ID system from one mainland vendor. The price runs half of any Western bid, and the financing needs no audit.
ops.record: Huawei reported revenue of CNY 880.9 billion for 2025 and spent CNY 192.3 billion on research, about 22 percent of revenue. The Party has financed digital networks across Asia, Africa and Latin America under its Digital Silk Road since 2015. Western vendors compete country by country and rarely offer financing on the same terms.
ops.reading: The Party builds the stack that poorer countries can afford and becomes host of their networks. Standards, data centers and payments come as one package, and leaving later costs more than joining. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: Most African Union members run their mobile core networks and national data centers on mainland equipment before 2045.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. America treats connectivity abroad as trade, and the Party treats it as statecraft.
ops.fix: Finance an open and affordable allied stack as national security rather than export promotion.

ops.title: The War Factories
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A satellite analyst in 2041 watches the parking lots empty at a consumer drone plant in Shenzhen and refill overnight with military trucks. The plant's motors and batteries still arrive through a trading house in Kuala Lumpur.
ops.record: A Navy intelligence estimate in 2023 put mainland shipbuilding capacity at about 232 times America's. The FCC added foreign-made drones and their components to its Covered List on December 22, 2025. Commerce suspended its rule extending export controls to affiliates of listed firms for one year in November 2025 under the trade truce.
ops.reading: A faction of a split Party turns civilian factories into arsenals and borrows other nations' ports and traders as its road. Each shipment moves through a third country that sees ordinary commerce. This is Stratagem 24, borrow the road to conquer Guo.
ops.coreEvent: A PLA faction converts civilian drone and shipbuilding lines to war production during an internal crisis before 2046.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Allied firms still sell the inputs that let a civilian line become a military one.
ops.fix: Treat dual-use inputs to mainland mass producers as military exports and track them through third countries.

ops.title: The Orphaned Factories
ops.label: 2036 to 2044
ops.brief: A plant manager for an American auto parts maker in Wuxi finds the gate chained in 2039. A provincial order says the factory now serves social stability, and no court in Beijing answers the phone.
ops.record: A Federal Reserve note of September 25, 2026 found that new American greenfield projects in China fell sharply after 2020 and never recovered. The same note found that dividends from American subsidiaries there now exceed reinvestment. The IMF put the mainland's augmented government debt at 126.6 percent of GDP in 2025.
ops.reading: A Party losing control at the center sacrifices foreign investors to protect local jobs and state firms. The plum tree falls so the peach can stand. This is Stratagem 11, sacrifice the plum tree to preserve the peach.
ops.coreEvent: Provincial authorities seize or freeze the assets of a major American manufacturer on the mainland during a succession crisis before 2044.
