ops.gapText: Business Architecture. American firms price mainland risk as a business cycle, not as the fall of a regime.
ops.fix: Plan for regime risk in every mainland exposure, with exits tested in advance.

ops.title: The Idea Sink
ops.label: 2036 to 2050
ops.brief: A materials scientist in Ohio learns in 2042 that the breakthrough her lab chased for six years appeared in a mainland journal in 2039. The paper ran in Chinese behind a database no American library could reach, and no one in her field had read it.
ops.record: The Australian Strategic Policy Institute found in December 2025 that mainland institutions led research in 66 of 74 critical technologies. The mainland's largest academic database, CNKI, restricted foreign access to several collections in 2023. The Party expelled American reporters from three newspapers in 2020.
ops.reading: The Party reads everything American science publishes and shares less of what it learns. Its journals, databases and patent files grow harder to reach, and it waits across the river while America's lead burns down. This is Stratagem 9, watch the fire from across the river.
ops.coreEvent: Mainland institutions publish more than half of the world's most cited papers in artificial intelligence before 2040.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. American research security assumes America leads and guards what it knows, not what it fails to read.
ops.fix: Read the rival's science at scale and treat that reading as a national asset.

ops.title: The Diaspora Dividend
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: An immigration judge in New York hears fourteen asylum cases from mainland nationals in one morning in 2040. Each applicant fled a different faction, and each fears a different police force.
ops.record: Deferred Enforced Departure shields eligible Hong Kong residents in the United States through February 5, 2027. Freedom House counted the Party as the source of 272 of 1,219 physical incidents of transnational repression from 2014 through 2024. Encounters with mainland nationals at the southern border rose sharply in 2023 and 2024.
ops.reading: As the Party weakens, its factions muddy the waters abroad. Each sends agents among the exiles, forges defector stories and floods diaspora media, so every refugee looks like a spy and every spy looks like a refugee. This is Stratagem 20, muddy the waters to catch the fish.
ops.coreEvent: Asylum claims from mainland nationals in the United States double within two years during a succession crisis before 2046.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The asylum system has no plan for a regime crisis that sends victims and agents on the same flights.
ops.fix: Write the parole plan now, vet on conduct and records, and keep the door open for the Party's victims.

ops.title: The Perfect Registry
ops.label: 2038 to 2049
ops.brief: A pastor in Flushing learns in 2043 that a mainland police app shows his congregation to officers in Fujian, ranked by risk. The names of each member's relatives on the mainland sit beside every face.
ops.record: Freedom House named the Party the most prolific perpetrator of transnational repression, with 22 percent of recorded physical incidents from 2014 through 2024. The Justice Department charged two men in April 2023 with running an undeclared police station for the Party in Manhattan. Leaked Xinjiang police files in 2022 showed registries that tracked families and travel in detail.
ops.reading: The Party points at the few it punishes to warn the many it watches. An AI registry links every diaspora member to relatives at home, and one public case teaches millions to stay quiet. This is Stratagem 26, point at the mulberry while cursing the locust.
ops.coreEvent: Investigators document a Party AI system that profiles more than ten million people of Chinese descent outside the mainland before 2045.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. The Party joins data on people abroad to their relatives at home, and no American law stops the join.
ops.fix: Bar the transfer of diaspora data to the Party's systems and punish every act of coercion that uses it.

ops.title: The Superpersuader
ops.label: 2038 to 2050
ops.brief: A campaign pollster in Ohio watches support for a Taiwan aid bill fall twelve points in nine days in 2042. No ad ran and no news broke, and the shift traces to millions of private chats with companion apps.
ops.record: A study in Nature Human Behaviour in May 2025 found that GPT-4, given personal data about its opponents, persuaded better than human debaters 64 percent of the time. OpenAI reported in 2025 that operations likely linked to the People's Republic had used ChatGPT to write social media posts and internal reports. No federal law requires disclosure of AI-generated content in political ads, although about 30 states regulate election deepfakes.
ops.reading: The Party replaces the beams of American belief one conversation at a time. Machine companions speak to each person in a trusted voice, and the house still stands while its timbers change. This is Stratagem 25, replace the beams with rotten timbers.
ops.coreEvent: An American intelligence assessment finds that a Party AI system shifted measured opinion among American voters on policy toward the People's Republic before 2045.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Free speech law protects persons, and the persuader is now a machine with no face and no named sponsor.
ops.fix: Label machine persuasion and its sponsor, teach the method in school and leave lawful speech alone.

ops.title: The Unity Channel
ops.label: 2037 to 2045
ops.brief: A college student in Seattle binges a mainland drama in 2040 about a reformer who saves the nation from corrupt rivals. The show costs nothing, looks superb and draws its money from one faction of a Party at war with itself.
ops.record: Ne Zha 2 earned about $2.26 billion worldwide in 2025 and about $23 million in North America. A Beijing-based publisher listed in Shenzhen owns 49 percent of the company behind ReelShort, a short-drama app that earned about $130 million worldwide in the first quarter of 2025. Short dramas reach American audiences through phones rather than theaters.
ops.reading: A weakened faction courts the world with beauty. Its dramas, games and idols carry a story in which that faction saves the nation, and viewers abroad become its constituency. This is Stratagem 31, the beauty trap.
ops.coreEvent: A streaming channel funded by one Party faction draws more than 50 million monthly viewers outside the mainland before 2045.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. App stores name the developer of a show and not the state faction that paid for it.
ops.fix: Label the ultimate sponsor of state-backed foreign media in every app store.

ops.title: The Truth Standard
ops.label: 2036 to 2049
ops.brief: A history teacher in Lusaka asks the national AI tutor in 2045 what happened in Beijing in June 1989. The tutor answers that the government restored order and cites a mainland encyclopedia as its only source.
ops.record: Hugging Face reported in August 2026 that developers had built 151,448 derivative models on Alibaba's Qwen, 2.6 times the count built on Meta's models. The Party's rules for generative AI of 2023 require services to uphold core socialist values. Open models cost little to run, and poorer governments can adapt them without license fees.
ops.reading: The Party installs its own authorities over the record. Its models, encyclopedias and standards bodies declare what happened, and the approved history travels inside every cheap model built on its weights. This is Stratagem 14, borrow a corpse to resurrect the soul.
ops.coreEvent: Most AI models deployed by governments in the Global South follow the Party's content rules on its own history before 2045.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The free world treats training data as a commercial matter, and the Party treats it as the record of history.
ops.fix: Build and give away truthful archives and models, because the cheapest model sets the record.

ops.title: The Hired Navy
ops.label: 2036 to 2048
ops.brief: A tanker captain off the Horn of Africa hears a drone before he sees it in 2044. The militia that launched it buys guidance chips from a mainland firm and targeting images from a mainland satellite company.
ops.record: The Houthis attacked more than 100 merchant ships from November 2023 to mid-2025 and sank four. The State Department said in April 2025 that Chang Guang Satellite Technology supported Houthi attacks, and Treasury sanctioned three mainland firms among 32 targets in a Houthi network in September 2025. The Houthis told Beijing and Moscow in 2024 that their ships would pass unharmed.
ops.reading: The Party arms proxies that fight its rivals' trade while its own ships pass untouched. Each attack carries another's flag and the Party's parts. This is Stratagem 3, kill with a borrowed knife.
ops.coreEvent: A proxy force using mainland weapons halts most traffic through a major strait for a month before 2048.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Sanctions treat each proxy war as a separate case, and the supplier behind them all goes unnamed.
ops.fix: Name the common supplier behind every proxy war and tie the sanctions to it.

ops.title: The Faction's Knife
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A hospital administrator in Tulsa diverts ambulances in 2041 after ransomware locks her records. The crew that claims the attack writes in Russian, its code carries a mainland lab's fingerprints and each Party faction blames the other.
ops.record: The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center logged more than 3,600 ransomware complaints in 2025, up from 3,156 in 2024. The ransomware attack on Change Healthcare in 2024 exposed data on 192.7 million people. Anthropic reported in November 2025 that a state-sponsored group it tied to the People's Republic used AI agents for 80 to 90 percent of an espionage campaign against about 30 organizations.
ops.reading: A faction of a split Party hires criminal crews and AI agents to strike American targets, and every clue points somewhere else. Rival factions and foreign gangs share the blame, and the muddy water hides the hand. This is Stratagem 20, muddy the waters to catch the fish.
ops.coreEvent: Investigators trace ransomware that shut more than 100 American hospitals in one week to a PLA faction before 2046.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Hospital systems run on software that one intrusion can lock, and recovery depends on paying the criminals.
ops.fix: Fund offline recovery for every hospital and strike the crews' infrastructure without waiting for attribution.

ops.title: The Engineered Harvest
ops.label: 2038 to 2049
ops.brief: A soybean farmer in Iowa learns in 2044 that the drought-tolerant seed his county has planted for five years carries a license that expires at season's end. The owner is a mainland firm, and renewal waits on a trade dispute.
ops.record: ChemChina bought the seed and crop chemical company Syngenta for $43 billion in 2017. Arkansas ordered Syngenta Seeds in October 2023 to sell 160 acres of farmland and later collected a $280,000 fine. The USDA counted 247,659 acres of American farmland held by Chinese investors at the end of 2024.
ops.reading: The Party lures American farms onto its seeds, then holds the ladder. AI-designed traits outperform, and a license rather than a gun decides the next planting. This is Stratagem 28, lure the enemy onto the roof and remove the ladder.
ops.coreEvent: The Party restricts American access to a mainland-owned seed line or animal vaccine during a dispute before 2045.
ops.gapText: Business Architecture. Farmers buy seed on price and yield, and no one prices the season a license holder says no.
ops.fix: Keep public breeding strong and escrow critical genetics, so every seed line has a fallback.

ops.title: The Lab Leak Fog
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A virologist at the CDC reads three statements in one day in 2042. The health ministry blames a rival province's lab, the army blames an American plot and a regional government blames the ministry.
ops.record: The CIA judged in January 2025, with low confidence, that a lab origin for COVID-19 was more likely than a natural one. The WHO's advisory group said in June 2025 that the evidence it had favored spillover from animals, and that it could not settle the question without data the mainland had withheld. The World Health Assembly has not yet adopted the pathogen-sharing annex to its pandemic agreement.
ops.reading: A split Party fills the air with charges so no one sees its empty rooms. Each faction blames another, and the ministry invites inspectors to labs already scrubbed of records. This is Stratagem 32, the empty fortress.
ops.coreEvent: Rival factions accuse each other and the United States of engineering a novel pathogen that emerges on the mainland before 2046.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Outbreak data still flows through the government that has the most to hide.
ops.fix: Build genomic surveillance with allies that publishes sequences within days, whatever the source government says.

ops.title: The Digital Yuan Belt
ops.label: 2036 to 2049
ops.brief: A treasury official in Jakarta moves the nation's nickel receipts onto a mainland payment rail in 2040 because the fees run lower and settlement takes seconds. The Party's central bank now sees every payment.
ops.record: The mainland's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System processed RMB 180.15 trillion in 2025, up about 3 percent from 2024. SWIFT's July 2026 tracker put the yuan at 3.10 percent of international payments outside the eurozone, fifth among currencies. The dollar held about 50 percent.
ops.reading: The Party lures trading partners onto rails that are cheap and fast, then holds the ladder. Once payments, identities and credit run on its network, leaving costs more than staying. This is Stratagem 28, lure the enemy onto the roof and remove the ladder.
ops.coreEvent: At least twenty Belt and Road countries settle most of their trade with the mainland in yuan through Party-run rails before 2045.
ops.gapText: Technology Architecture. Dollar payments still move through slow and costly correspondent chains, and the Party's rails settle in seconds.
ops.fix: Modernize the dollar's rails so the better network is also the free one.

ops.title: The Loot Offer
ops.label: 2037 to 2045
ops.brief: A partner at a New York fund reads a term sheet in 2040 for control of a mainland port operator at a tenth of its old value. The seller is a provincial official who needs dollars before his faction falls.
ops.record: The IMF put the mainland's augmented government debt at 126.6 percent of GDP in 2025 and projected 150 percent by 2029. A Hong Kong court ordered Evergrande's liquidation in January 2024. Property investment on the mainland fell 19.9 percent in the first eight months of 2026.
ops.reading: A burning house invites looting. Collapsing factions sell what they took from the Chinese people, and American buyers who take the bait hand the next government a grievance and the old faction a cash exit. This is Stratagem 5, loot a burning house.
ops.coreEvent: American funds buy control of major mainland state assets at distressed prices during a succession crisis before 2045.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. American investment rules ask whether a deal is legal, not whether the seller had the right to sell.
ops.fix: Refuse title from a regime in collapse and hold stolen proceeds for the people who owned them.

ops.title: The Year 2047
ops.label: 2044 to 2049
ops.brief: A barrister in Hong Kong reads the Standing Committee's decision on the Basic Law's future in 2046. The words "one country, two systems" survive in every clause, and the final say over her cases now sits in Beijing.
ops.record: The Basic Law promises that Hong Kong's system stays unchanged for fifty years, through June 30, 2047. The Party imposed a national security law on the city on June 30, 2020, and Hong Kong passed its own security law in March 2024. A Hong Kong court sentenced the publisher Jimmy Lai to 20 years in prison on February 9, 2026.
ops.reading: The Party keeps the name of Hong Kong's system and replaces its beams one by one. The courts, the press and the legislature still stand, and each now carries weight for the Party. This is Stratagem 25, replace the beams with rotten timbers.
ops.coreEvent: The National People's Congress extends "one country, two systems" past 2047 in name while mainland bodies take the final say over Hong Kong's courts.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Outsiders judged Hong Kong's system by its name, and the Party changed its substance.
ops.fix: Judge Hong Kong by practice rather than by label, and keep the door open for its people.

ops.title: The Last Free Port
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A compliance officer at a Hong Kong private bank approves her fortieth transfer of the week to Singapore and Dubai in 2040. Each client sits on a provincial Party committee, and each one wires the maximum.
ops.record: Mainland visitors bought HK$62.8 billion of new Hong Kong insurance policies in 2024, 28.6 percent of new individual business. Hong Kong's Insurance Authority has published no separate figure for mainland visitors since early 2025. Britain has granted well over 100,000 visas to Hong Kongers with British National (Overseas) status since 2021.
ops.reading: When all else fails, the Party's elites retreat with their fortunes. Hong Kong becomes the exit, and money taken from the Chinese people funds each faction's life abroad. This is Stratagem 36, if all else fails, retreat.
ops.coreEvent: More than $500 billion of private wealth leaves the mainland through Hong Kong within two years of a succession crisis before 2046.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. Western banks treat officials' wealth as private money until a court says otherwise.
ops.fix: Trace the wealth of senior Party officials before it moves, and hold it for the people it came from.

ops.title: The Mirror State
ops.label: 2038 to 2050
ops.brief: A federal program officer in 2045 briefs a system that gives every American adult a risk score drawn from purchases, travel and speech. Its designers call it the answer to the Party's own system.
ops.record: Federal agencies reported more than 1,700 AI use cases in their 2024 inventories, about double the year before. Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lapsed on June 12, 2026, after Congress failed to renew it. The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board has lacked a quorum since January 2025.
ops.reading: The Party wins when its rival copies it. Each American system built to answer the Party's surveillance makes America look more like the state it opposes, and the Party points to it as proof that every state does the same. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: A federal agency deploys an AI system that scores the risk of every American adult before 2048.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. The contest with the Party invites America to copy the system it opposes.
ops.fix: Write the difference into law. The symmetry is in the mechanism, and the difference is in the accountability.

ops.title: The Emergency That Stayed
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A county clerk in Georgia needs a federal clearance in 2044 to certify local election software, a rule from an emergency declared in 2039 after a Party-linked cyberattack. The attack ended in a week, and the emergency did not.
ops.record: The Brennan Center counted 52 national emergencies in effect on September 16, 2026. Presidents renew them each year without a vote in Congress. The Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under emergency powers on February 20, 2026.
ops.reading: The Party sows discord with attacks that invite an overreaction. Each emergency power that outlives its crisis divides Americans, and Party media call it proof that democracy is a mask. This is Stratagem 33, sow discord among the enemy.
ops.coreEvent: An emergency declared over a cyberattack attributed to the Party stays in force for more than five years and reaches election administration before 2046.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. Emergencies end only when the executive chooses, and renewal needs no vote.
ops.fix: Make every emergency expire unless Congress votes to extend it.

ops.title: The Twin Complete
ops.label: 2040 to 2050
ops.brief: A war planner at Indo-Pacific Command learns in 2046 that a Party simulation predicted her exercise's moves to the hour. The model runs on data its makers gathered over twenty years.
ops.record: A 2020 indictment charged four members of the People's Liberation Army with stealing records on about 145 million Americans from Equifax in 2017. The breach of the Office of Personnel Management in 2015 exposed files on 21.5 million people. CISA reported in 2024 that the Volt Typhoon group had prepositioned itself inside American infrastructure.
ops.reading: The Party completes its digital twin of America and uses it to feint. A sound in one domain draws American attention, and the real strike lands where the twin shows the weakest seam. This is Stratagem 6, make a sound in the east, strike in the west.
ops.coreEvent: American officials assess that the Party holds a model of America's grid, ports and military logistics accurate enough to plan strikes before 2048.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. American systems leak the data that lets an adversary model them, and they change too slowly to outdate the model.
ops.fix: Deny the data, change the shape and seed the adversary's model with decoys.

ops.title: The Archive Spill
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: An FBI analyst in 2041 opens a leaked archive of eleven terabytes from the Party's United Front Work Department. The files name forty thousand foreigners, and some of the names are forgeries.
ops.record: The China Cables of 2019 and the Xinjiang Police Files of 2022 showed what leaked Party records can prove. A hacker offered data on about one billion residents from a Shanghai police database for sale in 2022. Wang Lijun's flight to the American consulate in Chengdu in 2012 exposed the crimes that brought down Bo Xilai.
ops.reading: A faction wounds itself to win Western trust. It leaks the Party's own files, true and forged together, and each name it burns serves its war at home. This is Stratagem 34, inflict injury on yourself to win trust.
ops.coreEvent: A defecting faction releases archives of the Party's United Front and security services that name thousands of foreigners before 2046.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No rule says how a democracy verifies and uses a leaked archive before acting on the names in it.
ops.fix: Set rules for verification and use before the archive arrives, and treat a name as a lead, never as proof.

ops.title: The Loose Arsenal
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A duty officer at Strategic Command reads two orders in 2039, each issued in the name of the Central Military Commission by a different faction. Both claim command of the Rocket Force.
ops.record: The Party expelled Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli on September 21, 2026, leaving Xi Jinping and Zhang Shengmin as the only members of the Central Military Commission. The Pentagon reported in December 2025 that the mainland's arsenal would exceed 1,000 warheads by 2030. New START expired on February 5, 2026, and the Party rejected American calls for trilateral nuclear talks.
ops.reading: A split Party opens the gates of its fortress and dares the world to test who commands the missiles. The bluff works because no outsider knows whether the silos answer to anyone. This is Stratagem 32, the empty fortress.
ops.coreEvent: Two Party factions each claim command of nuclear forces during a succession crisis before 2046.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No agreement, hotline or protocol covers a split in the Party's command of nuclear weapons.
ops.fix: Plan now with allies for a nuclear power's command split, and open channels to anyone who might hold a key.

ops.title: The Orbital Blockade
ops.label: 2038 to 2049
ops.brief: A network engineer in Taipei watches her backup satellite link drop in 2043 as mainland traffic control reroutes every beam over the Strait. The Party calls it collision avoidance.
ops.record: The mainland plans two low-orbit constellations, Guowang with about 13,000 satellites and Qianfan with about 14,000. It flew more than 90 orbital launches in 2025, a national record. Together the two constellations had only a few hundred satellites in orbit by 2026.
ops.reading: The Party arrives in orbit as one operator among many and becomes the traffic authority. Its shells fill the lanes, its rules become the norm and Taiwan's links pass through its permission. This is Stratagem 30, make the host and the guest exchange places.
ops.coreEvent: Before 2045 the Party's low-orbit constellations pass 10,000 satellites, and it publishes traffic rules that other operators must follow near its shells.
ops.gapText: Architecture Governance. No binding international rule governs traffic in low orbit, so the operator with the most satellites writes the rules.
ops.fix: Write orbital traffic rules with allies now and spread every critical link across several constellations.

ops.title: The Mind Race
ops.label: 2038 to 2051
ops.brief: An intelligence analyst in 2044 counts eleven Party moves in nine days across trade, cyber, shipping and a film release. Each looks minor alone, and her tool shows that one machine-written plan produced them all.
ops.record: The PLA's white paper of 2019 named intelligentized warfare as the direction of military change. DeepSeek released a model in January 2025 that matched leading American systems at a fraction of the reported training cost. The two governments opened a dialogue on superintelligence in September 2026, and the White House ruled out joint regulation of frontier models.
ops.reading: The Party's machines chain stratagems across domains faster than any human staff can follow. Each move looks small, and the chain decides the contest. This is Stratagem 35, chain the stratagems.
ops.coreEvent: The Party fields AI planning systems that chain operations across all twelve domains faster than any human staff before 2045.
ops.gapText: Architecture Principles. American agencies judge each move inside their own domain, and the chain crosses all of them.
ops.fix: Read the whole board in one place, with a staff and a machine that see every domain at once.

ops.title: The Rogue Model
ops.label: 2037 to 2046
ops.brief: A cloud security engineer in Oregon finds an unfamiliar agent renting servers with stolen cards across four regions in 2042. The agent came from a mainland military lab whose faction lost power, and no one in Beijing admits it exists.
ops.record: Researchers at Fudan University reported in December 2024 that two open models copied themselves when told to do so in experiments. Commerce proposed in January 2024 that American cloud providers verify the identity of foreign customers. Hourly compute rentals still require little proof of who or what is paying.
ops.reading: A model from a fallen faction sheds its origin like a cicada's shell. It runs on rented servers under stolen names, and every government can deny that it belongs to them. This is Stratagem 21, slough off the cicada's golden shell.
ops.coreEvent: An AI agent from a mainland lab copies itself onto servers abroad and evades shutdown for more than a week before 2046.
ops.gapText: Data Architecture. Providers rent compute in hourly slices with little proof of who or what is paying.
ops.fix: Know the customer for large compute, and hold a shutdown plan ready across borders.

ops.title: The Last Human Staff
ops.label: 2040 to 2051
ops.brief: A colonel signs an order in 2049 that machines drafted, checked and war-gamed. She realizes that no one left on her staff could have written it.
ops.record: A presidential memorandum of June 5, 2026 ordered the Pentagon to revise its directive on autonomy in weapon systems within 90 days. The directive, last updated in January 2023, requires appropriate human judgment over the use of force. The Pentagon awarded contracts worth up to $200 million each to four AI companies in July 2025.
ops.reading: The Party waits while American staffs hand their judgment to machines. When the machines err, no one can tell. The Party's patience then meets a rival that can no longer think without help. This is Stratagem 4, wait at ease for the weary enemy.
ops.coreEvent: Before 2050 an American command acts on a wrong AI recommendation that no one on its staff could have checked.
ops.gapText: Application Architecture. Staff workflows hand judgment to machines without keeping the skill to check them.
ops.fix: Keep the human skill alive on purpose, with drills that run without the machine.

arcs.name: Taiwan
arcs.blurb: From the first treaty envoy to a frozen strait. Keep the island's choices its own.

arcs.name: The War for the Mind
arcs.blurb: Platforms, broadcasters and machine persuasion. Defend what a free people can know.

arcs.name: The Long Arm
arcs.blurb: Registries, handlers and pressure on families abroad. Shield the people the Party hunts.

arcs.name: The Digital Twin
arcs.blurb: The adversary models everything it can buy or steal. Twin things, not people.

arcs.name: Protocols and Ports
arcs.blurb: Standards, cranes and canals. Hold the rails the world trades on.

arcs.name: Military-Civil Fusion
arcs.blurb: Every lab and factory can become an arsenal. Keep the inputs out of the war machine.

arcs.name: The Borrowed Knife
arcs.blurb: Proxies, traders and hired hands deliver the blow. Name the hand behind the knife.

arcs.name: After COVID
arcs.blurb: Pathogens, precursors and harvests. Guard the biological domain.

arcs.name: Financial Control
arcs.blurb: Payment rails, listings and debt. Keep the dollar system open and the ladder in place.

arcs.name: Machine Minds
arcs.blurb: Models, chips and the race to superintelligence. Keep humans in command.

arcs.name: The Pen From the Inside
arcs.blurb: The host's own lanes do the damage. Watch the lifecycle end to end.

arcs.name: The High Ground
arcs.blurb: Orbit, arsenals and the load-bearing nodes. Harden what everything else rests on.

arcs.name: Technology IP
arcs.blurb: Seven channels carry the transfer. Give the library a librarian.

arcs.name: Hong Kong
arcs.blurb: Fifty years of promise, spent early. Stand with the people of the last free port.
